quotes.quote_text: Building Canada strong means investing in the industries that will strengthen our economy today and into the future. Quantum technology represents a tremendous opportunity to create good jobs, strengthen our economic sovereignty and grow world-leading industries here at home. By investing in advanced manufacturing and innovation in Canada, we are building a more resilient economy, developing Canadian talent and ensuring we remain competitive in a rapidly changing world.
quotes.speaker: Mélanie Joly
quotes.dept_en: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada invests in Xanadu to build up advanced quantum manufacturing in Canada

quotes.quote_text: Canada is home to some of the world’s leading quantum researchers, innovators and companies. Strategic investments like this one help transform Canadian breakthroughs into globally competitive businesses, strengthen our quantum ecosystem and create high-value jobs here at home. Quantum technologies will be one of the foundational technologies of the 21st century. By supporting advanced manufacturing and commercialization in Canada, we are helping ensure that Canada remains a global leader in quantum innovation and that more of the economic benefits of that leadership are created here at home.
quotes.speaker: Evan Solomon
quotes.dept_en: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada invests in Xanadu to build up advanced quantum manufacturing in Canada

quotes.quote_text: Etobicoke–Lakeshore has a long tradition of being a community where you can live and work. This announcement will preserve our local culture while bringing us into the modern age.
quotes.speaker: James Maloney
quotes.dept_en: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada invests in Xanadu to build up advanced quantum manufacturing in Canada

quotes.quote_text: This agreement is a major milestone for Xanadu and for Canada’s ambition to lead in quantum technology and advanced manufacturing. We believe building utility-scale quantum computers will require a new generation of highly specialized manufacturing capabilities. With the Government of Canada’s commitment through the Strategic Response Fund, we can move forward with establishing that infrastructure here at home, strengthening Canada’s quantum supply chain and creating a foundation for future quantum data centre deployment. We are grateful for the Government of Canada’s confidence in Xanadu, and we look forward to continuing our discussions with the Government of Ontario as we work to realize the full vision for Project OPTIMISM.
quotes.speaker: Dr. Christian Weedbrook
quotes.dept_en: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada invests in Xanadu to build up advanced quantum manufacturing in Canada

quotes.quote_text: When the United States asked too much and offered too little, we chose to stand up for Canadians. Our dollar-for-dollar, rate for rate counter-tariffs as well as a multi-billion dollar support package will protect workers, farmers, families, and businesses as we build a stronger, more resilient, and more diversified Canadian economy.
quotes.speaker: François-Philippe Champagne
quotes.article_title: Canada announces targeted countermeasures and substantive support for workers and businesses in response to U.S. tariffs

quotes.quote_text: In a more uncertain world, Canada will continue to invest in our greatest strengths: our workers, our businesses, and our capacity to compete. Today’s new measures will protect jobs, strengthen the industries that drive our economy, and secure the supply chains that underpin our prosperity. Canada will not simply respond to change, we will shape it, growing a stronger economy that delivers opportunity, security, and prosperity for Canadians.
quotes.speaker: Mélanie Joly
quotes.article_title: Canada announces targeted countermeasures and substantive support for workers and businesses in response to U.S. tariffs

quotes.quote_text: Canada has what the world wants, and we will not allow any nation to determine our future. We will always stand up for Canadian workers and businesses. We are strong because we take of each other and that is why we will always be masters of our own destiny.
quotes.speaker: Patty Hajdu
quotes.article_title: Canada announces targeted countermeasures and substantive support for workers and businesses in response to U.S. tariffs

quotes.quote_text: Canadians expect their government to stand up for them and their interests. As the United States impose unjustified tariffs, Canada’s government is focused on building our strength at home and protecting our economy. Today’s countermeasures will ensure workers, farmers, families, and businesses affected are supported throughout this period of uncertainty. Together, we will weather this storm—united and resilient.
quotes.speaker: Dominic LeBlanc
quotes.speaker_title: President, Internal Trade and One Canadian Economy
quotes.article_title: Canada announces targeted countermeasures and substantive support for workers and businesses in response to U.S. tariffs

quotes.quote_text: Our new government is focused on what we can control - building a stronger, more resilient economy here at home. That means investing in Canadian workers and businesses, strengthening our supply chains and expanding our trade relationships to create good jobs and long-term growth.
quotes.speaker: John Zerucelli
quotes.article_title: Canada announces targeted countermeasures and substantive support for workers and businesses in response to U.S. tariffs

quotes.quote_text: Southwestern Ontario is among the regions facing the greatest pressure from unjustified U.S. tariffs, and as the federal voice for this region, I am ensuring that reality is understood in Ottawa. Our government is taking action to protect jobs and keep businesses operating and growing across Southwestern Ontario. We are committed to ensuring workers and businesses in this region have the support they need to weather uncertainty and emerge stronger.
quotes.speaker: Arielle Kayabaga
quotes.article_title: Canada announces targeted countermeasures and substantive support for workers and businesses in response to U.S. tariffs

quotes.quote_text: Through dollar-for-dollar, rate-for-rate counter-tariffs and a multi-billion-dollar support package, our new government is prioritizing Canadian businesses and workers while reducing our reliance on a single trading partner. Together, we will overcome these challenges and build a stronger, more resilient economy.
quotes.speaker: Peter Fragiskatos
quotes.article_title: Canada announces targeted countermeasures and substantive support for workers and businesses in response to U.S. tariffs

quotes.quote_text: Government support during this period of trade uncertainty has made a tangible difference for Canadian manufacturers like Attica. These investments are about much more than new equipment—they are investments in our people, our technology, our productivity and our ability to compete on the world stage. We’re proud to manufacture in London, Ontario, and we’re committed to continuing to invest in our skilled workforce and the future of Canadian manufacturing.
quotes.speaker: Andy Mavrokefalos
quotes.article_title: Canada announces targeted countermeasures and substantive support for workers and businesses in response to U.S. tariffs

quotes.quote_text: To everyone in British Columbia facing the impacts of this summer’s devastating wildfires, know that Canadians stand with you. As families and communities continue the difficult work of recovery, the federal government is proud to match donations made to the Canadian Red Cross, doubling the impact of every contribution from across the country. This initiative will help ensure that those affected receive the support they need today, while helping communities rebuild and emerge stronger in the months ahead.
quotes.speaker: Eleanor Olszewski
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada to match donations to the Red Cross’ 2026 British Columbia Wildfires Appeal

quotes.quote_text: The wildfires in British Columbia this summer have destroyed homes and impacted livelihoods, affecting individuals and families in many communities. The Canadian Red Cross thanks everyone who has donated or will be donating to the 2026 British Columbia Wildfires Appeal for their support, as well as the Government of Canada for these matching funds.
quotes.speaker: Conrad Sauvé
quotes.speaker_title: President and CEO, Canadian Red Cross
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada to match donations to the Red Cross’ 2026 British Columbia Wildfires Appeal

quotes.quote_text: By matching donations to the Canadian Red Cross, the Government of Canada is providing additional support to communities affected by wildfires in British Columbia, including in the Okanagan. This initiative will help individuals and families impacted by fires to access the resources they need to recover. The Okanagan and communities across B.C. are stronger thanks to the hard work of firefighters, first responders and volunteers.
quotes.speaker: Stephen Fuhr
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada to match donations to the Red Cross’ 2026 British Columbia Wildfires Appeal

quotes.quote_text: The new Sectoral Workforce Innovation Fund builds on our commitment to supporting the workers, industries and major projects that will shape Canada’s future. As labour shortages continue to affect key sectors, this fund will help more Canadians access the skills and opportunities they need to succeed. A strong workforce is essential to keeping Canadian industries competitive in a changing global economy. By investing in people today, we are turning opportunity into growth, for workers, for industries, and for a Canada that is stronger and more self-reliant.
quotes.speaker: Patty Hajdu
quotes.article_title: The Government of Canada is launching a call for proposals under the Sectoral Workforce Innovation Fund to support workforce projects across key sectors

quotes.quote_text: Canada is focused on supporting Canadians and their families as this devastating situation unfolds. Our consular teams are working around the clock, both here in Canada and on the ground in the region, to reach Canadians and provide assistance. We are working closely with authorities in Nepal and China, as well as our partners and allies, and doing everything we can to help Canadians affected by this crisis. Our thoughts are with the people of Nepal and China, and with all those affected by this tragedy.
quotes.speaker: Anita Anand
quotes.article_title: Canada provides funding for humanitarian response to devastation caused by severe flash floods and landslides along Nepal-China border

quotes.quote_text: The devastation caused by these flash floods and landslides is heartbreaking, with lives lost, communities displaced and extensive damage caused to homes and infrastructure. My thoughts are with everyone affected, particularly those still waiting to hear about the safety and well-being of loved ones. Canada’s initial response is focused on helping meet the most urgent humanitarian needs, and we will continue to explore how we can provide support as the situation unfolds.
quotes.speaker: Randeep Sarai
quotes.article_title: Canada provides funding for humanitarian response to devastation caused by severe flash floods and landslides along Nepal-China border

quotes.quote_text: As the United States fundamentally transforms its commercial relationships and imposes new tariffs on Canadian goods, we are focusing on what we can control: diversifying our trading relationships and building strength at home. Major projects like the Mackenzie Valley Highway and Roberts Bank Termi nal 2 will help position Canada for lo ng-ter m success. The publication of these notices reflects our commitment to transparency and meaningful consultation as we advance nati on-bu ilding infrastructure projects that connect our businesses with global markets and make Canada more resilient and se lf-reliant.
quotes.speaker: Dominic LeBlanc
quotes.speaker_title: President, U.S., Trade, Internal Trade and One Canadian Economy
quotes.article_title: Canada takes next step in potential listing of Mackenzie Valley Highway and Roberts Bank Terminal 2 projects under Building Canada Act

quotes.quote_text: In a time of uncertainty and changing trade and economic relationships worldwide, Canada is expanding and strengthening our network around the world. These efforts ensure we have the minerals our economies need, diversify and secure our trade and create opportunities for Canadian workers and businesses. Canada and Chile share a strong and long-standing partnership built on investment, responsible resource development, innovation and shared economic interests. This trip reinforced for our Chilean partners that Canada is a partner of choice for investment, business and collaboration.
quotes.speaker: Claude Guay
quotes.article_title: Canada and Chile advance critical minerals partnership to diversify trade, grow our economy and create jobs

quotes.quote_text: Trade disruptions are threatening the industries that drive Canada's economy. That is why the Government of Canada is standing up for Canadian businesses and making investments that strengthen our supply chains, grow productivity, and open doors to new markets. By investing in B.C. businesses, we are protecting good jobs and strengthening Canada’s long-term economic resilience.
quotes.speaker: Gregor Robertson
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada invests over $10 million to help Lower Mainland businesses navigate trade disruptions and seize new opportunities

quotes.quote_text: Small businesses and workers drive British Columbia's economy and strengthen communities across our province. As businesses adjust to unjustified tariffs, our government is investing in their success, protecting jobs, and creating opportunities for long-term growth. We will always stand with Canadian businesses and Canadian workers.
quotes.speaker: Jill McKnight
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada invests over $10 million to help Lower Mainland businesses navigate trade disruptions and seize new opportunities

quotes.quote_text: Richmond’s businesses have consistently demonstrated resilience, ingenuity, and entrepreneurial spirit. With support from this PacifiCan investment, they will be better positioned to overcome the challenges posed by unfair and illegal tariffs, continue innovating, and compete with confidence on the world stage. I remain committed to helping more businesses diversify, grow, and thrive.
quotes.speaker: Parm Bains
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada invests over $10 million to help Lower Mainland businesses navigate trade disruptions and seize new opportunities

quotes.quote_text: With support from the Regional Tariff Response Initiative, Nickels will accelerate key equipment purchases and advance strategies to expand our Canadian customer base through our Heirloom division. Amid current market uncertainty, these efforts will create new good paying jobs and strengthen our operational competitiveness.
quotes.speaker: Ted Federau
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada invests over $10 million to help Lower Mainland businesses navigate trade disruptions and seize new opportunities

quotes.quote_text: The Marten Falls Community Access Road Project demonstrates how collaboration with Indigenous communities and the provincial government can improve year-round access, support economic development, and create new opportunities for future generations. The project highlights the importance of working in partnership with Indigenous Peoples to advance infrastructure priorities in a way that respects Indigenous rights and protects the environment.
quotes.speaker: Julie Dabrusin
quotes.article_title: Federal impact assessment of the Marten Falls Community Access Road Project complete

quotes.quote_text: The Government of Canada is committed to supporting businesses and workers in the Hamilton area and throughout southern Ontario. Through the Regional Tariff Response Initiative, we are taking action to help businesses confront tariff-related pressures, secure their place in critical supply chains, protect jobs, and unlock new opportunities for growth and investment. Today's investment for these nine companies in the Hamilton area will support growth and innovation, helping ensure the region remains a key centre for manufacturing and economic activity while contributing to a stronger Canadian economy.
quotes.speaker: Evan Solomon
quotes.dept_en: Federal Economic Development Agency for Southern Ontario
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada announces support for businesses and workers in Hamilton

quotes.quote_text: Hamilton businesses and workers are adapting and succeeding in a changing global economy. Today's investment will help nine local companies grow, protect jobs, and strengthen our region's manufacturing sector.
quotes.speaker: Lisa Hepfner
quotes.dept_en: Federal Economic Development Agency for Southern Ontario
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada announces support for businesses and workers in Hamilton

quotes.quote_text: Hamilton has the businesses, skilled workers, and manufacturing expertise to compete and grow. This investment will help nine local companies expand, create jobs, and build new opportunities for workers and families across our city.
quotes.speaker: John-Paul Danko
quotes.dept_en: Federal Economic Development Agency for Southern Ontario
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada announces support for businesses and workers in Hamilton

quotes.quote_text: Hamilton's success is built on the strength of its businesses and workers. Today's investment in these nine businesses will strengthen our local economy, protect jobs, and seize new opportunities, creating lasting economic benefits for our community.
quotes.speaker: Aslam Rana
quotes.dept_en: Federal Economic Development Agency for Southern Ontario
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada announces support for businesses and workers in Hamilton

quotes.quote_text: This RTRI funding will allow Niko Apparel to invest and strengthen our Canadian production capabilities and become more competitive both here at home and in export markets. Most importantly, it helps us continue to grow our business, create and protect skilled manufacturing jobs, and demonstrate that world-class apparel can be made designed and made right here in Ontario.
quotes.speaker: Joe Camillo
quotes.dept_en: Federal Economic Development Agency for Southern Ontario
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada announces support for businesses and workers in Hamilton

quotes.quote_text: Supporting Red River Métis communities in ways that are meaningful to their values and traditions contributes to a more inclusive agricultural sector. This project will create a better understanding of Red River Métis producer experiences and priorities, help tackle identified challenges, support their participation in agriculture and highlight the important contributions they make to Canada’s agriculture sector.
quotes.speaker: Heath MacDonald
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada invests in Red River Métis participation in agriculture

quotes.quote_text: Red River Métis agricultural producers have deep knowledge, experience and perspectives that strengthen Manitoba’s agriculture sector. As we look to the future of agriculture in our province, it’s important that their voices are at the table and that we listen to their priorities and ambitions. I’m proud that our government is supporting this work and helping create more opportunities for Red River Métis producers to contribute, grow and succeed.
quotes.speaker: Ginette Lavack
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada invests in Red River Métis participation in agriculture

quotes.quote_text: The Red River Métis have helped to shape the rich agricultural landscape of the Canadian prairies since before Canada’s confederation. The Manitoba Métis Federation is grateful for the opportunity to bring together Red River Métis Citizens who actively participate in the agriculture and agri-food sectors to better understand their priorities, opportunities, and challenges, and to develop programming and initiatives that will ensure meaningful, sustained Red River Métis participation in this traditional economy.
quotes.speaker: David Beaudin
quotes.speaker_title: Minister for Agriculture, Manitoba Métis Federation
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada invests in Red River Métis participation in agriculture

quotes.quote_text: This agreement is a step forward in reconciliation, and it is built on the leadership Gitanyow has shown in caring for the salmon in this watershed. It covers the next ten years of making decisions about this fishery together, and that is what keeps salmon healthy and the fishery strong for Gitanyow families.
quotes.speaker: Joanne Thompson
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada and Gitanyow Nation Sign Incremental Fisheries Reconciliation Agreement

quotes.quote_text: The Gitanyow Incremental Fisheries Reconciliation Agreement marks a significant step forward towards our ongoing path of reconciliation with Gitanyow. This agreement advances our relationship by fostering new opportunities in fisheries founded on collaboration, mutual respect, and capacity-building.
quotes.speaker: Rebecca Alty
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada and Gitanyow Nation Sign Incremental Fisheries Reconciliation Agreement

quotes.quote_text: Our people have carried the responsibility of caring for the salmon and fisheries within our Lax’yip for thousands of years. This agreement strengthens our ability to continue that work while creating greater opportunities for Gitanyow people to participate in the fisheries that have sustained our Nation. We look forward to continuing to build a strong relationship with Canada based on respect, collaboration and our shared responsibility to ensure healthy salmon populations for generations to come.
quotes.speaker: Joel Starlund/Sk’a’nism Tsa ‘Win’Giit
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada and Gitanyow Nation Sign Incremental Fisheries Reconciliation Agreement

quotes.quote_text: The vision of our Elders, and the strength of our culture and language, connection to the land, and care for one another is the foundation of the Délı̨nę Got’ı̨nę Government. We have much work ahead of us, and on this tenth anniversary acknowledge the efforts of Elders, past leaders and staff to build our government; thank the community members for their ongoing support; and recognize the importance of our work for our youth and generations to come. We are committed to continuing to strengthen our relationships with our Treaty partners, the GNWT and Canada, to implement our self government agreement and land claim in ways that benefit our members, and create opportunities for them and for all residents of the Northwest Territories.
quotes.speaker: Danny Gaudet
quotes.dept_en: Crown-Indigenous Relations and Northern Affairs Canada
quotes.article_title: Celebration of the tenth anniversary of the establishment of the Délı̨nę Got’ı̨nę Government

quotes.quote_text: As the Délı̨nę Got’ı̨nę Government marks its tenth anniversary, we celebrate a decade of strong leadership, community service, and self-determination. The success of this historic self-government agreement over the past ten years reflects the vision and determination of the community and demonstrates what is possible when Indigenous Peoples have the ability to shape their own futures. Our government is proud to recognise these achievements and remains committed to supporting the continued success of the Délı̨nę Got’ı̨nę Government and the people it serves.
quotes.speaker: Rebecca Alty
quotes.dept_en: Crown-Indigenous Relations and Northern Affairs Canada
quotes.article_title: Celebration of the tenth anniversary of the establishment of the Délı̨nę Got’ı̨nę Government

quotes.quote_text: Congratulations to the Déline Got'ine Government and the people of Déline on this important milestone. Over the past decade, the Self-Government Agreement has demonstrated what can be achieved when Indigenous peoples are able to exercise their right to self-government, and when all levels of government work together with mutual respect and a shared commitment to the people they serve. As partners, we have strengthened our government-to-government relationship and created new opportunities to support the community's priorities. I look forward to continuing that work together.
quotes.speaker: R.J. Simpson
quotes.dept_en: Crown-Indigenous Relations and Northern Affairs Canada
quotes.article_title: Celebration of the tenth anniversary of the establishment of the Délı̨nę Got’ı̨nę Government

quotes.quote_text: Canadian livestock producers work hard every day to be resilient in the face of unpredictable challenges due to extreme weather conditions. Through the Livestock Tax Deferral provision, our government is giving them greater flexibility and certainty as they make important decisions about their herds and operations.
quotes.speaker: Heath MacDonald
quotes.article_title: Minister MacDonald announces initial list of 2026 Livestock Tax Deferral regions

quotes.quote_text: In a changing world, Canada needs to build more here at home and sell more in new markets abroad. Last week, we announced more than $11 billion to build six new Canadian Coast Guard icebreakers and create opportunities across Canada’s marine supply chains. Atlantic Canadian companies have the technology and expertise to compete with the best in the world. Now, we’re helping 28 companies and organizations from across the region take their expertise to the world, meet new buyers, and bring more business back home.
quotes.speaker: Sean Fraser
quotes.article_title: Canada helps 20 Atlantic ocean tech companies reach global shipbuilding markets

quotes.quote_text: Our companies are providing world class solutions to the Defence, shipbuilding and maritime sectors. SMM provides an opportunity to showcase these solutions to international partners and further strengthen our ties with German partners who we will be working with much more closely to develop a strong and secure supply chain for our respective countries. We know that strong predictable supply chains ensure programs can be executed successfully and the partnerships made at events such as SMM are crucial to creating and maintaining these connections.
quotes.speaker: Chris Bourque
quotes.article_title: Canada helps 20 Atlantic ocean tech companies reach global shipbuilding markets

quotes.quote_text: Airports are essential infrastructure, no matter where you live in Canada. They connect people to health care, business opportunities, and loved ones. The investment announced today strengthens connectivity in northern Saskatchewan and supports safe and reliable air transportation for the communities that depend on Wollaston Lake Airport.
quotes.speaker: Steven MacKinnon
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada invests in key infrastructure at the Wollaston Lake Airport in northern Saskatchewan

quotes.quote_text: In northern Saskatchewan, reliable transportation is essential infrastructure. For Wollaston Lake and Hatchet Lake Denesuline First Nation, this airport means access to health care, essential supplies, family, and opportunity. This $11.6 million investment from our government will make those vital connections safer and more reliable.
quotes.speaker: Buckley Belanger
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada invests in key infrastructure at the Wollaston Lake Airport in northern Saskatchewan

quotes.quote_text: This investment demonstrates the strong partnership in supporting northern communities. By rehabilitating critical airport infrastructure at Wollaston Lake, we are improving transportation safety and reliability while strengthening year-round access to essential services, economic opportunities, and community connections. These upgrades will help ensure residents and visitors can continue to depend on safe, reliable air transportation for years to come.
quotes.speaker: Kim Gartner
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada invests in key infrastructure at the Wollaston Lake Airport in northern Saskatchewan

quotes.quote_text: The Build Communities Strong Fund is building the infrastructure that Canadians rely on every day. Today’s investment will help provide redundancy and additional pumping capacity to ensure Calgarians have reliable access to water services. This project is essential to unlocking opportunities for future development and meeting demand as northwest Calgary grows.
quotes.speaker: Corey Hogan
quotes.article_title: Building Canada strong by investing in North Calgary Water Servicing project

quotes.quote_text: This funding is an important investment in the North Calgary Water Servicing Project, significantly increasing drinking water capacity for north Calgary while strengthening the overall water system through critical redundancy,” said Michael Thompson, Acting Chief Operating Officer, Water Utility, The City of Calgary. “This investment contributes to a project that will help ensure a reliable supply of clean, safe drinking water for current and future generations of Calgarians.
quotes.speaker: Michael Thompson
quotes.article_title: Building Canada strong by investing in North Calgary Water Servicing project

quotes.quote_text: National parks and national historic sites in Canada are among our country’s greatest shared treasures. The federal government is committed to investing in the infrastructure that supports them, helping to protect our natural and cultural heritage, strengthening resilience to a changing climate, and ensuring visitors can safely experience these remarkable places for generations to come.
quotes.speaker: Julie Dabrusin
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada invests close to $130 million in critical infrastructure and heritage assets in Parks Canada administered places across Cape Breton/Unama’ki and Canso

quotes.quote_text: Cape Breton/Unama’ki and Canso are home to extraordinary natural landscapes and nationally significant historic places that are deeply important to our communities and to visitors around the world. These federal investments help ensure these places remain safe, accessible, and resilient while protecting the natural and cultural heritage that define this region. By investing in infrastructure today, we are helping preserve these special places so they can continue to be enjoyed and appreciated for years to come.
quotes.speaker: Jaime Battiste
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada invests close to $130 million in critical infrastructure and heritage assets in Parks Canada administered places across Cape Breton/Unama’ki and Canso

quotes.quote_text: The funding announced today represents an investment in Cape Breton’s history and in the future of our region. These projects help protect the places that tell our stories, strengthen local communities and create opportunities for visitors to discover what makes Cape Breton and eastern Nova Scotia so special. I’m proud to see federal funding supporting infrastructure projects across the region.
quotes.speaker: Mike Kelloway
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada invests close to $130 million in critical infrastructure and heritage assets in Parks Canada administered places across Cape Breton/Unama’ki and Canso

quotes.quote_text: National parks and national historic sites in Canada are among our country’s greatest shared treasures. The federal government is committed to investing in the infrastructure that supports them, helping to protect our natural and cultural heritage, strengthening resilience to a changing climate, and ensuring visitors can safely experience these remarkable places for generations to come.
quotes.speaker: Julie Dabrusin
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada invests close to $130 million in critical infrastructure and heritage assets in Parks Canada administered places across Cape Breton/Unama’ki and Canso

quotes.quote_text: Cape Breton/Unama’ki and Canso are home to extraordinary natural landscapes and nationally significant historic places that are deeply important to our communities and to visitors around the world. These federal investments help ensure these places remain safe, accessible, and resilient while protecting the natural and cultural heritage that define this region. By investing in infrastructure today, we are helping preserve these special places so they can continue to be enjoyed and appreciated for years to come.
quotes.speaker: Jaime Battiste
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada invests close to $130 million in critical infrastructure and heritage assets in Parks Canada administered places across Cape Breton/Unama’ki and Canso

quotes.quote_text: The funding announced today represents an investment in Cape Breton’s history and in the future of our region. These projects help protect the places that tell our stories, strengthen local communities and create opportunities for visitors to discover what makes Cape Breton and eastern Nova Scotia so special. I’m proud to see federal funding supporting infrastructure projects across the region.
quotes.speaker: Mike Kelloway
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada invests close to $130 million in critical infrastructure and heritage assets in Parks Canada administered places across Cape Breton/Unama’ki and Canso

quotes.quote_text: The people of Jasper have shown extraordinary resilience and determination as they rebuild their community. This project reflects our government’s ongoing commitment to supporting that recovery, not just today, but for the long term. Together with our partners, we are accelerating progress so that Jasper emerges stronger, more resilient, and ready to thrive for generations to come.
quotes.speaker: Eleanor Olszewski
quotes.speaker_title: Minister, and Ministerial Lead for Jasper
quotes.article_title: Minister Olszewski announces investment for wastewater infrastructure in Jasper to support ongoing wildfire recovery efforts

quotes.quote_text: Jasper’s experience has underscored how essential resilient infrastructure is to the safety and well-being of all communities. As we rebuild, we have an opportunity to both restore what was here, and to strengthen the systems and infrastructure our community relies upon to better prepare for the challenges of the future. This investment will enhance the resilience of Jasper’s wastewater system, protect the natural environment which surrounds and sustains us, and help ensure that our infrastructure serves and supports our community as it recovers, rebuilds, and prepares for its exciting future. We are grateful to both the Government of Canada and the Government of Alberta for their investments in this important project and for their continued partnership in Jasper’s continuing recovery and long-term resilience.
quotes.speaker: Richard Ireland
quotes.article_title: Minister Olszewski announces investment for wastewater infrastructure in Jasper to support ongoing wildfire recovery efforts

quotes.quote_text: This settlement has been a long time coming for the people of Hatchet Lake Denesuline First Nation. Our ancestors entered into Treaty 10 with the understanding that its promises would be honoured, including the land that was owed to our people. Today, we honour the generations who carried this claim forward and whose determination brought us here. This agreement gives our Nation an opportunity to invest in our community and create a stronger future for our children and grandchildren.
quotes.speaker: Chief Bartholomew J. Tsannie
quotes.dept_en: Crown-Indigenous Relations and Northern Affairs Canada
quotes.article_title: Hatchet Lake Denesuline First Nation reaches settlement agreement on Treaty Land Entitlement specific claim

quotes.quote_text: Treaties are promises, and for too long, the promises made to Hatchet Lake Denesuline First Nation under Treaty 10 were not fully honoured. This settlement cannot undo that history, but it recognizes the wrong that was done and takes a meaningful step toward righting it. I'm proud that Canada is fulfilling its responsibility and helping create new opportunities for Hatchet Lake to invest in its land, its community, and its future.
quotes.speaker: Buckley Belanger
quotes.dept_en: Crown-Indigenous Relations and Northern Affairs Canada
quotes.article_title: Hatchet Lake Denesuline First Nation reaches settlement agreement on Treaty Land Entitlement specific claim

quotes.quote_text: Reaching this settlement together, we help support Hatchet Lake Denesuline First Nation in a meaningful way with new opportunities for community development, investment and long-term growth. Saskatchewan continues working with First Nations and the Government of Canada to strengthen relationships and support a stronger future for Indigenous communities across our province, while honouring outstanding obligations.
quotes.speaker: Eric Schmalz
quotes.speaker_title: Minister Responsible for First Nations, Métis and Northern Affairs
quotes.dept_en: Crown-Indigenous Relations and Northern Affairs Canada
quotes.article_title: Hatchet Lake Denesuline First Nation reaches settlement agreement on Treaty Land Entitlement specific claim

quotes.quote_text: Canada has what the world wants and increasingly needs, whether it's critical minerals, conventional and clean energy, or the potash that helps feed the world. Our plan has always been clear: strengthening our economy at home and expanding our trade relationships abroad. In Asheville, I met with partners from around the globe to deepen economic cooperation, advance shared priorities, and create new opportunities for Canadian businesses and workers. These discussions support the trade diversification Canadians are seeking and reinforce Canada's role as a reliable partner in an increasingly uncertain global economy.
quotes.speaker: François-Philippe Champagne
quotes.article_title: Minister Champagne advances Canada's economic interests at G20 meeting in North Carolina

quotes.quote_text: The Government of Canada is taking action to improve mental health outcomes for youth by investing in research that supports better services and stronger decision-making. Through the Youth Mental Health Fund, this new investment will support the evaluation of real-world programs and the establishment of a national platform to share proven approaches, ensuring young people and their families get the high-quality care they deserve.
quotes.speaker: Marjorie Michel
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada announces $13M in new youth mental health research funding opportunities

quotes.quote_text: Young people deserve mental health care that is grounded in the best available evidence and responsive to their needs. These investments will help us better understand what works, for whom and in what settings, and put that knowledge into the hands of the people delivering care. By bringing together researchers, service providers, youth and families, we can help ensure effective approaches reach more young people across Canada.
quotes.speaker: Maggie Chi
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada announces $13M in new youth mental health research funding opportunities

quotes.quote_text: At CIHR, we know that generating scientific evidence is only part of the solution; what truly matters is how that evidence is applied to improve everyday care. By advancing implementation science and building a shared evidence platform, we are helping ensure that cutting-edge research translates into meaningful improvements in care for young people and their families. We encourage Canada’s research community to apply for these open funding opportunities and join us in building a stronger, more responsive mental health system for our youth.
quotes.speaker: Dr. Paul Hébert
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada announces $13M in new youth mental health research funding opportunities

quotes.quote_text: The Institute of Neurosciences, Mental Health and Addiction supports research that helps us better understand the factors that influence brain health across the lifespan. There are a number of interventions that have been proven to protect and improve youth mental health, and these programs have the potential to promote lifelong brain health. It is important that we invest in approaches with demonstrated effectiveness while directing research toward areas where evidence gaps remain. We are proud to support the researchers, clinicians and community partners who will advance this important work.
quotes.speaker: Dr. Patricia Conrod
quotes.speaker_title: Scientific Director, Mental Health and Addictio
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada announces $13M in new youth mental health research funding opportunities

quotes.quote_text: Today’s launch of the new Energy and Electricity Workforce Alliance is a crucial step toward securing Canada’s energy future. Building a strong workforce requires the voices of those closest to workers, employers, educators and Indigenous partners. This new Alliance will bring those voices to the forefront to help ensure Canada’s electricity and energy sector has the skilled workforce it needs for the future.
quotes.speaker: The Honorable Patty Hajdu
quotes.article_title: Minister Hajdu establishes the Energy & Electricity Workforce Alliance

quotes.quote_text: Amidst global volatility and growing power demand, Canada is taking action to strengthen our position as an energy superpower. The Energy and Electricity Workforce Alliance is a key part of that, bringing together partners to make sure Canadian workers have the right skills and support workforce development across the energy sector. By investing in our workforce today, we are preparing to build the energy systems and economy of tomorrow.
quotes.speaker: The Honorable Tim Hodgson
quotes.article_title: Minister Hajdu establishes the Energy & Electricity Workforce Alliance

quotes.quote_text: Canada’s energy strength is built on its resource endowment and the expertise of a highly skilled workforce across the sector. From conventional energy to emerging technologies, Canadian energy companies play an important role in providing reliable, affordable and sustainable energy choices while adapting to changing markets, new technologies and major project demands. Energy Council of Canada is pleased to be a part of the Energy and Electricity Workforce Alliance to help ensure Canada can anticipate workforce challenges, identify practical solutions and take timely action to support the people and skills needed for sector’s continued success.
quotes.speaker: Howard Shearer
quotes.article_title: Minister Hajdu establishes the Energy & Electricity Workforce Alliance

quotes.quote_text: This investment is a significant step toward building the workforce that Canada’s energy future demands. As our sector is transformed by new technologies, digital innovation and major infrastructure development, success will depend on collaboration, coordination and a shared commitment to workforce planning. Through the Energy and Electricity Workforce Alliance, EHRC will bring partners together to strengthen workforce planning and develop the skilled workforce needed to support economic growth, critical infrastructure and a resilient energy future. We are proud to lead this effort and help position Canada’s workforce to seize the opportunities of a rapidly evolving sector.
quotes.speaker: Michelle Branigan
quotes.article_title: Minister Hajdu establishes the Energy & Electricity Workforce Alliance

quotes.quote_text: Electricity demand in Canada is set to grow rapidly as industries electrify and the economy digitizes. Wind, solar and energy storage are the fastest and most affordable ways to meet that demand while modernizing the grid. However, none of this happens without skilled workers. That’s why CanREA is proud to work with partners in the Energy and Electricity Workforce Alliance to help build the workforce Canada needs.
quotes.speaker: Vittoria Bellissimo
quotes.article_title: Minister Hajdu establishes the Energy & Electricity Workforce Alliance

quotes.quote_text: Paterson is an important border crossing in British Columbia’s West Kootenay region and a crucial economic link for the whole province. Once completed, the new port of entry will provide travellers and commercial carriers with a smooth and more efficient border crossing experience, and equip Border Services Officers with modern infrastructure and technologies to support them keep the border secure.
quotes.speaker: Nina Patel
quotes.article_title: The CBSA begins construction to modernize Paterson port of entry in British Columbia

quotes.quote_text: Across Ontario, hundreds of thousands of young students ride on school buses. By working with school bus operators to electrify their fleets, we are helping them cut carbon emissions and reduce the environmental impact of getting our kids to school safely. The federal government is proud to support public transit and school bus operators as they transition to a zero-emission bus fleet.
quotes.speaker: Karina Gould
quotes.article_title: Federal government and Switzer-Carty Transportation Services invest in school bus electrification

quotes.quote_text: Electrifying a school bus fleet is about more than replacing diesel buses with electric ones—it requires careful planning across routes, operations, infrastructure and maintenance. This investment has helped us understand what that transition will look like for our fleet and how we can do it responsibly, while continuing to provide safe and reliable transportation for the more than 125,000 students we serve every day.
quotes.speaker: Dan Maradin
quotes.article_title: Federal government and Switzer-Carty Transportation Services invest in school bus electrification

quotes.quote_text: Saskatchewan businesses have always found ways to overcome challenges, from fluctuations in commodity prices to extreme weather events. Today, they are responding to unjustified U.S. tariffs with that same resilience by investing in their operations, strengthening domestic supply chains, and expanding into new markets. In doing so, they are protecting jobs and helping build a stronger Canadian economy. Through PrairiesCan, our government is proud to stand with them through investments supporting their efforts to adapt, grow, and compete.
quotes.speaker: Eleanor Olszewski
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada announces investments to support Saskatchewan workers and businesses

quotes.quote_text: No matter what, our Plan A was always to defend Canadian workers, businesses and industries and help them become more prosperous and independent – because we can give ourselves more than anyone can take away. Growing up on the Prairies, it has been clear to me my whole life that Saskatchewan is pivotal to the Canadian economy, and I am proud to stand with them against tariffs in the short-term, while helping them pivot, grow, and thrive in the long-term.
quotes.speaker: Tim Hodgson
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada announces investments to support Saskatchewan workers and businesses

quotes.quote_text: Saskatchewan is home to world-class businesses and workers who make products that can compete with anyone, anywhere. This new $11.6 million investment will help Saskatoon companies build more here at home and find new customers around the world. In the face of unjustified tariffs, Saskatchewan businesses and workers are stepping up — and our government is going to keep showing up for them.
quotes.speaker: Buckley Belanger
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada announces investments to support Saskatchewan workers and businesses

quotes.quote_text: Saskatchewan is full of high-end machine shops, and we’re not one of them — we build what isn’t there. Twice now, a crisis has shown up uninvited. When Canada needed ventilators, we became Saskatchewan’s first licensed medical device manufacturer and built them here; this investment lets us answer tariffs the same way. Same purpose both times: drive change to make the world better.
quotes.speaker: Jim Boire
quotes.speaker_title: P. Eng. PMP, President and Founder
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada announces investments to support Saskatchewan workers and businesses

quotes.quote_text: Drake Meats is in the final stages of constructing its new federally inspected plant in Saskatoon, scheduled to open in December 2026. The new Saskatoon facility will increase Drake Meats production capacity and deliver high-quality, Canadian-produced products to consumers across the country. Drake Meats appreciates the strong support provided by the PrairiesCan RTRI investment, along with our other key partners—FCC, Westcap and a local group of Saskatoon investors—especially during this challenging time for the Canadian ag sector due to trade issues and global conflicts.
quotes.speaker: Caileigh Beckman
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada announces investments to support Saskatchewan workers and businesses

quotes.quote_text: We’re helping businesses here in Nova Scotia, like Ace Machining, adapt to the unjustified U.S. tariffs. For Ace, that means buying a new CNC machine to boost productivity, expand in the Canadian market, and compete for new business around the world. The $14 million in direct support we’re announcing today will help Ace and 26 other businesses and organizations across the province. These are among the first investments we’re delivering, with more to come across Atlantic Canada. Our government will continue to make sure our response is fast and agile, so workers and businesses affected by these tariffs get the support they need.
quotes.speaker: Sean Fraser
quotes.article_title: Canada invests $14M to help Nova Scotia businesses respond to tariffs

quotes.quote_text: As global trade relationships shift, businesses here in Dartmouth need to be ready to compete and seize new opportunities. Of the $14 million our federal government is investing across Nova Scotia today, more than $400,000 is going right here to Ace Machining for a new CNC machine that will help them produce more, expand in the Canadian market, and compete for new customers around the world. This is the kind of immediate, targeted support Canada’s new government is delivering to help local businesses adapt to tariffs, grow and succeed in a changing global economy.
quotes.speaker: Darren Fisher
quotes.article_title: Canada invests $14M to help Nova Scotia businesses respond to tariffs

quotes.quote_text: Trade wars have real consequences, affecting the jobs and livelihoods of hard-working people on both sides of the border. When the first round of U.S. tariffs was introduced, we decided to remove American suppliers from consideration during our equipment procurement process. We selected the Matsuura MX-420 distributed by Elliott Matsuura Canada, which is increasing our throughput, improving productivity, and enhancing our competitiveness on the world stage. Our purchase alone will not change the outcome of the trade dispute, but we hope that if enough Canadian companies make similar decisions, it will send a clear message.
quotes.speaker: Ron Wallace
quotes.article_title: Canada invests $14M to help Nova Scotia businesses respond to tariffs

quotes.quote_text: With many families still feeling the pressure of higher costs, we’re extending the federal fuel tax suspension to keep more money in Canadians’ pockets. This will provide meaningful relief for families and businesses and help make everyday life more affordable.
quotes.speaker: François-Philippe Champagne
quotes.article_title: The Government of Canada extends the federal fuel excise tax relief on gasoline, diesel, and aviation fuels for Canadians

quotes.quote_text: Canadians should not have to pay for what they did not cause – whether it is disruption in the Middle East or an unjustified trade war. An affordable, comfortable life is a priority for our government, and by extending the suspension of the fuel excise tax, we are ensuring more money stays in Canadians’ pockets, and standing with every Canadian family as we build a stronger, more resilient Canada.
quotes.speaker: Tim Hodgson
quotes.article_title: The Government of Canada extends the federal fuel excise tax relief on gasoline, diesel, and aviation fuels for Canadians

quotes.quote_text: The progress achieved at McIlvenna Bay is a clear example of what Canada can accomplish when governments, Indigenous partners, workers and industry work together. As one of Canada’s most significant new sources of copper and zinc, this project is strengthening our economic prosperity and national security at a time when we have never needed to build for ourselves more. That is why, through the Major Projects Office, we are moving faster on projects of national interest that unlock our resources; create opportunities for Canadians; and deliver lasting prosperity in Saskatchewan and across Canada.
quotes.speaker: Tim Hodgson
quotes.article_title: Canada celebrates progress on the McIlvenna Bay mine: production underway, jobs created, supply chains strengthened

quotes.quote_text: McIlvenna Bay means real opportunities for workers, families and communities in rural and northern Saskatchewan. This project demonstrates how responsible resource development and strong Indigenous partnerships can build a more resilient economy while maximizing on-the-ground benefits for local Saskatchewan communities and for Canadians from coast to coast to coast.
quotes.speaker: Buckley Belanger
quotes.article_title: Canada celebrates progress on the McIlvenna Bay mine: production underway, jobs created, supply chains strengthened

quotes.quote_text: Reaching first production at McIlvenna Bay is an important milestone for Eldorado, local communities, Indigenous peoples, investors and our employees and contractors who have helped bring this project to life. We appreciate the Government of Canada’s focus on advancing major projects and creating the conditions for investment, jobs and more-resilient supply chains. With first production achieved, a study underway to evaluate a potential mill expansion and the addition of a silver-lead circuit, and significant district-scale exploration potential, we look forward to continuing to work with governments and Indigenous partners to unlock McIlvenna Bay’s full potential for Canada.
quotes.speaker: Christian Milau
quotes.article_title: Canada celebrates progress on the McIlvenna Bay mine: production underway, jobs created, supply chains strengthened

quotes.quote_text: Newfoundland and Labrador is ready to build. We have the resources, expertise, people, and the know-how. This co-operation agreement with the province implements a “one project, one review” approach to environmental and impact assessments on major projects. We are simplifying the process to attract more investment to support our communities. Together, we’re building Newfoundland and Labrador strong to build Canada strong.
quotes.speaker: Joanne Thompson
quotes.article_title: Newfoundland and Labrador and Canada sign co-operation agreement to accelerate project assessments

quotes.quote_text: This agreement represents another milestone in efficient project reviews and shows our commitment to supporting responsible sustainable development that protect the environment, strengthen the economy, and uphold obligations to Indigenous Peoples .
quotes.speaker: Julie Dabrusin
quotes.article_title: Newfoundland and Labrador and Canada sign co-operation agreement to accelerate project assessments

quotes.quote_text: This agreement in principle reflects the determination of the government of Newfoundland and Labrador and the federal government to deliver for Canadians. By reducing duplication and coordinating impact assessments, we are creating greater certainty for investors and Indigenous rights holders and helping major projects move more efficiently.
quotes.speaker: Dominic LeBlanc
quotes.speaker_title: President, Internal Trade and One Canadian Economy
quotes.article_title: Newfoundland and Labrador and Canada sign co-operation agreement to accelerate project assessments

quotes.quote_text: Our government is focused on delivery, not delay, and this co-operation agreement with Newfoundland and Labrador is another step in getting big things built in Newfoundland and Labrador, from energy to mines to roads and new transmission lines. Improving efficiency and streamlining approvals with our partners in the province means that we can meet the moment by responsibly and efficiently building the infrastructure that will secure Canada’s economic future.
quotes.speaker: Tim Hodgson
quotes.article_title: Newfoundland and Labrador and Canada sign co-operation agreement to accelerate project assessments

quotes.quote_text: The cooperation agreement aims to streamline project assessments. By eliminating duplication in environmental assessments and regulatory processes, the Government of Newfoundland and Labrador and the Government of Canada will create efficiency, increase certainty for stakeholders and attract investment in our province. Together, we will continue to ensure environmental protections are upheld and development occurs in a sustainable manner for all of us.
quotes.speaker: Andrea Barbour
quotes.article_title: Newfoundland and Labrador and Canada sign co-operation agreement to accelerate project assessments

quotes.quote_text: Canada is a Pacific nation, and our security and prosperity are closely connected to the security of the Indo-Pacific. Bringing defence leaders from across the region together in Victoria strengthens the relationships, trust and cooperation we need to respond to shared challenges. Canada will continue to work alongside our Allies and partners to advance a free, open and stable Indo-Pacific, grounded in international law.
quotes.speaker: David J. McGuinty
quotes.article_title: Canada concludes 28th Indo-Pacific Chiefs of Defense Conference in Victoria

quotes.quote_text: I was very pleased to co-host this year’s Indo-Pacific Chiefs of Defense Conference and to welcome colleagues from across the region to Canada. The security challenges we face are increasingly complex, and no country can address them alone. The conference gave us an important opportunity to strengthen our relationships, learn from one another and identify how we can work even more closely together. This collaboration builds trust and understanding and makes us better prepared to face the challenges ahead.
quotes.speaker: General Jennie Carignan
quotes.article_title: Canada concludes 28th Indo-Pacific Chiefs of Defense Conference in Victoria

quotes.quote_text: For more than 40 years, the Temiskaming Art Gallery has been showcasing the rich artistic heritage of Northeastern Ontario through a bilingual program deeply committed to regional, Indigenous and women artists. Thanks to this investment, local residents and visitors will continue to discover the stories, creativity and cultural heritage that bring our communities together.
quotes.speaker: Marc Miller
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada supports the Temiskaming Art Gallery

quotes.quote_text: The Temiskaming Art Gallery is an important cultural hub for our region, connecting people with the artists, stories and history that define Northeastern Ontario. This funding will support bilingual exhibitions, educational programming, and community initiatives that make arts and heritage more accessible to residents and visitors. By investing in organizations like the Gallery, we are helping strengthen community life while celebrating the unique cultural identity of our region.
quotes.speaker: Pauline Rochefort
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada supports the Temiskaming Art Gallery

quotes.quote_text: Canada’s top athletes are a source of pride for our entire country and are among our greatest ambassadors. The Government of Canada’s investment in the Canadian Sport Institute Ontario will see Canadian athletes better supported at every step on their path to the podium. We are building Canada strong through sport, from playground to podium.
quotes.speaker: Adam van Koeverden
quotes.article_title: Building Canada strong from playground to podium — Government of Canada invests in Ontario Sport

quotes.quote_text: The Toronto Pan Am Sports Centre and Canadian Sport Institute Ontario are vital athletics resources, helping make Scarborough a hub of healthy, active lifestyles and a home of champions. Supporting renovations at CSIO demonstrates how we are building a stronger Canada by investing in our athletes.
quotes.speaker: Gary Anandasangaree
quotes.article_title: Building Canada strong from playground to podium — Government of Canada invests in Ontario Sport

quotes.quote_text: We are incredibly grateful to the Government of Canada for this important investment through the Build Communities Strong Fund in support of our facility renovations. This funding will help us enhance the daily training environment for high-performance athletes and coaches across Ontario, ensuring they have access to the facilities, resources and tools they need to train, compete and perform at their best. Investing in the environments where athletes prepare is an investment in their pursuit of excellence and in the future of Canadian sport.
quotes.speaker: Debbie Low
quotes.article_title: Building Canada strong from playground to podium — Government of Canada invests in Ontario Sport

quotes.quote_text: Canada did not choose this trade conflict with the United States, but we are determined to support the workers, businesses, and communities facing its impacts. Manitoba manufacturers have long been a driving force behind the success of North American free trade, and they are now adapting to a fundamentally different trading environmentby investing in new equipment, increasing production, and pursuing new markets. Our government is proud to stand with businesses as they strengthen supply chains, grow domestic capacity, and create the conditions for a stronger, more resilient Canadian economy.
quotes.speaker: Eleanor Olszewski
quotes.article_title: Federal investment helps defend Winnipeg’s advanced manufacturing sector against U.S. tariffs

quotes.quote_text: Strong supply chains are essential to communities in Winnipeg, whether for community infrastructure or economic development. Investments in Manitoba’s manufacturing sector help build that capacity here at home, while creating new opportunities for businesses to grow and reach new markets. That strengthens our economy and supports a more resilient and connected Canada.
quotes.speaker: Rebecca Chartrand
quotes.article_title: Federal investment helps defend Winnipeg’s advanced manufacturing sector against U.S. tariffs

quotes.quote_text: Fort Garry Fire Trucks greatly appreciates the ongoing support for manufacturers being provided by the Canadian Government. Funding provided to Fort Garry Fire Trucks by the Canadian Government, through PrairiesCan’s Regional Tariff Response Initiative and Business Scale-up and Productivity Program, will allow Fort Garry Fire Trucks to increase its manufacturing capacity and secure its supply chain by bringing the manufacture of key fire truck components, currently being sourced internationally, back into Canada. This funding will increase the number of trucks built, generate increased economic activity, and create new well-paying manufacturing jobs. Fire trucks are essential to ensure the safety of our communities. Supporting Canadian emergency service manufacturers to ensure that Canada has the ability to build its own fire trucks is important, especially in these uncertain times.
quotes.speaker: James Peters
quotes.article_title: Federal investment helps defend Winnipeg’s advanced manufacturing sector against U.S. tariffs

quotes.quote_text: Winnipeg’s manufacturing sector is built on skilled workers, strong businesses and a long history of innovation. At a time when tariffs are creating new challenges, the companies receiving support today are investing in their operations, creating opportunities for growth and strengthening supply chains here at home. These investments will help ensure Winnipeg businesses remain competitive and continue contributing to a strong Canadian economy.
quotes.speaker: Ben Carr
quotes.article_title: Federal investment helps defend Winnipeg’s advanced manufacturing sector against U.S. tariffs

quotes.quote_text: Winnipeg manufacturers are the people who build, produce and keep our local economy moving. As we face uncertainty from U.S. tariffs, we’re making sure businesses right here in Winnipeg have the support they need to adapt, invest and grow. These investments will help local manufacturers modernize, strengthen their supply chains and create more good, skilled jobs in our community. I am proud to see federal support delivering real results for Winnipeg West and helping our local businesses build a stronger future right here at home.
quotes.speaker: Doug Eyolfson
quotes.article_title: Federal investment helps defend Winnipeg’s advanced manufacturing sector against U.S. tariffs

quotes.quote_text: In the face of President Trump’s latest tariffs, we’re working with all levels of government to lower costs for families, keep workers on the job and get shovels in the ground faster on new homes. Mayor Parrish and Mississauga council were early leaders in lowering development charges and with today’s announcement of new provincial and federal funding for housing-enabling infrastructure, we’re continuing our progress to make homes more affordable for families in Mississauga and across Ontario.
quotes.speaker: Doug Ford
quotes.article_title: Canada and Ontario Making Homes More Affordable in Mississauga

quotes.quote_text: Together, we’re building Ontario and Canada strong. By partnering with Ontario, the federal government is helping speed up housing construction by lowering up-front costs and investing in housing-enabling infrastructure projects — building strong, resilient communities that boost housing supply and drive economic opportunities.
quotes.speaker: Jennifer McKelvie
quotes.article_title: Canada and Ontario Making Homes More Affordable in Mississauga

quotes.quote_text: Building the homes Canadians need takes collaboration at every level. Through the Development Charge Reduction Program, the Government of Canada is working alongside Ontario and the City of Mississauga to help reduce the costs of new housing and support the infrastructure needed to accommodate growth. This investment will help turn plans into new homes, strengthen local communities and create more opportunities for Canadians to find a place to call home.
quotes.speaker: Peter Fonseca
quotes.article_title: Canada and Ontario Making Homes More Affordable in Mississauga

quotes.quote_text: Everyone deserves a safe, affordable place to call home. Through the Building Communities Strong Fund, we are partnering with the Ontario Government to reduce development charges and make critical infrastructure investments. The funds allocated to the City of Mississauga will lower costs and speed up construction to get more Mississaugans into homes that meet their needs at prices they can afford.
quotes.speaker: Charles Sousa
quotes.article_title: Canada and Ontario Making Homes More Affordable in Mississauga

quotes.quote_text: Across Ontario, there is a need for critical infrastructure and housing of all types to support our fast-growing communities. That is why our government continues to deliver programs like the Development Charge Reduction Program alongside our federal partners, which helps provide cities like Mississauga with the funding they need to ensure their city remains a desirable place to live, work and raise a family. Congratulations to Mayor Parrish and the Mississauga City Council for working with us to bring the dream of homeownership within reach for more Mississauga families.
quotes.speaker: Rob Flack
quotes.article_title: Canada and Ontario Making Homes More Affordable in Mississauga

quotes.quote_text: Ontario families deserve to live in homes that meet their needs, at a price they can afford. That is why it is important that we decrease the cost of new homes by cutting taxes and fees and simultaneously build infrastructure to accommodate future growth. By investing over $400 million into Mississauga for infrastructure and transit projects, we are removing barriers for growth and supporting families in Mississauga.
quotes.speaker: Sheref Sabawy
quotes.article_title: Canada and Ontario Making Homes More Affordable in Mississauga

quotes.quote_text: Making homeownership more attainable for families requires action to reduce the cost of building homes while ensuring our communities have the infrastructure needed to grow. Through the Development Charge Reduction Program, our government is supporting Mississauga's efforts to lower development charges and unlock new housing, while investing in the infrastructure needed to support growing communities. These investments will help create more housing options, strengthen our communities and support greater affordability for families across Mississauga.
quotes.speaker: Deepak Anand
quotes.article_title: Canada and Ontario Making Homes More Affordable in Mississauga

quotes.quote_text: Families in Mississauga are working hard to build a future here and they deserve a fair shot at owning a home or finding a quality place to rent. Reducing development charges helps bring down the cost of building new homes, and this funding means we can invest in the transit and infrastructure needed to support the neighbourhoods we are building. I am proud to see Mississauga’s leadership recognized and all levels of government taking a Team Canada approach to support housing in our community.
quotes.speaker: Silvia Gualtieri
quotes.article_title: Canada and Ontario Making Homes More Affordable in Mississauga

quotes.quote_text: Mississauga is a growing community, and we need to make sure families can find homes they can afford while having the infrastructure and services they rely on. This investment will help lower the cost of building new homes, support critical transit and community infrastructure, and help get more shovels in the ground. I’m proud to see our government working with our federal and municipal partners to deliver meaningful results for families across Mississauga.
quotes.speaker: Nina Tangri
quotes.speaker_title: MPP for Mississauga—Streetsville and Associate Minister
quotes.article_title: Canada and Ontario Making Homes More Affordable in Mississauga

quotes.quote_text: Today’s announcement is great news for Mississauga. Through Premier Ford’s leadership, our government is lowering the cost of building new homes while ensuring the necessary investments are made in building critical infrastructure. This will bring the dream of home ownership to more people and keep Mississauga as a great place to live, work and raise a family.
quotes.speaker: Natalia Kusendova-Bashta
quotes.article_title: Canada and Ontario Making Homes More Affordable in Mississauga

quotes.quote_text: Our government’s historic investment of over $400 million in housing-supportive infrastructure in Mississauga builds on Mayor Parrish’s forward-thinking leadership in reducing development charges and lowering the cost of building new homes. Combined with our government’s HST relief, these measures could save local families over $160,000 on a new home, while helping get shovels in the ground to unlock 90,000 new homes across Mississauga, including in transformative waterfront communities like Brightwater and Lakeview Village. By working together with our federal and municipal partners, we’re helping ensure the next generation can achieve the dream of homeownership and build their future in vibrant, affordable communities.
quotes.speaker: Rudy Cuzzetto
quotes.speaker_title: Parliamentary Assistant to the Minister, MPP for Mississauga-Lakeshore
quotes.article_title: Canada and Ontario Making Homes More Affordable in Mississauga

quotes.quote_text: This is great news for the people of Mississauga – especially for those looking to buy a home, for those looking for a reasonably priced apartment, and for workers in the construction sector. This significant funding from our provincial and federal partners will facilitate our investments in local transit and in critically needed infrastructure. We have led on cutting development charges. We are proud of that leadership.
quotes.speaker: Mississauga Mayor Carolyn Parrish
quotes.article_title: Canada and Ontario Making Homes More Affordable in Mississauga

quotes.quote_text: The Building Industry and Land Development Association welcomes the announcement today by the federal and provincial governments regarding the significant infrastructure investment for the City of Mississauga in recognition of the city’s commitment to reduce development charges and the cost to build. Mayor Parrish and City Council have been leaders in advancing efforts to accelerate housing supply and economic opportunities and have repeated these initiatives for over a year. We applaud the provincial and federal governments for recognizing that today’s meaningful contribution will help improve new housing project economic viability, and our members look forward to continuing to get shovels in the ground and welcoming future homeowners in the communities that they are proud to build in Mississauga.
quotes.speaker: Dave Wilkes
quotes.article_title: Canada and Ontario Making Homes More Affordable in Mississauga

quotes.quote_text: As both a builder and a proud Mississauga resident, I know how important today’s announcement is for our city and for families hoping to call it home. Reducing development charges is about more than just lowering construction costs. It’s about making it possible to get more homes built, at prices more families can afford. OHBA has been clear that restoring housing affordability will take meaningful action to reduce the cost of delivering new homes. We commend the governments of Ontario and Canada, in partnership with the City of Mississauga under the leadership of Mayor Parrish, for this investment, which is exactly the kind of coordinated action we need to unlock new housing and help more Ontario families achieve the dream of homeownership.
quotes.speaker: Christina Giannone
quotes.article_title: Canada and Ontario Making Homes More Affordable in Mississauga

quotes.quote_text: As Canadian businesses and workers face the impact of unjustified U.S. tariffs, our government is ensuring they have access to the support they need to manage pressures, protect jobs and continue investing in their businesses. These measures are aimed at giving Canadian businesses greater certainty and strengthening their capacity to grow at home and compete around the world. By supporting businesses and workers through this period, we are protecting Canada’s economic strength today while building a more competitive and resilient economy for the future.
quotes.speaker: Rechie Valdez
quotes.dept_en: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
quotes.article_title: Minister Valdez highlights substantive support for workers and businesses in response to U.S. tariffs

quotes.quote_text: Here in the Niagara region and across Canada, our government is taking action to support businesses and workers and strengthen our economy during uncertainty. These new measures will help Canadian businesses access the support they need to protect jobs, make investments and continue to grow. We are focused on creating the conditions for businesses and communities to succeed and on building a strong, competitive Canadian economy for the years ahead.
quotes.speaker: Chris Bittle
quotes.dept_en: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
quotes.article_title: Minister Valdez highlights substantive support for workers and businesses in response to U.S. tariffs

quotes.quote_text: Canada is building the digital infrastructure we need to lead in the age of AI, grow our economy and strengthen our sovereignty. But how we build matters. Data centres must protect ratepayers, respect water and energy resources, and create lasting benefits for the communities that host them. These principles set a clear national standard: If you build in Canada, you must build responsibly and transparently and you must build for Canadians.
quotes.speaker: Evan Solomon
quotes.dept_en: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada launches Canada’s Responsible Data Centre Development Principles

quotes.quote_text: As demand for AI grows, municipalities are increasingly being asked to review complex data centre proposals that will have significant impacts on local communities. Today’s announcement is an important first step in helping municipalities better understand and assess projects being proposed in their regions. No two data centre projects are alike, nor will they have the same impact. Municipal leaders need clear and complete information to make informed decisions. FCM welcomes today’s commitment by industry leaders to work closely with local governments, mitigate local impacts and ensure local benefits. We look forward to continuing to work with the federal government and industry to improve transparency, strengthen accountability and provide municipalities with the resources they need to protect local interests.
quotes.speaker: Tim Tierney
quotes.dept_en: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada launches Canada’s Responsible Data Centre Development Principles

quotes.quote_text: People across the province are feeling the effects of this trade uncertainty, and we need to hear directly from the workers, businesses and industries on the front lines in Northern B.C. Their insights will help ensure our response reflects the realities businesses are facing. The federal government is stepping up with new support to help workers, families, and businesses navigate these challenges while strengthening Canada’s long-term economic resilience.
quotes.speaker: Gregor Robertson
quotes.article_title: Minister Robertson convenes Northern B.C. businesses to discuss impacts of ongoing U.S. trade situation

quotes.quote_text: Farmers work hard to prepare for growing seasons, but extreme weather can quickly change realities on the ground. That’s why we’re committed to supporting producers through our Business Risk Management programs to help with the adaptable support they need to navigate unpredictability and protect their farms.
quotes.speaker: Heath MacDonald
quotes.speaker_title: federal Minister of Agriculture and Agri-Food
quotes.article_title: Governments of Canada and Saskatchewan announce support for producers through the 2026 AgriStability Program

quotes.quote_text: Excess moisture and flooding created challenging conditions for many Saskatchewan producers early in the growing season. Saskatchewan producers are resilient and our Business Risk Management programs are designed to help them manage uncertainty. These changes provide additional flexibility to help producers make decisions that best support their operations.
quotes.speaker: David Marit
