quotes.article_title: Governments of Canada and Saskatchewan announce support for producers through the 2026 AgriStability Program

quotes.quote_text: Saskatchewan producers are managing circumstances beyond their control, and timely, responsive business-risk-management programs are essential. These measures are a positive step that recognizes the real impacts of wet conditions on farm operations. SARM looks forward to continued work with federal and provincial governments to build greater flexibility and meaningful improvements into AgriStability and other risk-management programs so they can respond sooner and more effectively to the diverse and evolving risks facing producers.
quotes.speaker: Bill Huber
quotes.article_title: Governments of Canada and Saskatchewan announce support for producers through the 2026 AgriStability Program

quotes.quote_text: Sask Wheat appreciates the advocacy of the Ministry of Agriculture, Minister Marit and the Government of Canada for producers’ best interests, especially in a year with unique challenges with wet spring conditions. The changes to AgriStability can now take into consideration the unseeded acres due to extremely wet conditions at seeding time or flooded out acres. The losses from not being able to grow canola, cattle feed or any other crop on those acres do affect farm businesses’ bottom lines.
quotes.speaker: Jocelyn Velestuk
quotes.article_title: Governments of Canada and Saskatchewan announce support for producers through the 2026 AgriStability Program

quotes.quote_text: We appreciate the Government of Saskatchewan’s and Government of Canada’s attention to the risk-management tools available to producers. With farms facing another challenging year, the extended deadline gives farmers more time to assess whether AgriStability is right for their operation. While it may not fit every farm, it remains an important part of the risk-management options available to producers.
quotes.speaker: Dean Roberts
quotes.article_title: Governments of Canada and Saskatchewan announce support for producers through the 2026 AgriStability Program

quotes.quote_text: We appreciate the federal and provincial governments providing additional flexibility and increasing the interim benefit for producers dealing with production challenges caused by excess moisture and flooding. These changes will help provide timely support to producers facing difficult growing conditions.
quotes.speaker: Kelly Williamson
quotes.article_title: Governments of Canada and Saskatchewan announce support for producers through the 2026 AgriStability Program

quotes.quote_text: Saskatchewan beekeepers are facing significant production challenges this year due to cool, wet conditions that affected honeybee populations and honey yields. We appreciate the federal and provincial governments' efforts to provide additional flexibility through AgriStability. The extended deadline and enhanced support measures give beekeepers more time to assess the impacts of this difficult season and determine the business risk-management tools that best support their operations.
quotes.speaker: Simon Lalonde
quotes.article_title: Governments of Canada and Saskatchewan announce support for producers through the 2026 AgriStability Program

quotes.quote_text: Canadians and our allies are looking for a strong grid, critical minerals, LNG and more — and none of that is possible without affordable power. The North Coast Transmission Line will deliver the clean electricity needed to unlock B.C.’s world-class deposits, power new processing facilities and secure Canada's role as a trusted global supplier. By building this vital infrastructure faster and more responsibly, we are taking control of our own future and getting big things built in Canada again.
quotes.speaker: Tim Hodgson
quotes.article_title: Canada breaks ground on North Coast Transmission Line to deliver clean power and reduce emissions

quotes.quote_text: Today’s groundbreaking announcement for the North Coast Transmission Line marks a pivotal step for Canada’s critical minerals sector. Major projects like these are strengthening Canada — creating good jobs, attracting investment, cutting carbon emissions and building the infrastructure we need to compete and prosper for generations to come.
quotes.speaker: Dominic LeBlanc
quotes.speaker_title: President, Internal Trade and One Canadian Economy
quotes.article_title: Canada breaks ground on North Coast Transmission Line to deliver clean power and reduce emissions

quotes.quote_text: This critical transmission investment builds on B.C.’s clean energy advantage and unlocks the economic potential of the North Coast. By expanding our transmission system, we are reducing constraints on the grid, supporting sustainable development and opening new opportunities for trade, investment and job creation that will benefit people throughout the province.
quotes.speaker: Adrian Dix
quotes.article_title: Canada breaks ground on North Coast Transmission Line to deliver clean power and reduce emissions

quotes.quote_text: The Government of Canada is committed to building the infrastructure B.C. needs to power economic growth, support communities and create new opportunities right across the province. Today’s groundbreaking of the North Coast Transmission Line marks a major milestone for B.C.’s clean energy future, and at a critical time for Canada, the focus is on building a stronger, more resilient economy. Together we are building B.C. and Canada strong.
quotes.speaker: Gregor Robertson
quotes.article_title: Canada breaks ground on North Coast Transmission Line to deliver clean power and reduce emissions

quotes.quote_text: In a time of global uncertainty, British Columbia is focused on what we can control here at home: diversifying our trading partners and building critical infrastructure to make our province the economic engine of a stronger Canada. The North Coast Transmission Line is a generational project that will power clean growth and deliver thousands of jobs for families across B.C.
quotes.speaker: David Eby
quotes.article_title: Canada breaks ground on North Coast Transmission Line to deliver clean power and reduce emissions

quotes.quote_text: The Canada Infrastructure Bank’s early works investment is helping advance the foundational planning and development activities for the North Coast Transmission Line. This project has the potential to unlock clean power, support economic growth and create long-term benefits for communities, Indigenous partners and businesses across British Columbia.
quotes.speaker: Ehren Cory
quotes.article_title: Canada breaks ground on North Coast Transmission Line to deliver clean power and reduce emissions

quotes.quote_text: Today represents a new beginning for our region, our shared economy and our shared alignment of values that move strong economy-building projects forward. We remain deeply committed to working with our partner First Nations throughout the region, Canada and British Columbia to advance projects that meet our collective goals while ensuring the safety and prosperity of natural habitats for future generations to enjoy. Today marks the commencement of powering our future.
quotes.speaker: Chief Dolleen Logan
quotes.article_title: Canada breaks ground on North Coast Transmission Line to deliver clean power and reduce emissions

quotes.quote_text: Our government is resolute in our commitment to fighting climate change and reaching net-zero by 2050. This is why we are making durable, structural changes to strengthen Canada’s economy through building clean and renewable power, mass electrification, clean technology, and greater energy efficiency in homes and businesses. We just announced the largest clean energy investment in North American history, and we are just getting started.
quotes.speaker: Julie Dabrusin
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada releases new climate report supporting climate resilience planning

quotes.quote_text: Innovation helps improve the way people live, work and connect. At the G20 Innovation Ministerial, Canada joined international partners to exchange ideas and share expertise on emerging technologies, research collaboration and the responsible development of innovation. By working together on common challenges and opportunities, we can help ensure that new technologies benefit Canadians and strengthen our communities.
quotes.speaker: Mélanie Joly
quotes.dept_en: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
quotes.article_title: Canada advances international collaboration at the G20 Innovation Ministerial

quotes.quote_text: The rapid pace of technological change highlights the importance of international dialogue on the responsible development and use of emerging technologies. The G20 Innovation Ministerial provided a valuable opportunity to exchange perspectives and strengthen collaboration on innovation, artificial intelligence and digital technologies. Canada will continue to champion approaches that foster innovation while helping ensure these technologies deliver real benefits for people, businesses and communities.
quotes.speaker: Evan Solomon
quotes.dept_en: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
quotes.article_title: Canada advances international collaboration at the G20 Innovation Ministerial

quotes.quote_text: Canada has a world-class innovation ecosystem driven by researchers, entrepreneurs and organizations that are finding solutions to challenges at home and around the world. Through discussions at the G20 Innovation Ministerial, Canada highlighted the value of collaboration, knowledge-sharing and inclusive innovation. Canada will continue to work with its international partners to make advances in science, technology and research to improve outcomes for Canadians and contribute to global progress.
quotes.speaker: Karim Bardeesy
quotes.dept_en: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
quotes.article_title: Canada advances international collaboration at the G20 Innovation Ministerial

quotes.quote_text: At defining moments in its history, Saskatchewan has responded by building. Today, as Canada navigates a changing global economy, we are building strength at home by supporting Canadian businesses developing the technologies we need to build smarter. ASI Engineering’s new platform will help communities make more informed investments, strengthen their infrastructure and get better value from the assets people rely on every day.
quotes.speaker: Eleanor Olszewski
quotes.article_title: New asset management platform to help communities build smarter receives federal investment

quotes.quote_text: When we support Saskatchewan businesses like ASI Engineering, we’re investing in world-class innovation developed right here at home. This nearly $1 million in federal support from PrairiesCan will help the company bring new technology to market so that they give clients better information to manage their infrastructure, control costs, and plan for the future.
quotes.speaker: Buckley Belanger
quotes.article_title: New asset management platform to help communities build smarter receives federal investment

quotes.quote_text: This support will help speed up ASI Software’s development, bring it to market sooner, and help organizations better manage assets, reduce risk, prioritize investments, and create a positive impact on society faster.
quotes.speaker: Darren Wiebe
quotes.article_title: New asset management platform to help communities build smarter receives federal investment

quotes.quote_text: The shoreline along Glide Path Road is an important part of the community in Pasadena. This work protects more than 75 metres of it from erosion and adds a trail linking South Brook Point to Pasadena Beach, with benches and a viewing area looking out over the lake. Residents and visitors get a new way to be outdoors close to home, and the town gets a coastline that holds up to the weather. By investing in infrastructure that improves and protects our communities, our government is building Newfoundland and Labrador strong.
quotes.speaker: Joanne Thompson
quotes.speaker_title: Minister, and Member of Parliament for St. John’s East
quotes.article_title: Federal government investment charts path to new park amenities and trail in Pasadena

quotes.quote_text: We are delighted to receive funding through the Government of Canada’s Natural Infrastructure Fund for the development of Glide Path Park. This investment will allow us to expand Pasadena’s existing trail network, better connect South Brook Point to trail networks, and create additional spaces where residents and visitors can gather, enjoy the outdoors and experience the natural beauty of our community. The shoreline protection included in this project will also help preserve this important area for years to come. We sincerely thank the Government of Canada for its investment and partnership in making this project possible.
quotes.speaker: Darren Gardner
quotes.article_title: Federal government investment charts path to new park amenities and trail in Pasadena

quotes.quote_text: In many ways, Alberta, Saskatchewan and British Columbia are the beating heart of our energy and natural resource sectors. This week, I saw first-hand the people, projects and partnerships that are building Canada Strong amidst the unjustified trade war we are experiencing. From responsible resource development and world-class research to critical infrastructure and energy innovation, Canadians are creating the conditions for long-term prosperity, security, sustainability and sovereignty.
quotes.speaker: Tim Hodgson
quotes.article_title: Minister Hodgson highlights Western Canada’s role in Canada’s energy and economic future

quotes.quote_text: Our pork producers care deeply about their animals and work hard to protect them against infectious diseases. By investing in swine health surveillance solutions, we are continuing to equip the industry with the tools it needs to detect and respond quickly. This funding reflects our commitment to building a resilient, innovative and globally competitive pork sector that continues to thrive for generations to come.
quotes.speaker: Heath MacDonald
quotes.article_title: Minister MacDonald announces support to advance swine health surveillance in Canada

quotes.quote_text: By enhancing surveillance and diagnostic capabilities, we're not only protecting animal health and welfare but also safeguarding the livelihoods of producers and the stability of our food supply. This project, led by the Canadian Pork Council and taking place right here at the world-class Atlantic Veterinary College, demonstrates our commitment to sector resilience and ensuring Canada remains a trusted leader in pork production.
quotes.speaker: Sean Casey
quotes.article_title: Minister MacDonald announces support to advance swine health surveillance in Canada

quotes.quote_text: Early swine health detection is one of our strongest defences in protecting our herd and maintaining affordable and high-quality Canadian pork products. This $3.1 million investment will improve the speed, accuracy, and coordination of swine health surveillance by advancing innovative diagnostic tools, nationally consistent testing, and secure data systems. The Canadian Pork Council is pleased to collaborate with the Atlantic Veterinary College and partners across veterinary medicine, laboratories, industry and government to turn better surveillance into faster action and stronger protection for Canadian pork producers.
quotes.speaker: Rene Roy
quotes.article_title: Minister MacDonald announces support to advance swine health surveillance in Canada

quotes.quote_text: This project is an important step forward in strengthening Canada's capacity to detect and monitor swine diseases. By advancing diagnostic testing, supporting a coordinated Atlantic Canada surveillance approach, and developing a national proficiency program, we can provide veterinarians and producers with reliable, timely information to help protect herd health and respond effectively to endemic and emerging disease threats.
quotes.speaker: Elizabeth Dobbin
quotes.speaker_title: Principal Investigator and Director of Diagnostic Services Laboratory
quotes.article_title: Minister MacDonald announces support to advance swine health surveillance in Canada

quotes.quote_text: Seizing more than $13.8 million in tobacco and nicotine products shows the strength of Canada’s border enforcement. These actions help protect Canadians and ensure criminal organizations cannot take advantage of our borders for financial gain.
quotes.speaker: Gary Anandasangaree
quotes.article_title: CBSA seizes over $13.8 million in tobacco and nicotine products across Southern Ontario in August

quotes.quote_text: These results reflect the skill, experience and determination of CBSA’s frontline officers across Southern Ontario. Guided by intelligence and supported by tools such as handheld devices, X-ray technology and detector dogs, our officers use their specialized training and expertise to identify contraband and other prohibited or restricted goods. Their knowledge and vigilance are critical to our enforcement efforts.
quotes.speaker: Michael Prosia
quotes.article_title: CBSA seizes over $13.8 million in tobacco and nicotine products across Southern Ontario in August

quotes.quote_text: Canada is strengthening its defence capabilities and the industrial base that sustains them. As lead nation at MSPO, we are showcasing what Canadian workers, innovators and companies can deliver while deepening defence cooperation with Poland and our NATO Allies. A stronger Canadian defence industry means a stronger Canada, a stronger NATO and a more secure Alliance.
quotes.speaker: The Honourable
quotes.article_title: Minister McGuinty to advance defence cooperation and industrial partnerships with Poland at MSPO 2026

quotes.quote_text: Canada's defence industry contributed over $11 billion to Canada's GDP and supports 82,000 jobs . Participating in MSPO 2026 is a chance to strengthen our defence industrial ties across Europe and showcase Canadian innovation. By deepening these trade relationships, Canada can contribute to more resilient supply chains while creating new export opportunities for Canadian businesses and workers.
quotes.speaker: The Honourable
quotes.article_title: Minister McGuinty to advance defence cooperation and industrial partnerships with Poland at MSPO 2026

quotes.quote_text: Northern B.C. businesses, workers and communities are vital to Canada’s economic strength. These investments will help businesses improve productivity, strengthen supply chains and reach new markets, while expanding skills and economic opportunities in rural, remote and Indigenous communities. By responding to today’s trade pressures and investing in the North’s long-term potential, we are supporting good jobs, growing businesses, and building a stronger Canadian economy.
quotes.speaker: Gregor Robertson
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada invests over $11 million to strengthen businesses, jobs and communities in Northern B.C.

quotes.quote_text: We are grateful for PacifiCan’s support, which enables Open Waters Solar to scale manufacturing of our breakthrough technology, drive productivity through automation, attract investment, and create high-paying jobs in Northern BC. This funding positions us to expand our reach in European markets and compete on a global scale.
quotes.speaker: Tony Olynyk
quotes.speaker_title: Chief Commercial Officer, Open Waters Solar
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada invests over $11 million to strengthen businesses, jobs and communities in Northern B.C.

quotes.quote_text: As flooding continues to become more frequent and severe, Canadians can rest assured that the federal government is here to assist when help is needed most. In July we worked to support the Manitoba-led response in the Parkland Region and this funding is another way the federal government can support the ongoing road to recovery here in Manitoba as communities and people across the province get back on their feet after the difficult days earlier this summer.
quotes.speaker: Eleanor Olszewski
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada matches donations to the Red Cross’ 2026 Manitoba Flood Appeal

quotes.quote_text: The time required for people to recover from a flooding event is long after when the water recedes. For the individuals and families impacted, that is when the hard work begins. The Canadian Red Cross thanks everyone who donated to the Manitoba and Ottawa floods appeals, as well as the Government of Canada for matching donations. These matching funds will help people on their journey to recovery.
quotes.speaker: Conrad Sauvé
quotes.speaker_title: President and CEO, Canadian Red Cross
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada matches donations to the Red Cross’ 2026 Manitoba Flood Appeal

quotes.quote_text: In the aftermath of the unprecedented flooding our government worked to ensure that Manitobans had the support they needed through the Disaster Financial Assistance and Manitoba Flood Relief Programs. We announced that we would be matching Red Cross donations and we are pleased to have our federal counterparts matching donations as well. We will continue to work closely with the federal government to provide the necessary support to all Manitobans affected.
quotes.speaker: Lisa Naylor
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada matches donations to the Red Cross’ 2026 Manitoba Flood Appeal

quotes.quote_text: The Canada Day floods in Ottawa had a devastating impact on communities and homes. Many lost more than can be replaced. But our community came forward and helped by giving donations to the Canadian Red Cross to help their neighbours. Today the Government of Canada is also there to help with matching donations. We will always be there to support the people of Ottawa.
quotes.speaker: Anita Vandenbeld
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada matches donations to the Red Cross’ 2026 Manitoba Flood Appeal

quotes.quote_text: This is a deeply meaningful moment for Gitwangak, Gitanyow and Gitsegukla. For more than a decade, we have worked together to bring high school education closer to home, allowing our children to remain connected to their families, culture and communities. Gitksen West Secondary School represents our commitment to our children and their future. Reclaiming education holds profound significance for our people, especially given the history of residential schools. Today, we are bringing education home and creating opportunities for our children on our own terms. We honour everyone who helped carry this vision forward, including those who are no longer with us. This is their legacy, and a legacy we are building for generations to come.
quotes.speaker: Chief Chasity Daniels
quotes.article_title: Gitwangak, Gitanyow and Gitsegukla First Nations celebrate the opening of their new Gitksen West Secondary School

quotes.quote_text: Gitwangak Chief and Council are incredibly proud to celebrate the opening of Gitksen West Secondary School. This moment represents the realization of a vision held by our Elders for many years—a vision to have a Gitksen school where our children can learn through Gitksen culture, values, language, and curriculum while also receiving a strong provincial education. The opening of this school represents years of hard work, determination, and collaboration among the three communities of Gitwangak, Gitanyow, and Gitsegukla. It is an investment in our youth, our culture, and future generations. We are honoured to see the vision of our Elders becoming a reality and look forward to the opportunities this school will provide for our children and communities for generations to come.
quotes.speaker: Deputy
quotes.article_title: Gitwangak, Gitanyow and Gitsegukla First Nations celebrate the opening of their new Gitksen West Secondary School

quotes.quote_text: This is the start of a new era where we empower our flowers to bloom in a world that can benefit from Indigenous Knowledge and ways of being. I am proud of the previous Council members who put in countless hours of work to make this happen. I look forward to seeing Gitksen scholars contributing to our future.
quotes.speaker: Chief Bryan Williams
quotes.article_title: Gitwangak, Gitanyow and Gitsegukla First Nations celebrate the opening of their new Gitksen West Secondary School

quotes.quote_text: We are happy to see Gitxsan West High School completed. We see a day when we have our youth succeed in our communities with Dogwood Certificates and not Leaving Certificates. The students will be given the opportunity to go forward in schooling with crucial supports at school.We look forward in the next couple of years to see the success of our youth going into post-secondary programs.
quotes.speaker: Chief Councillor Annie Howard
quotes.article_title: Gitwangak, Gitanyow and Gitsegukla First Nations celebrate the opening of their new Gitksen West Secondary School

quotes.quote_text: The opening of Gitksen West Secondary School is a significant achievement for the Gitwangak, Gitanyow, and Gitsegukla First Nations. This community-led school will allow students to learn closer to home while strengthening connections to Gitxsan culture, language, and traditions. Through partnerships like this, we are supporting First Nations-led education and creating opportunities for future generations.
quotes.speaker: Mandy Gull-Masty
quotes.article_title: Gitwangak, Gitanyow and Gitsegukla First Nations celebrate the opening of their new Gitksen West Secondary School

quotes.quote_text: The Pacific Island Forum Leaders Meeting is an important opportunity for Canada to work alongside Pacific partners on Pacific-led priorities and solutions. By deepening collaboration with Pacific Islands leaders, Canada is investing in a safer, more stable and resilient region while creating opportunities for shared prosperity that contribute to a more equitable global future
quotes.speaker: Randeep Sarai
quotes.article_title: Secretary of State Sarai concludes participation at Pacific Islands Forum Leaders Meeting

quotes.quote_text: For 175 years, this building has been part of the history of St. Boniface and of those who have helped shape it. Even today, the museum brings the community together and keeps the cultural heritage of Francophones, Métis and First Nations alive. Preserving places like this one means keeping our identity alive, bringing generations closer together and strengthening the bonds that unite us.
quotes.speaker: Marc Miller
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada supports celebrations for the 175th anniversary of the heritage building that houses Le Musée de Saint-Boniface

quotes.quote_text: For the community of St. Boniface, this important anniversary is an opportunity to come together and celebrate a heritage that we can be proud of. The museum has an important place in the life of our region, and I am proud to highlight the Government of Canada’s support for its future, as well as the work of the people who, day after day, help make it a vibrant place of remembrance.
quotes.speaker: Ginette Lavack
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada supports celebrations for the 175th anniversary of the heritage building that houses Le Musée de Saint-Boniface

quotes.quote_text: As we prepare to celebrate the 175th anniversary of this remarkable building on September 7, this investment through Canadian Heritage’s Legacy Fund comes at an especially meaningful moment. For generations, this historic place has carried the stories of our Francophone, Métis and broader community, and today it continues to serve as a museum where those stories can be preserved, shared and understood. This funding will help us continue the careful preservation of the building so that it remains a living place of heritage, learning and community for generations to come.
quotes.speaker: Cindy Desrochers
quotes.speaker_title: Executive Director, Le Musée de Saint-Boniface
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada supports celebrations for the 175th anniversary of the heritage building that houses Le Musée de Saint-Boniface

quotes.quote_text: Who doesn’t love summer at the parks, beaches and lakes in Conception Bay South? Our government is proud to support these new upgrades, ensuring residents and visitors alike can enjoy all the beautiful paths, parks and scenery that Conception Bay South has to offer.
quotes.speaker: Paul Connors
quotes.article_title: Federal government invests in active transportation infrastructure in Conception Bay South

quotes.quote_text: Conception Bay South is fortunate to have an extensive network of trails and outdoor spaces that provide residents and visitors with opportunities to walk, cycle and connect with our natural environment. This funding will support important enhancements to our active transportation infrastructure, including improved change room and locker facilities, additional bicycle parking, and strategically located amenities along the trailway where users can stop, rest and enjoy a meal. These investments will improve the overall experience for active transportation users, encourage more people to choose active modes of transportation, and strengthen connections throughout our community.
quotes.speaker: Darrin Bent
quotes.article_title: Federal government invests in active transportation infrastructure in Conception Bay South

quotes.quote_text: Safe and dependable transportation infrastructure is essential to strong, connected communities across Canada’s North and Arctic. This $405 million investment will help build more dependable connections, strengthen supply chains, create economic opportunities and improve access to essential services. Through the Arctic Infrastructure Fund, we are investing in infrastructure that responds to the needs of northern and Indigenous communities while strengthening Canada’s resilience, security and sovereignty in the Arctic.
quotes.speaker: Steven MacKinnon
quotes.article_title: The Government of Canada invests $405 million to advance the Mackenzie Valley Highway Project and strengthen Arctic connectivity

quotes.quote_text: Today's investment brings a decades-long vision for a stronger, better-connected North another step closer to reality. By improving year-round connectivity, supporting economic development, strengthening Canada's security and sovereignty, and helping communities access the essential services they need, the Mackenzie Valley Highway reflects what can be achieved when federal, territorial, and Indigenous governments and organisations work in partnership to advance shared priorities. The benefits of this transformative project will be felt for generations to come as we move quickly to build a more resilient and prosperous North.
quotes.speaker: Rebecca Alty
quotes.article_title: The Government of Canada invests $405 million to advance the Mackenzie Valley Highway Project and strengthen Arctic connectivity

On behalf of the City of Barrie, I want to thank the Government of Canada for its ongoing commitment to strengthening public transit infrastructure in communities like ours.

The enhanced Regional Tariff Response Initiative will help businesses weather the storm, protect good paying jobs, and make the investments needed to grow, compete, and reach new markets all across the globe. Together, we are building a stronger, more resilient Prairie economy and a stronger Canada.
quotes.speaker: Eleanor Olszewski
quotes.article_title: Eligible businesses in the Prairies can now apply for tariff support under the enhanced Regional Tariff Response Initiative

quotes.quote_text: Canadian agri-businesses are leading the way in creating innovative solutions to reduce emissions and build a more resilient agricultural sector. With support from the ACT – Research and Innovation Stream, SmartGRO can develop new technology that has the potential to help Canadian farmers grow more food while using less electricity. By making indoor agriculture more efficient and sustainable, this innovation can help reduce costs and environmental impacts, while strengthening year-round food production across Canada.
quotes.speaker: Heath MacDonald
quotes.article_title: Minister MacDonald announces up to nearly $895,000 to develop and test new clean technology to benefit Canada’s indoor agriculture sector

quotes.quote_text: Canada has the talent and technology to lead the next generation of controlled-environment agriculture. This support from Agriculture and Agri-Food Canada will help SmartGRO validate at commercial scale a patent-pending, Canadian-developed lighting and intelligent control platform designed to help growers produce more food, year-round, using dramatically less electricity.
quotes.speaker: Jared Wolfe
quotes.article_title: Minister MacDonald announces up to nearly $895,000 to develop and test new clean technology to benefit Canada’s indoor agriculture sector

quotes.quote_text: We’re excited to partner with SmartGRO to test this advanced technology under real-world commercial growing conditions. Improving energy efficiency is essential to the future of indoor agriculture, and innovations like this can help growers reduce costs, increase productivity, and make year-round food production in Canada more sustainable. We’re proud to support its development.
quotes.speaker: Marc Schulz
quotes.article_title: Minister MacDonald announces up to nearly $895,000 to develop and test new clean technology to benefit Canada’s indoor agriculture sector

quotes.quote_text: Our government is focused on making life more affordable for Canadians. The extension of the pause on the federal fuel tax is one of many affordability measures that aim to alleviate some of the financial pressures that Canadians face every day.

quotes.article_title: The Government of Canada extends the federal fuel excise tax relief on gasoline, diesel, and aviation fuels for Canadians

quotes.quote_text: At a time when Canadians are facing uncertainty and higher costs, our government is focused on delivering meaningful relief. Canadians should not have to bear the cost of forces beyond their control. In the face of an unjustified trade war, extending fuel tax relief will help keep more money in the pockets of Canadian families, workers and businesses.
quotes.speaker: Peter Fragiskatos
quotes.speaker_title: Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister, Refugees and Citizenship

quotes.quote_text: In communities like Delta, workers, businesses, and families succeed together. Behind every product on a store shelf is a supply chain powered by Canadian workers and local businesses. By extending fuel tax relief, we are helping keep goods moving, supporting jobs, and easing costs for Canadians. It is a practical measure that will make a real difference for families while strengthening our economy in uncertain times.
quotes.speaker: Jill McKnight
quotes.article_title: The Government of Canada extends the federal fuel excise tax relief on gasoline, diesel, and aviation fuels for Canadians

quotes.quote_text: The inclusion of diesel in Ottawa’s extension of the federal fuel tax pause is welcomed by trucking companies like ours, Aheer Transportation Group, here in Delta, B.C., on behalf of our company drivers, our independent owner-operators, and our customers. Moreover, the lower gasoline costs will just as importantly benefit our drivers, our staff, our customers, and their families in their daily lives and make a real difference in their day-to-day cost of living.
quotes.speaker: Shinda Aheer

quotes.quote_text: Canada has the businesses, the skilled workers, and the expertise to compete and grow. Through the expanded Regional Tariff Response Initiative, we are providing additional support to help businesses respond to tariff pressures, strengthen supply chains, build resilience, and pursue new market opportunities. By investing in Canadian workers, businesses, and industries, we are helping protect jobs, strengthen our economy, and build a more competitive and prosperous future for Canadians.
quotes.speaker: Evan Solomon
quotes.dept_en: Federal Economic Development Agency for Southern Ontario
quotes.article_title: Eligible businesses and organizations in southern Ontario can now apply for support through the enhanced Regional Tariff Response Initiative

quotes.quote_text: Saskatchewan businesses have always persevered through tough times. Today, they are responding to unjustified U.S. tariffs with that same determination—investing in their operations, strengthening domestic supply chains and finding new markets. Their work is helping protect jobs and build a stronger Canadian economy. Through PrairiesCan, our government is standing with them and investing alongside them as they adapt, grow and compete.
quotes.speaker: Eleanor Olszewski
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada investments defend Saskatchewan workers and businesses from U.S. tariffs

quotes.quote_text: Saskatchewan is a trading province, and our world-class businesses and workers make products that can compete with anyone, anywhere. In the face of unjustified tariffs, today’s investment of $5.3 million through Canada’s Regional Tariff Response Initiative will help companies across Saskatchewan build more here at home and find new customers around the world.
quotes.speaker: Buckley Belanger
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada investments defend Saskatchewan workers and businesses from U.S. tariffs

quotes.quote_text: We're proud to grow our manufacturing right here in Regina. This investment sharpens our competitive edge, creates new opportunities for our employees, and reinforces our commitment to delivering the dependable, high-quality equipment our customers expect from Degelman.
quotes.speaker: Richard Greenough
quotes.speaker_title: VP Finance and Chief Financial Officer
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada investments defend Saskatchewan workers and businesses from U.S. tariffs

quotes.quote_text: SeedMaster is proud to build world-class agricultural equipment in Saskatchewan and take it to farmers around the world. This investment will help us accelerate export growth, strengthen our international dealer network, and create more opportunity for the skilled people who design and build our products here at home.
quotes.speaker: Allan Wiens
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada investments defend Saskatchewan workers and businesses from U.S. tariffs

quotes.quote_text: Sport is so much more than physical activity, it is an important part of our culture and the fabric of our communities. It brings people together, supports physical health and well-being, and gives young people opportunities to build confidence, friendships, and lifelong skills. Investing in sport means investing in healthier, more connected communities. Ensuring our sports facilities are accessible means everyone can participate and cheer on their community without barriers. This funding will help create an inclusive facility that serves our community for generations to come.
quotes.speaker: Ben Carr
quotes.article_title: Building Canada strong by supporting professional women’s soccer in Winnipeg

quotes.quote_text: Sport has the power to shape lives and connect people in ways that very few things can. This new multi-use sports facility will build on the legacy of women’s soccer in Canada, creating more opportunities for Canadians to play, train and proudly wear the maple leaf on the world stage. By investing in projects like this, we are strengthening women’s sport and our ability to host major sporting events, including the 2026 FIFA World Cup, while supporting participation and inspiring the next generation of athletes. We’re building Canada Strong, from playground to podium.
quotes.speaker: Adam van Koeverden
quotes.article_title: Building Canada strong by supporting professional women’s soccer in Winnipeg

quotes.quote_text: For decades, Manitobans have demonstrated a deep passion for soccer. From community clubs and school programs, to provincial and national competitions - soccer has brought people together in every corner of our province, and across the globe. The establishment of a professional women's soccer team creates a new pathway for talented athletes right here at home. The Province of Manitoba is thrilled to be part of this historic announcement.
quotes.speaker: Nellie Kennedy
quotes.article_title: Building Canada strong by supporting professional women’s soccer in Winnipeg

quotes.quote_text: Today, we’re opening new doors for women and girls in sport. A professional women’s soccer team means young athletes can see a future for themselves excelling in the sport they love. This is an important step forward for women’s sport in Manitoba, showing there is no limit to what women and girls can achieve.
quotes.speaker: Nahanni Fontaine
quotes.article_title: Building Canada strong by supporting professional women’s soccer in Winnipeg

quotes.quote_text: This project is another great example of what we can accomplish when governments and community partners work together. The City of Winnipeg is proud to join the federal and provincial governments and the Northern Super League in building a great new community facility at the Ralph Cantafio Soccer Complex. It will create more opportunities for girls and young women to play, compete and see a pathway to the highest levels of the sport right here in Winnipeg. We want professional women’s soccer to thrive in our city, and this partnership is an important step toward making that possible.
quotes.speaker: Scott Gillingham
quotes.article_title: Building Canada strong by supporting professional women’s soccer in Winnipeg

quotes.quote_text: Bringing professional women’s soccer to more Canadian communities depends on partnership and investment in local infrastructure. The NSL is grateful for this funding that ensures our players have modern, professional facilities that will help Canada attract and retain the best players in the world. Beyond elite competition, our league aims to develop homegrown players and inspire greatness on and off the pitch, and we are excited about what this club, the stadium and venue enhancements will mean to the Winnipeg sports and soccer community.
quotes.speaker: Christina Litz
quotes.article_title: Building Canada strong by supporting professional women’s soccer in Winnipeg

quotes.quote_text: This is more than a stadium project. It’s an opportunity to rethink sports infrastructure altogether, and what a modern venue can be: adaptive, community-anchored, and built to evolve alongside the sport itself. We’re proud to bring that approach to Winnipeg and help build a home worthy of the next chapter of professional women’s soccer. Investments like this strengthen the game at every level and create the facilities and opportunities needed to support the continued growth of soccer in Canada.
quotes.speaker: Dean Shillington
quotes.article_title: Building Canada strong by supporting professional women’s soccer in Winnipeg

quotes.quote_text: Canada and Poland are strong Allies with a shared understanding of what is required to protect our people and strengthen our collective security. At MSPO, we showcased the very best of Canadian defence innovation, opened new doors for our industries, and renewed a Defence Cooperation Agreement that will deepen our work together for years to come. Canada will continue to stand with Poland as we build a stronger and more secure Euro-Atlantic region.
quotes.speaker: The
quotes.article_title: Minister McGuinty concludes visit to Poland, advancing Canada–Poland defence and industrial cooperation

quotes.quote_text: The RCMP is one of Canada’s most recognizable institutions — with deep roots right here in Saskatchewan — and its long and complex history is an important part of our national story. quotes.speaker: Buckley Belanger
quotes.speaker_title: Secretary, on behalf of the Honourable Gregor Robertson, Minister
quotes.article_title: Federal government invests in cultural infrastructure in Regina

quotes.article_title: Federal government invests in cultural infrastructure in Regina

quotes.quote_text: This investment supports a strong Canada – today and for generations to come. The Board is pleased and grateful to see this investment. We look forward to continuing to collaborate with the Government of Canada, and building on our established track record of being a place for all Canadians.
quotes.speaker: Rod Buckingham
quotes.article_title: Federal government invests in cultural infrastructure in Regina

Through the enhanced Regional Tariff Response Initiative, the Government of Canada is providing new, non-repayable liquidity support to help businesses strengthen supply chains, improve productivity, and pursue new market opportunities. By investing in B.C. businesses, workers and communities, we are protecting jobs, supporting long-term growth, and building Canada strong.

quotes.quote_text: By meeting with us over the summer and sharing their insights and priorities, Canadians have played a critical role in shaping Budget 2026. At a time of ongoing global economic uncertainty and trade tensions, our government is taking action to protect Canadian jobs, make life more affordable, and build long-term prosperity. While challenges remain, we are moving forward with confidence and purpose.
quotes.speaker: François-Philippe Champagne
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada Concludes Pre-Budget Consultations for Budget 2026

quotes.quote_text: This summer's pre-budget consultations gave Canadians a direct voice in shaping the future of their economy. The ideas and priorities they shared will help ensure Budget 2026 delivers on the needs, ambitions, and aspirations of people and communities across the country.
quotes.speaker: Wayne Long
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada Concludes Pre-Budget Consultations for Budget 2026

quotes.quote_text: Canadians from all walks of life have brought valuable insights and diverse perspectives to this year's pre-budget consultations. These contributions will help inform the policies and investments needed to strengthen Canada's economy, support good jobs, and build a more prosperous future for generations to come.
quotes.speaker: Ryan Turnbull
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada Concludes Pre-Budget Consultations for Budget 2026

quotes.quote_text: We are grateful to the Canadians who shared their ideas and priorities for Budget 2026. Their input will help shape the decisions we make to strengthen Canada's economy, protect our sovereignty, unlock new opportunities, and build a more prosperous, competitive, and resilient future for all.
quotes.speaker: Sophie Chatel
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada Concludes Pre-Budget Consultations for Budget 2026

quotes.quote_text: We still have a long way to go to advance reconciliation and build a future grounded in respect, understanding and stronger relationships with Indigenous Peoples. Initiatives like this put reconciliation into action by creating meaningful opportunities for Canadians to learn from Indigenous histories and experiences, hear directly from Survivors and engage in important dialogue.
quotes.speaker: Marc Miller
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada invests in Brantford Native Housing and Darmont GivesBack

quotes.quote_text: Organizations like Brantford Native Housing and Darmont GivesBack are strengthening our communities by creating opportunities for people to come together, learn from one another, and build meaningful connections. These investments will support dialogue, advance reconciliation, promote greater understanding across cultures and generations, and help foster communities where everyone feels valued, respected, and included in our communities.
quotes.speaker: Lisa Hepfner
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada invests in Brantford Native Housing and Darmont GivesBack

quotes.quote_text: Every single life carries a unique melody, found in our ceremonies, the wisdom of our Elders, and the fierce hope of our children. True reconciliation means listening to those melodies, taking the TRC roadmap off the page, and knowing when to step back so Indigenous voices can lead the way.
quotes.speaker: Alma Arguello
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada invests in Brantford Native Housing and Darmont GivesBack

quotes.quote_text: We are deeply grateful to MP Lisa Hepfner and the Department of Canadian Heritage for recognizing the urgency and importance of fostering intergenerational dialogue on race, identity and belonging. This funding enables Darmont GivesBack to bring together youth, elders, newcomers, and long-term residents across the County of Brant in authentic conversation about the lived realities of racism and discrimination. By creating space for respectful, honest dialogue across generations and cultural differences, we are building a foundation for genuine inclusion and community action. This is exactly the kind of partnership needed to advance Canada's Anti-Racism Strategy at the community level.
quotes.speaker: Tobi Adedayo
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada invests in Brantford Native Housing and Darmont GivesBack

quotes.quote_text: Fresh water is central to our quality of life, our environment, and our economic security. Developing a National Water Security Strategy will bring Canadians together around a shared vision for a water-secure Canada, informed by Indigenous Knowledge Systems and diverse experiences. Through investments in the Great Lakes, we are turning that vision into action to protect water quality and ecosystems for generations to come.
quotes.speaker: Julie Dabrusin
quotes.article_title: Minister Dabrusin launches public engagement on Canada’s National Water Security Strategy and announces new projects to protect the Great Lakes from environmental challenges

quotes.quote_text: In Spadina—Harbourfront, the Great Lakes are part of daily life. They are our drinking water, our shoreline, and the parks and public spaces where families gather, children play, and people connect with the water. I am proud that this funding will help bring our waterfront back to health, and that people across my community can now help shape a national strategy to keep our water secure.
quotes.speaker: Chi Nguyen
quotes.article_title: Minister Dabrusin launches public engagement on Canada’s National Water Security Strategy and announces new projects to protect the Great Lakes from environmental challenges

quotes.quote_text: Whitefish Island holds deep cultural and historical significance for Batchewana First Nation, and we have a responsibility to protect and restore this important part of our territory for future generations. This funding will allow us to advance meaningful fish habitat restoration while strengthening our participation in the stewardship that affects the health of the St. Marys River and the Great Lakes. We are pleased to see this investment supporting First Nations led action and look forward to working with our partners to achieve lasting improvements for fish and wildlife in the area.
quotes.speaker: Chief Mark McCoy
quotes.article_title: Minister Dabrusin launches public engagement on Canada’s National Water Security Strategy and announces new projects to protect the Great Lakes from environmental challenges

quotes.quote_text: A healthy Lake Ontario and waterfront support vibrant communities, local economies, recreation and biodiversity across our region. With support from the Canada Water Agency’s Great Lakes Freshwater Ecosystem Initiative, TRCA will continue working with governments, First Nations and Indigenous communities, partners and the public through an integrated land-to-lake approach. Together, we are restoring habitat, improving water quality, and strengthening science and planning to advance progress toward delisting Toronto and Region as an Area of Concern.
quotes.speaker: John MacKenzie
quotes.article_title: Minister Dabrusin launches public engagement on Canada’s National Water Security Strategy and announces new projects to protect the Great Lakes from environmental challenges

Canada and Manitoba renew commitment to Lake Winnipeg as Canada announces over $2.8 million for freshwater projects

quotes.quote_text: Lake Winnipeg is at the heart of our region's identity, environment, and economy. By taking local action, we are making a difference. Collectively, the projects that we are funding bring together governments, Indigenous partners, researchers, and communities to take meaningful action for cleaner water and healthier ecosystems. These investments will help protect Lake Winnipeg for future generations while strengthening local leadership and water stewardship.
quotes.speaker: Terry Duguid
quotes.article_title: MP Duguid highlights launch of public engagement on Canada’s National Water Security Strategy and announces new projects to protect Lake Winnipeg

quotes.quote_text: Here in Winnipeg, the water in our rivers flows north into Lake Winnipeg, so caring for the lake begins close to home. I am proud that this investment backs the First Nations and Métis communities leading water stewardship across the basin and brings governments and partners together to give this lake the protection it has long needed.
quotes.speaker: Ginette Lavack
quotes.article_title: MP Duguid highlights launch of public engagement on Canada’s National Water Security Strategy and announces new projects to protect Lake Winnipeg

quotes.quote_text: Lake Winnipeg is one of Manitoba's most important natural resources, and protecting it takes all of us working together. This agreement strengthens the partnership between Manitoba and Canada and will help us continue the important work of protecting the lake and the communities that depend on it. We are proud to be working with our federal partners to keep Lake Winnipeg healthy for generations to come.
quotes.speaker: Mike Moyes
quotes.article_title: MP Duguid highlights launch of public engagement on Canada’s National Water Security Strategy and announces new projects to protect Lake Winnipeg

quotes.quote_text: Lake Winnipeg has always been central to the Red River Métis way of life. For generations, our Citizens have lived, harvested, travelled, and built their livelihoods along these waters, creating a relationship and responsibility that continues today. As the National Government of the Red River Métis, the Manitoba Métis Federation is committed to ensuring our Citizens, our knowledge, and our priorities shape the future of freshwater management across our National Homeland. These investments are an important step toward healthier waters and stronger water security, and we will continue to work with Canada and Manitoba as government partners to protect Lake Winnipeg and the waters our families will depend on for generations to come.
quotes.speaker: Minister David Beaudin
quotes.article_title: MP Duguid highlights launch of public engagement on Canada’s National Water Security Strategy and announces new projects to protect Lake Winnipeg

quotes.quote_text: We know that affordability is the single most pressing issue for far too many Canadians. That’s why our government is focused on helping Canadians keep more of their hard-earned money. The extension of the pause on the federal fuel tax will provide a boost to household budgets as Canadians feel the effects of global economic uncertainty.
quotes.speaker: Sean Casey
quotes.article_title: The Government of Canada extends the federal fuel excise tax relief on gasoline, diesel, and aviation fuels for Canadians

quotes.quote_text: With many families still feeling the pressure of higher costs, we’re extending the federal fuel tax suspension to keep more money in Canadians’ pockets. This will provide meaningful relief for families and businesses and help make everyday life more affordable.
quotes.speaker: François-Philippe Champagne
quotes.article_title: The Government of Canada extends the federal fuel excise tax relief on gasoline, diesel, and aviation fuels for Canadians

quotes.quote_text: Canadians have made it clear that they want a regulatory system that is more efficient and predictable, without compromising environmental protections or Indigenous rights. The feedback received will guide our next steps in accelerating nati on-buil ding projects and positioning Canada as a stronger, more sovereign, and more prosperous nation.
quotes.speaker: Dominic LeBlanc
quotes.speaker_title: President, U.S., Trade, Internal Trade and One Canadian Economy
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada releases What We Heard reports on proposed reforms on major projects, trade and transportation, and labour relations

quotes.quote_text: Canada’s trade corridors connect Canadian businesses to markets and supply chains at home and around the world. We heard directly from Indigenous Peoples, the transportation industry, and Canadians about what is needed to build stronger, more efficient and more resilient supply chains. We are taking action to reduce red tape, strengthen supply chains, accelerate infrastructure development and attract the investment needed to grow Canada’s economy and create good jobs.
quotes.speaker: Steven MacKinnon
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada releases What We Heard reports on proposed reforms on major projects, trade and transportation, and labour relations

quotes.quote_text: Across the country, workers, unions, employers and partners told us what they need from a modern labour relations framework. I want to thank all stakeholders who took the time to share their perspectives throughout these consultations. This feedback is invaluable in helping us build federally regulated workplaces that are fair, modern and ready for the economy of tomorrow.
quotes.speaker: Patty Hajdu
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada releases What We Heard reports on proposed reforms on major projects, trade and transportation, and labour relations

quotes.quote_text: Arts and culture organizations bring people together, strengthen local economies and make Toronto a vibrant place to live, work and visit. By investing in the performing arts, we are helping artists share their work and express their creativity, while advancing careers and supporting the organizations that drive Toronto’s cultural economy. In a rapidly changing world, a strong cultural sector is essential to a strong and resilient Canada.
quotes.speaker: Marc Miller
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada invests in four arts and culture organizations in Toronto

quotes.quote_text: As a Member of Parliament for Toronto, I see firsthand how creators and organizations like these bring our city together. They allow people to better understand each other, share stories and experience our rich cultural diversity. This funding will help these organizations, and their creators, continue to inspire audiences, support artists and strengthen the vibrant cultural fabric that makes Toronto such a special place.
quotes.speaker: Karim Bardeesy
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada invests in four arts and culture organizations in Toronto

quotes.quote_text: The Department of Canadian Heritage's support for Queer Voices Canada will help us continue to create connections and creative conversations between queer artists and audiences from across Canada. As queer rights and freedoms are threatened the world around, this critical investment strengthens our ability to uphold queer resistance here in Canada. Buddies in Bad Times, as an institution and a nexus for queer expression, plays a fundamental role in Canada's unique cultural ecology and expresses our values on the global stage. We thank the Government of Canada for helping us continue to foster the transgressive, sexy and provocative work of queer Canadian artists.
quotes.speaker: ted witzel
quotes.speaker_title: Artistic Director, Buddies in Bad Times Theatre
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada invests in four arts and culture organizations in Toronto

quotes.quote_text: This investment will help us further expand opportunities for Asian diasporic dance artists and bring their work to audiences across Canada. It supports our commitment to showcasing diverse artistic perspectives and creating meaningful platforms for cultural exchanges and creative collaboration. We have been able to meaningfully create platforms in Toronto, Montreal and more recently Vancouver, and we are working to expand our reach. We are very grateful for the recognition of the value of what we do and for whom. With this support, we will be able to continue to strengthen the visibility and impact of Asian diasporic artists across Canada.
quotes.speaker: Angie Cheng
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada invests in four arts and culture organizations in Toronto

quotes.quote_text: Support for Weesageechak Begins to Dance will help us continue nurturing Indigenous artists and advancing Indigenous storytelling on stage. This funding allows Native Earth to provide artists from Turtle Island and beyond with the time, resources and support they need to develop their work and share it with audiences.
quotes.speaker: Himanshu Sitlani
quotes.speaker_title: Managing Director, Native Earth Performing Arts
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada invests in four arts and culture organizations in Toronto

quotes.quote_text: This funding will help us bring high-quality professional theatre experiences to children and families across the Greater Toronto Area and beyond. Through stories that spark imagination, empathy and curiosity, we aim to inspire young people and contribute to a world where coming generations are more curious, confident and collaborative. This investment supports our mission to make theatre accessible and meaningful for the next generation.
quotes.speaker: Camilla Holland
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada invests in four arts and culture organizations in Toronto

quotes.quote_text: The Build Communities Strong Fund is building the infrastructure that Canadians rely on every day. Today’s investment in local community infrastructure in Coquitlam will help create a new hub for recreation, learning and community connection, while providing much-needed amenities for the growing Burke Mountain community and residents across Coquitlam.
quotes.speaker: Ron McKinnon
quotes.article_title: Building Canada strong by investing in the Burke Mountain Community Centre

quotes.quote_text: Every community deserves spaces where people of all ages and abilities feel welcome and connected. This investment will help Coquitlam create an inclusive community centre where residents can come together, stay active, access programs and services, and connect with their neighbours. With a new library branch located within the centre, the facility will also provide more opportunities for residents to learn, gather and access resources—all in one welcoming, accessible space.
quotes.speaker: Zoe Royer
quotes.article_title: Building Canada strong by investing in the Burke Mountain Community Centre

quotes.quote_text: This is a long-term investment in the future of Burke Mountain and the growing needs of its residents. By supporting a modern, accessible and sustainable community centre, we are helping ensure families, seniors, youth and residents of all abilities have access to spaces where they can stay active, connect and participate in their community. This investment will help build a stronger, more inclusive community for years to come.
quotes.speaker: Jake Sawatzky
quotes.article_title: Building Canada strong by investing in the Burke Mountain Community Centre

quotes.quote_text: This community centre will give people more opportunities for recreation, connection and access to services as our community continues to grow. This spring, our government announced $10 million to help advance this project forward, and today's federal investment builds on that commitment. It's encouraging to see all levels of government working together to deliver the services and amenities families need, now and into the future.
quotes.speaker: Jodie Wickens
quotes.article_title: Building Canada strong by investing in the Burke Mountain Community Centre

quotes.quote_text: Burke Mountain Community Centre has been thoughtfully planned and designed to become the social and recreational hub of this growing neighbourhood. With spaces for swimming, sports, fitness, play and community gatherings – surrounded by incredible views – it will be a place where residents can connect and create memories for generations to come. We are grateful for this federal investment, which will help Coquitlam deliver the infrastructure and amenities our growing community needs. Council remains committed to working with all levels of government to build a vibrant and livable community for Coquitlam residents and families.
quotes.speaker: Richard Stewart
quotes.article_title: Building Canada strong by investing in the Burke Mountain Community Centre

quotes.quote_text: We promised Canadians we would leverage our abundant energy resources to be an energy superpower — and that we would do it in an environmentally responsible way that we could be proud of. Projects like the Origins CCS Hub are doing exactly that: strengthening Canada’s energy sector, creating jobs and attracting investment, all while growing our way to net zero by 2050. The federal and provincial governments and industry are working together as one Team Canada to build big things in this country again and to make sure every Canadian benefits from a stronger, cleaner, more competitive economy.
quotes.speaker: Tim Hodgson
quotes.article_title: Building our way to net zero: Canada breaks ground on nation’s largest carbon capture and storage project

quotes.quote_text: Alberta is a global leader in carbon capture and storage technology, thanks to our geology, expertise and investment environment. The Enhance Energy Hub will help ensure Alberta produces the most responsible oil and gas in the world while creating investment and jobs in rural Alberta. This project will play a key role in driving our economy forward.
quotes.speaker: Brian Jean
quotes.speaker_title: Alberta Minister of Energy and Minerals
quotes.article_title: Building our way to net zero: Canada breaks ground on nation’s largest carbon capture and storage project

quotes.quote_text: Origins builds on Enhance’s demonstrated expertise in the safe, permanent storage of carbon emissions. By providing foundational carbon management infrastructure, the Origins CCS hub will help industries reduce emissions while continuing to produce the energy and commodities that Canada and the world rely on. We are proud this project demonstrates how Alberta and Canada can lead in both economic growth and emissions reduction, and that CCS is a right-now technology that can deliver both.
quotes.speaker: Candice PatonVice
quotes.article_title: Building our way to net zero: Canada breaks ground on nation’s largest carbon capture and storage project

quotes.quote_text: Every young person deserves the opportunity to thrive. Through this investment in REACH Edmonton, we are helping youth access positive mentorship, develop important life skills, and strengthen their connections to their communities. By creating pathways to support and opportunity, we are helping build safer neighbourhoods and brighter futures. Investments in long-term prevention, such as housing, mental health supports, and youth programs like this one, are essential to building a safer, stronger Canada.
quotes.speaker: Sean Fraser
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada invests in youth crime prevention in Edmonton

quotes.quote_text: This funding will allow REACH Edmonton and our community partners to deliver an innovative and holistic approach that combines non-contact boxing and physical activity with life-skills development, trauma-informed support and access to specialized services. Through Empire Fighting Chance: The Guardians of Tomorrow , young people will have opportunities to build confidence, strengthen healthy relationships and coping skills, and make positive choices that support safer, healthier futures.
quotes.speaker: Jan Fox
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada invests in youth crime prevention in Edmonton

quotes.quote_text: Extending the pause on the federal fuel tax is one practical way our government is helping families, farmers, and businesses keep more of their hard-earned money — and we know it works. When the pause took effect in April, gas prices dropped 11 cents a litre on the very first day. Extending that relief means lower costs at the pump and more breathing room for Canadians at a time of global economic uncertainty.
quotes.speaker: Buckley Belanger
quotes.dept_en: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
quotes.article_title: Secretary of State Belanger highlights extension of federal fuel tax relief

quotes.quote_text: With many families still feeling the pressure of higher costs, we’re extending the federal fuel tax suspension to keep more money in Canadians’ pockets. This will provide meaningful relief for families and businesses and help make everyday life more affordable.
quotes.speaker: François-Philippe Champagne
quotes.dept_en: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
quotes.article_title: Secretary of State Belanger highlights extension of federal fuel tax relief

quotes.quote_text: Municipal vehicles keep our roads safe, clear snow and support the essential services residents rely on every day. Lowering the cost of fueling these vehicles helps municipalities manage their operating expenses and limit the pressure on local property taxpayers.
quotes.speaker: Tim Louis
quotes.speaker_title: Member, d Stat, es (U.S.) Trade, Internal Trade and One Canadian Economy
quotes.article_title: Parliamentary Secretary Louis highlights the extension of the federal fuel excise tax relief on gasoline, diesel, and aviation fuels for Canadians

quotes.quote_text: With many families still feeling the pressure of higher costs, we’re extending the federal fuel tax suspension to keep more money in Canadians’ pockets. This will provide meaningful relief for families and businesses and help make everyday life more affordable.
quotes.speaker: François-Philippe Champagne
quotes.article_title: Parliamentary Secretary Louis highlights the extension of the federal fuel excise tax relief on gasoline, diesel, and aviation fuels for Canadians

quotes.quote_text: Behind every major construction project is a skilled worker who started as an apprentice. This funding will help young tradespeople develop in-demand skills and gain the hands-on experience needed for successful, well-paying careers.
quotes.speaker: John Zerucelli
quotes.article_title: Secretary of State Zerucelli highlights funding to support Edmonton’s skilled trades workforce

quotes.quote_text: The federal government's ongoing support continues to have real and meaningful impacts on the future of the skilled trades in Canada. This new equipment will expand our ability to prepare a safe, skilled union workforce to meet the growing needs of industry and allow our union to properly skill up the next generation of talented crane operators who are building Canada strong.
quotes.speaker: Chris Flett
quotes.speaker_title: IUOE 955 Business Manager and IUOE International Trustee
quotes.article_title: Secretary of State Zerucelli highlights funding to support Edmonton’s skilled trades workforce

quotes.quote_text: Canada’s economy thrives when we build major projects and modernize our supply chains. These changes are a critical step toward creating a regulatory system that supports investment and remains committed to meaningful engagement with Indigenous Peoples, and working collaboratively with provinces, territories, industry, stakeholders, and Canadians as we advance our plan to build a stronger, more competitive, and more resilient economy.
quotes.speaker: Dominic LeBlanc
quotes.speaker_title: President, U.S., Trade, Internal Trade and One Canadian Economy
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada Streamlines Project Assessments to strengthen one Canadian economy

quotes.quote_text: Protecting our environment and upholding the rights of Indigenous peoples are at the heart of every impact assessment we undertake. As Canada builds, our government will continue to deliver the rigorous review and meaningful consultation that Canadians count on.
quotes.speaker: Julie Dabrusin
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada Streamlines Project Assessments to strengthen one Canadian economy

quotes.quote_text: Canada has what the world wants, and we need to get those products to domestic and international markets, faster. These changes will create a more efficient and predictable regulatory system for major projects, reducing duplication while maintaining strong environmental protections and respect for Indigenous rights. To make it easier to build major projects, we’re not lowering standards, but raising competence – so we can catalyze investment, unlock our abundant resource vase, create good jobs for Canadians and strengthen Canada's economy at a time when economic competitiveness matters more than ever.
quotes.speaker: Tim Hodgson
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada Streamlines Project Assessments to strengthen one Canadian economy

quotes.quote_text: When children have access to healthy food at school, they can learn, grow and reach their full potential. In partnership with the Government of Alberta, Canada’s National School Food Program is investing in more nutritious meals that are reaching more children across the province while bringing down costs for Alberta families this school year.
quotes.speaker: Anna Gainey
quotes.article_title: National School Food Program helps students and families in Alberta as a new school year begins

quotes.quote_text: No child should have to learn on an empty stomach. Alberta is investing nearly $20 million in the provincial school food program and, together with our federal partners, is reaching more students with the nutritious meals they need to succeed in the classroom.
quotes.speaker: Demetrios Nicolaides
quotes.speaker_title: Alberta’s Minister of Education and Childcare
quotes.article_title: National School Food Program helps students and families in Alberta as a new school year begins

quotes.quote_text: How our children and young people are affected by emerging technologies is an ever-growing concern. Parents, experts and governments all have a role to play in keeping our kids safe. As we put greater responsibility on platforms to make their services safer by design, we thank partners like Children’s Healthcare Canada for conducting critical research that will help inform our policies and better support the mental health and well-being of young Canadians.
quotes.speaker: Marc Miller
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada invests in youth online safety and well-being

quotes.quote_text: Digital environments are an increasingly important part of children’s lives, yet we still have much to learn about what they mean for their health and well-being. Funded by the Digital Citizen Program at Heritage Canada, Children’s Healthcare Canada Mind Over Media Project will bring together evidence and expertise from across the children’s healthcare community to better understand these impacts. This in turn will help inform policies that focus on the health and well-being of children, aligning with our mission to improve experiences and outcomes of care for children and youth in Canada.
quotes.speaker: Emily Gruenwoldt
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada invests in youth online safety and well-being

quotes.quote_text: Canada helped create modern AI. Now we are making sure Canadians have the knowledge and confidence to shape what comes next. AI literacy gives people the practical skills to benefit from these technologies, understand their risks and decide where AI belongs in their lives. Through AI for All, we are making that opportunity available to students, educators, workers and communities across the country.
quotes.speaker: Evan Solomon
quotes.dept_en: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada launches National AI Literacy Initiative

quotes.quote_text: As artificial intelligence continues to reshape the world of work, Canadians need the skills and opportunities to succeed. Through the National AI Literacy Initiative and the Job Bank Training Finder, we are helping people build new skills, explore career opportunities and prepare for the jobs of tomorrow. By helping Canadians adapt and grow in a changing economy, we are making sure more people can take advantage of the opportunities ahead.
quotes.speaker: Patty Hajdu
quotes.dept_en: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada launches National AI Literacy Initiative

quotes.quote_text: Amii is one of Edmonton’s great success stories. As one of Canada’s three national AI institutes, Amii has shown how world-class research can be translated into practical knowledge and opportunity. Through this new $13 million national partnership, we are taking expertise built here in Edmonton and helping one million post-secondary students, more than 50,000 educators, and workers and Canadians across the country understand AI, use it responsibly and share in the opportunities it creates.
quotes.speaker: Eleanor Olszewski
quotes.dept_en: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada launches National AI Literacy Initiative

quotes.quote_text: This national mandate is a profound validation of Amii’s proven track record in AI literacy, and we are deeply proud to answer this call—grounded firmly in our dedicated work in AI excellence as a national AI institute. By delivering free, world-class AI learning to post-secondary institutions, educational spaces and communities nationwide, we are demystifying technology and empowering all Canadians at every age, creating a generational impact on their ability to navigate an evolving digital world with confidence and trust.
quotes.speaker: Cam Linke
quotes.dept_en: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada launches National AI Literacy Initiative

quotes.quote_text: Projects like Sing, Smile, Connect are helping seniors remain engaged, active and connected to their communities. I am proud to work in partnership with organizations like the Heartbeat Society, to strengthen inclusive and supportive environments where older adults can thrive and enjoy a better quality of life.
quotes.speaker: Stephanie McLean
quotes.article_title: Secretary of State McLean announces funding for Alberta seniors

quotes.quote_text: The Heartbeat Society is incredibly grateful to the Government of Canada for its support through the New Horizons for Seniors Program. This funding allows us to bring the joy and healing power of singing, songs, and music to seniors in memory care, supporting their mental and emotional well-being in a truly meaningful way. Music has a remarkable ability to reach places that words sometimes cannot. It can awaken memories, stir emotions, and reconnect people with moments, relationships, and feelings they may have thought were forgotten. We are deeply thankful for the opportunity to make these meaningful experiences possible.
quotes.speaker: (Sgt Ret’d) Gary Benoit
