This agreement is a compelling example of how Canada is deepening partnerships with like-minded allies to protect Canadians and contribute to a safer and more secure world.
quotes.speaker: Stephen Fuhr
quotes.article_title: Canada and Germany sign General Security of Information Agreement

quotes.quote_text: When the federal government invests in active transportation infrastructure, like this multi-use path in Bridgewater, we’re increasing transportation options and contributing to healthy and active communities. Active transportation infrastructure allows people to get their daily exercise on the way to work or school, while reducing our carbon footprint and traffic congestion.
quotes.speaker: Jessica Fancy
quotes.article_title: Federal government improves safety for pedestrians and cyclists in Bridgewater

quotes.quote_text: When the bridge was damaged in 2023 , it created challenges for our residents who rely on this important route every day. Thanks to this new funding, when the full bridge is replaced, it will be safer and more accessible for pedestrians and cyclists, and better suit the needs of our community.
quotes.speaker: David Mitchell
quotes.article_title: Federal government improves safety for pedestrians and cyclists in Bridgewater

quotes.quote_text: AI is changing the way we work and creating new opportunities across our economy. We want young Canadians to have the skills and real-world experience they need to seize those opportunities. By creating 10,000 AI-related work placements through Mitacs, we are investing in Canadian talent while helping businesses adopt AI, boost productivity and compete. This is how we make sure the opportunities created by AI translate into good jobs and a stronger economy for Canadians.
quotes.speaker: Evan Solomon
quotes.dept_en: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada invests in 10,000 AI-related work placements for young Canadians

quotes.quote_text: Through Mitacs AI Advantage, we’re embedding young, highly skilled Canadians directly into businesses, giving them real-world work experience with responsible AI, while helping our small and medium-sized enterprises adopt AI, innovate and compete with confidence. This is how we build the workforce of the future and a stronger Canadian economy.
quotes.speaker: Dr. Stephen Lucas
quotes.dept_en: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada invests in 10,000 AI-related work placements for young Canadians

quotes.quote_text: The Build Communities Strong Fund is building infrastructure at a speed and scale not seen in generations. By partnering with New Brunswick, we are building stronger, safer, more connected communities for all New Brunswickers.
quotes.speaker: Gregor Robertson
quotes.article_title: Canada and New Brunswick partner to build communities strong and invest in healthcare infrastructure

quotes.quote_text: This agreement marks an important step forward in building the infrastructure New Brunswick needs to meet the needs of tomorrow. Canada and New Brunswick are making strategic investments that will help unlock new housing, strengthen post-secondary education and support modern, reliable health infrastructure. By investing in the expansion and modernisation of the Dr. Georges-L.-Dumont University Hospital, we are helping build a stronger health care system that New Brunswickers can rely on for years to come.
quotes.speaker: Dominic LeBlanc
quotes.speaker_title: President, Internal Trade and One Canadian Economy
quotes.article_title: Canada and New Brunswick partner to build communities strong and invest in healthcare infrastructure

quotes.quote_text: New Brunswickers deserve to get the right care, in the right place, when they need it, and that means making sure our health-care teams have the facilities and equipment they need to provide that care. This investment will help us expand and modernize health-care infrastructure, including at Georges-L.-Dumont, while creating more opportunities to build affordable housing. By working with our federal partners, we are building the capacity we need to deliver better care closer to home and make life more affordable for New Brunswickers.
quotes.speaker: Susan Holt
quotes.article_title: Canada and New Brunswick partner to build communities strong and invest in healthcare infrastructure

quotes.quote_text: Thanks to this partnership between Canada and New Brunswick, the investments being announced today will have a meaningful impact for people in Greater Moncton and communities across southeastern New Brunswick. By supporting the modernization of Dr. Georges-L.-Dumont University Hospital, we are helping ensure patients have access to high-quality care while increasing the capacity to meet the needs of our growing communities.
quotes.speaker: Ginette Petitpas Taylor
quotes.article_title: Canada and New Brunswick partner to build communities strong and invest in healthcare infrastructure

quotes.quote_text: Investing in modern health-care infrastructure is an important part of improving the care New Brunswickers receive. This funding will allow us to upgrade and expand health-care facilities across the province so our health-care professionals have the spaces and equipment they need to provide high-quality care.
quotes.speaker: John Dornan
quotes.article_title: Canada and New Brunswick partner to build communities strong and invest in healthcare infrastructure

quotes.quote_text: Today’s announcement is good news for communities right across the province. By partnering with the federal government through the Build Communities Strong Fund, the province can continue to invest in essential municipal infrastructure, promote housing development, and support the needs of New Brunswick residents now and in the future.
quotes.speaker: Gilles LePage
quotes.article_title: Canada and New Brunswick partner to build communities strong and invest in healthcare infrastructure

quotes.quote_text: The Dr. Georges-L.-Dumont University Hospital Centre plays an essential role in the delivery of specialized care in New Brunswick and in training the next generation of health-care professionals. We are pleased with the commitment of the provincial and federal governments to invest in its modernization. These investments will support the transformation of our infrastructure to improve care environments, increase our capacity, and better meet the growing needs of the population.
quotes.speaker: Dr. France Desrosiers
quotes.article_title: Canada and New Brunswick partner to build communities strong and invest in healthcare infrastructure

quotes.quote_text: Northern Ontario is full of talented artists, creators and storytellers who deserve the opportunity to build successful careers close to home. Through music, film and television, artists help strengthen communities and build the connections that unite us as Canadians. This investment will help more creators share their talents, create new opportunities across the region and contribute to a stronger, more connected Canada.
quotes.speaker: Patty Hajdu
quotes.dept_en: Federal Economic Development Agency for Northern Ontario - FedNor
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada invests over $850,000 to strengthen and grow Northern Ontario’s music, film and television industries

quotes.quote_text: Today’s announcement will help take our music, film and television industry to the next level by making it easier to produce content here in Sudbury and across Northern Ontario. Our region at home an abundance of artists, crew and emerging talent that can help any production thrive. With more than 400 film and television projects filmed across Northern Ontario, this key industry has become a major driving force for our economy. This includes over $200 million in economic activity for Greater Sudbury alone.
quotes.speaker: Viviane Lapointe
quotes.dept_en: Federal Economic Development Agency for Northern Ontario - FedNor
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada invests over $850,000 to strengthen and grow Northern Ontario’s music, film and television industries

quotes.quote_text: Thanks to FedNor’s continued support, the impact of Northern Ontario’s music, film and television industries now reaches far beyond our region. Our artists, stories and productions are finding audiences around the world, while generating meaningful careers and business opportunities here at home. This investment will allow CION to build on that momentum by attracting new productions, developing our workforce, supporting emerging talent and creating new opportunities for Northern Ontario’s creative industries to compete on a global stage.
quotes.speaker: Patrick O’Hearn
quotes.dept_en: Federal Economic Development Agency for Northern Ontario - FedNor
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada invests over $850,000 to strengthen and grow Northern Ontario’s music, film and television industries

quotes.quote_text: We’re strengthening Canada’s sport system by ensuring that much-needed resources get to National Sport Organizations quickly so they can put them in motion. For Cycling Canada, this means increased support for athletes, coaches and programs that help Canadians participate and excel in sport. As we welcome the world to Montréal for the 2026 UCI Road World Championships, we’re proving once again that Canada is the best sport-hosting nation, while supporting our athletes and inspiring the next generation.
quotes.speaker: Adam van Koeverden
quotes.article_title: Secretary of State van Koeverden announces new funding for Cycling Canada at Montréal 2026 UCI Road World Championships

quotes.quote_text: "Secretary of State Adam van Koeverden has been a tremendous champion for Canadian sport. His leadership creates more opportunities for Canadians to experience the power of sport, and this investment will help us inspire more young people to ride, realize their potential and dream of one day proudly representing Canada on the world stage”.
quotes.speaker: Mathieu Boucher
quotes.article_title: Secretary of State van Koeverden announces new funding for Cycling Canada at Montréal 2026 UCI Road World Championships

quotes.quote_text: UNGA has always been a hub for the international community to come together to advance shared prosperity and stability. Canada’s unwavering commitment to strengthening connections and taking collective action on global challenges will create lasting benefits for Canadians and communities worldwide.
quotes.speaker: Randeep Sarai
quotes.article_title: Secretary of State Sarai participates in 81st United Nations General Assembly and announces international assistance funding

quotes.quote_text: Ensuring the safety and security of Canadians at home requires supporting emergency health measures abroad. That is why Health Emergency Readiness Canada is contributing to a multi-agency investment that will assist in combatting the spread of the Ebola virus in Africa. Global health emergencies require global cooperation to resolve, and Canada is proud to contribute to the international effort to eradicate Ebola.
quotes.speaker: Mélanie Joly
quotes.article_title: Secretary of State Sarai participates in 81st United Nations General Assembly and announces international assistance funding

quotes.quote_text: We’re proud to support Nuit Blanche’s immersive nighttime experiences, which celebrate our country’s rich culture and showcase the creativity and innovation of our artists. At a time when we need to come together, arts and culture have the power to bring us closer together, unite us through our shared identity and values, and strengthen our communities.
quotes.speaker: Marc Miller
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada invests in Nuit Blanche Ottawa event

quotes.quote_text: As Member of Parliament for Ottawa–Vanier–Gloucester, I have seen firsthand how this event brings our community together. Part of the celebrations for the 200th anniversary of Ottawa, it sparks meaningful conversations, promotes understanding and celebrates the rich diversity of cultures that makes our city so vibrant. This funding will help ensure this event continues to grow, strengthening Ottawa's dynamic cultural communities.
quotes.speaker: Mona Fortier
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada invests in Nuit Blanche Ottawa event

quotes.quote_text: We are deeply grateful to the Government of Canada, through Canadian Heritage, for its support of Nuit Blanche Ottawa. This investment enables us to deliver an ambitious, accessible and free artistic program while creating new opportunities for connection between artists, communities and audiences in the heart of the nation’s capital. For a new initiative such as ours, this support represents far more than funding; it directly contributes to establishing Nuit Blanche Ottawa as a lasting and unifying cultural event. We are proud to offer residents and visitors meaningful opportunities to engage in contemporary art, celebrate cultural diversity and come together through shared experiences that foster dialogue, inclusion and community.
quotes.speaker: Josee Bertrand
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada invests in Nuit Blanche Ottawa event

quotes.quote_text: At this year’s United Nations General Assembly, Canada worked closely with partners to strengthen international law, advance maritime and Arctic security, support Ukraine, promote a just and lasting peace in the Middle East and address global security challenges. We remain committed to effective international cooperation and to building a safer, more secure and more prosperous world for all.
quotes.speaker: Anita Anand
quotes.article_title: Minister Anand concludes participation in the 81st United Nations General Assembly High-Level Week

quotes.quote_text: Communities across Atlantic Canada need infrastructure that works, today and for the future. This targeted investment will help get federal dollars directly into Dartmouth to build and upgrade the places people rely on every day. Practical investments, like support for the St. George’s Tennis Club will bring people together and ensure residents can enjoy safe, accessible recreation well into the future.
quotes.speaker: Sean Fraser
quotes.article_title: $221,500 in federal funding supports upgrades at St. George’s Tennis Club in Dartmouth

quotes.quote_text: We’re delivering $221,500 to help the non-profit St. George’s Tennis Club resurface its clay courts and revitalize its facility for our community to enjoy. For over 140 years, this historic recreation hub has served Dartmouth residents, and this investment will help ensure it can continue encouraging healthy, active living and bringing people together through sport and recreation for generations to come.
quotes.speaker: Darren Fisher
quotes.article_title: $221,500 in federal funding supports upgrades at St. George’s Tennis Club in Dartmouth

quotes.quote_text: St George’s Tennis Club has been an integral part of Dartmouth’s sport and recreation community for over 140 years. The Club is committed to upgrading the facilities regarding energy efficiency and sustainability as well as improving access so that future generations will be able to benefit from the active lifestyle we promote. This federal contribution will have a significant impact on our “Building on History” renovation project.
quotes.speaker: Susan Ehler
quotes.article_title: $221,500 in federal funding supports upgrades at St. George’s Tennis Club in Dartmouth

quotes.quote_text: Canadians expect grocery stores to be able to advertise their best deals. We’re concerned that policies that prevent this make it harder for grocers to compete, and for consumers to access lower prices. At a time when food affordability remains an important concern for Canadians, we want to hear about how these policies are affecting grocery prices and consumer choice.
quotes.speaker: Jeanne Pratt
quotes.article_title: Competition Bureau concerned that grocery deals are being kept from Canadians

quotes.quote_text: This second round of funding is a significant step forward and builds on a total investment of $581.5 million since our incorporation on the winter solstice of 2022. We are seeing real momentum across the country, with projects moving from concept to construction. This continued investment allows us to scale that impact. When we talk about housing, we’re not just talking about units. We’re talking about security. We’re talking about health. We’re talking about the well-being of families, of individuals, of women, men, and children who need a safe, affordable, and culturally appropriate place to live.
quotes.speaker: Jocelyn Formsma
quotes.article_title: Minister Gull-Masty joins the National Indigenous Collaborative Housing Incorporated to announce renewed Indigenous-led housing initiative

quotes.quote_text: Today, we're proud to announce $300 million that will help advance Indigenous-led housing solutions, making a meaningful difference in the lives of Indigenous Peoples from coast to coast to coast. This investment represents more than funding; it represents keys in the hands of individuals and families. “With this commitment, the Government of Canada has now entrusted NICHI with more than half a billion dollars to support Indigenous housing. That investment reflects the federal government's confidence in NICHI as a national Indigenous housing organization and its belief that a For Indigenous, By Indigenous approach delivers results for communities. “We also recognize Indigenous Services Canada (ISC) for continuing to support NICHI in advancing a For Indigenous, By Indigenous approach to housing. This renewed investment builds on the success of the initial funding and shows what can be achieved when Indigenous organizations are trusted to lead, make decisions and deliver housing solutions that respond to the needs of their communities. “NICHI looks forward to advancing the next generation of Indigenous-led housing across the country.
quotes.speaker: John Gordon
quotes.article_title: Minister Gull-Masty joins the National Indigenous Collaborative Housing Incorporated to announce renewed Indigenous-led housing initiative

quotes.quote_text: A home is more than four walls. It is where families build their lives, where children grow up, and where people should be able to feel safe and secure. This $300 million investment will help more Indigenous Peoples have that foundation. Just as importantly, Indigenous Peoples are leading this work. NICHI’s ‘For Indigenous, By Indigenous’ approach puts decisions about Indigenous housing in the hands of people who know their communities and understand what is needed. That is the kind of partnership we want to continue building.
quotes.speaker: Mandy Gull-Masty
quotes.article_title: Minister Gull-Masty joins the National Indigenous Collaborative Housing Incorporated to announce renewed Indigenous-led housing initiative

quotes.quote_text: Renewed funding to NICHI shows our government’s commitment to supporting self-determination for Indigenous Peoples, who know what’s best for their communities and future generations. ‘For Indigenous, By Indigenous’ paves the way toward improved Indigenous housing outcomes made possible through Indigenous leadership.
quotes.speaker: Yasir Naqvi
quotes.speaker_title: Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister, Member
quotes.article_title: Minister Gull-Masty joins the National Indigenous Collaborative Housing Incorporated to announce renewed Indigenous-led housing initiative

quotes.quote_text: Investing in the Rankin Inlet Airport is an investment in Canada’s North, our Arctic sovereignty, and the communities that depend on reliable transportation every day. Through the Arctic Infrastructure Fund, we are strengthening critical infrastructure that serves both civilian and defence purposes, helping ensure northern transportation networks remain safe, resilient, and dependable well into the future.
quotes.speaker: Steven MacKinnon
quotes.article_title: The Government of Canada invests $85.5 million to rehabilitate the Rankin Inlet Airport and strengthen Arctic and northern connectivity

quotes.quote_text: For people in Rankin Inlet and across the Kivalliq, the airport is more than infrastructure. It connects families and communities and helps people access the food, supplies, services and opportunities they rely on. By investing in safe and reliable transportation in the North, we are strengthening communities and creating new opportunities, while also strengthening Canada's presence and sovereignty in the Arctic. A strong Arctic starts with strong communities and the people who call the North home.
quotes.speaker: Rebecca Chartrand
quotes.article_title: The Government of Canada invests $85.5 million to rehabilitate the Rankin Inlet Airport and strengthen Arctic and northern connectivity

quotes.quote_text: This project is about more than wastewater infrastructure, it’s about creating the capacity for Oromocto to grow and welcome new residents. By investing in essential infrastructure today, we are helping communities prepare for future housing development and ensuring that growth is supported by the services people need.
quotes.speaker: David Myles
quotes.article_title: Canada and New Brunswick invest in wastewater infrastructure to support housing growth in Oromocto

quotes.quote_text: Investing in the infrastructure needed to support housing growth is essential as communities like Oromocto plan for the future. This project will help expand wastewater capacity in Oromocto and support new housing, while strengthening the infrastructure needed to accommodate growth in a community that is home to Canada’s second-largest military base.
quotes.speaker: Gilles LePage
quotes.article_title: Canada and New Brunswick invest in wastewater infrastructure to support housing growth in Oromocto

quotes.quote_text: This funding announcement marks an important milestone for the Town of Oromocto and reflects a shared commitment to building a stronger, more sustainable future. Investing in modern infrastructure is essential to supporting population growth, enabling economic development, and protecting the environment. Through this partnership with the federal and provincial governments, we can undertake critical infrastructure improvements that would otherwise place significant financial pressure on local taxpayers. We are grateful for this investment and for the continued collaboration of our government partners in helping to ensure Oromocto remains a vibrant and resilient community for years to come.
quotes.speaker: Robert Powell
quotes.article_title: Canada and New Brunswick invest in wastewater infrastructure to support housing growth in Oromocto

quotes.quote_text: We were able to provide compensation to eligible producers who reached out to us when they were left unpaid by the buyer. Payment security is available through the Safeguards for Grain Farmers Program and producers are always encouraged to contact us as soon as possible if they are having difficulties receiving payment.
quotes.speaker: David Hunt
quotes.article_title: Canadian Grain Commission compensates eligible producers for unpaid deliveries to Grasslands Brokerage & Consulting Ltd.

quotes.quote_text: Community spaces are where people come together, access important services, learn, stay active and build connections. Investing in local, grassroots infrastructure means residents will live healthier, more connected lives. This funding will help transform Winnipeg’s historic Downtown Y into a more accessible and welcoming space, expanding opportunities for recreation, learning and essential services for people across the community for generations to come.
quotes.speaker: Ben Carr
quotes.article_title: Building Canada strong by investing in the Downtown Y Redevelopment Project

quotes.quote_text: Investments like this demonstrate what can be achieved when governments and community organizations work together toward a shared vision. The redevelopment of the Downtown Y will renew an important community asset, help strengthen Winnipeg’s downtown core, and ensure residents have access to modern spaces that support learning, wellness, and community engagement. This project will benefit Winnipeg families and residents for decades to come.
quotes.speaker: Ginette Lavack
quotes.article_title: Building Canada strong by investing in the Downtown Y Redevelopment Project

quotes.quote_text: Today’s research increasingly shows that purpose-built, safe third spaces don't just help struggling areas; they’re a bellwether of civic health and prosperity. By investing in the renaissance of Winnipeg’s downtown core, the Government of Canada is laying a cornerstone for radical hope, transformative belonging, and economic vitality for our families and businesses long into the future.
quotes.speaker: Cordella Friesen
quotes.article_title: Building Canada strong by investing in the Downtown Y Redevelopment Project

quotes.quote_text: The Kelowna International Airport is already a major economic engine for our region. This investment will unlock valuable airport lands, attract new investment and aerospace companies, and create skilled Canadian jobs. We're strengthening Kelowna's economy while creating new opportunities for Canada's aerospace industry to grow, right here in the Okanagan.
quotes.speaker: Stephen Fuhr
quotes.article_title: Building Canada strong by investing in Economic Enabling Infrastructure at the Kelowna International Airport

quotes.quote_text: Airports are much more than transportation hubs; They are powerful economic engines that connect people, businesses and industries to opportunity. This investment will help unlock new private-sector development, support the growth of Canada's aerospace sector and strengthen YLW's role as a gateway for innovation, trade and investment. We are grateful to the Government of Canada for recognizing the national significance of this opportunity.
quotes.speaker: Sam Samaddar
quotes.article_title: Building Canada strong by investing in Economic Enabling Infrastructure at the Kelowna International Airport

quotes.quote_text: Building a more accessible and inclusive Canada starts with listening to persons with disabilities and ensuring they are active partners in the decisions that affect their lives. By working together and learning from one another, we can continue to break down barriers and create more opportunities for people to reach their full potential.
quotes.speaker: Patty Hajdu
quotes.article_title: Minister Hajdu meets with Italian counterpart and stakeholders to highlight international collaboration to advance disability inclusion

quotes.quote_text: Meaningful progress on accessibility happens when governments, researchers, organizations and persons with disabilities come together to share experiences and solutions. Today’s discussion demonstrated the value of international collaboration in advancing inclusion and upholding the rights of persons with disabilities. By learning from one another and working in partnership, we can help build communities where everyone can fully participate.
quotes.speaker: Leslie Church
quotes.article_title: Minister Hajdu meets with Italian counterpart and stakeholders to highlight international collaboration to advance disability inclusion

quotes.quote_text: Cooperation is essential to advancing accessibility, inclusion and the rights of persons with disabilities. Today’s dialogue with our Canadian partners highlighted the importance of sharing experiences, knowledge and solutions to break down barriers and promote full participation. The Solfagnano Charter and the UN Convention on the Rights of Persons with Disabilities provide a strong foundation for our shared commitment to building more inclusive and accessible societies, where everyone can participate fully and contribute to its community.
quotes.speaker: Alessandra Locatelli
quotes.article_title: Minister Hajdu meets with Italian counterpart and stakeholders to highlight international collaboration to advance disability inclusion

quotes.quote_text: I'm delighted to welcome Crystal Lennie to the Canadian Institutes of Health Research Governing Council. Ms. Lennie brings a valuable perspective based on her community health and advocacy work for the people of the North, helping to ensure health research in Canada reflects the needs of the people and communities it serves.
quotes.speaker: Marjorie Michel
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada announces appointment of Crystal Lennie to the Canadian Institutes of Health Research Governing Council

quotes.quote_text: Climate change is already impacting Canadians’ safety and security, and it will continue to drive up costs. Through events like Adaptation Canada 2026, experts can explore actions and share solutions aimed at strengthening our climate resilience. By investing in the critical infrastructure needed to protect our communities and businesses from climate impacts, we are building a stronger, more resilient Canadian economy while raising awareness of the potential risks climate change poses to every region and sector across the country. By coming together, we can make more informed decisions, safeguard Canadians, and help ensure a sustainable future for generations to come.
quotes.speaker: Julie Dabrusin
quotes.article_title: Federal Government Advances Climate Resilience at 2026 Adaptation Canada Conference

quotes.quote_text: Canada's response to extreme weather doesn’t have to be a trade-off between public safety and economic growth. Every dollar spent on protecting people, infrastructure, and ecosystems today saves up to fifteen dollars in avoided damages and recovery costs in the future. Adaptation Canada is the premier platform to bring together governments, Indigenous partners, and practitioners to infuse climate resiliency in all major decisions so that we’re serving Canadians not only today, but 100 years from now.
quotes.speaker: Shannon Miedema
quotes.article_title: Federal Government Advances Climate Resilience at 2026 Adaptation Canada Conference

quotes.quote_text: Canada has the climate information, expertise, and experience needed to make real progress on adaptation. The challenge now is turning that knowledge into decisions that shape communities every day. That means bringing together the people doing the work across sectors and regions to share what is working, learn from one another, and move from evidence to action. Adaptation Canada 2026 is a chance to build those connections and accelerate the shift from understanding climate risk to implementing solutions.
quotes.speaker: Ewa Jackson
quotes.article_title: Federal Government Advances Climate Resilience at 2026 Adaptation Canada Conference

quotes.quote_text: Across Ontario, there is a need for critical infrastructure and housing of all types to support our fast-growing communities. This is why our government continues to deliver programs like the Development Charge Reduction Program alongside our federal partners, which helps provide cities like Barrie with the funding they need to ensure their community remains a desirable place to live, work and raise a family.
quotes.speaker: Rob Flack
quotes.article_title: Canada and Ontario Making Homes More Affordable in Barrie

quotes.quote_text: Building more homes requires strong partnerships and investments that make it easier and more affordable to build. Through the Development Charge Reduction Program, we are working with Ontario and the City of Barrie to reduce the cost of new housing while supporting the infrastructure needed to build complete, thriving communities. This investment will help make homebuilding more affordable for families in Barrie and support Ontario’s growing economy.
quotes.speaker: Jennifer McKelvie
quotes.article_title: Canada and Ontario Making Homes More Affordable in Barrie

quotes.quote_text: This is a game changer for Barrie and will give more Barrie residents an opportunity to own a home,” said Alex Nuttall, Mayor of the City of Barrie. “By reducing the cost of building new homes, we are making housing more attainable while creating more opportunities for the skilled tradespeople and local businesses who build our community. I want to thank the Ontario government for their continued partnership with the City of Barrie. This is what leadership looks like: working together to build more homes, support our trades and create opportunity for Barrie residents.
quotes.speaker: Alex Nuttall
quotes.article_title: Canada and Ontario Making Homes More Affordable in Barrie

quotes.quote_text: Barrie is growing, and we want to make sure that growth comes with more opportunities for families to find a place they can call home. By eliminating development charges on residential development, the City of Barrie is taking meaningful action to help reduce the upfront cost of building new homes. Our government is proud to recognize that commitment with up to $129 million through the Development Charge Reduction Program, helping support more housing and a stronger future for Barrie.
quotes.speaker: Doug Downey
quotes.article_title: Canada and Ontario Making Homes More Affordable in Barrie

quotes.quote_text: Today’s announcement is great news for the City of Barrie, and for the families hoping to call it home. Reducing development charges is about more than just lowering construction costs. It’s about making it possible to get more homes built, at prices more families can afford. OHBA has been clear that reducing the cost of delivering new homes will take meaningful action; the DCRP program does that.
quotes.speaker: Scott Andison
quotes.article_title: Canada and Ontario Making Homes More Affordable in Barrie

quotes.quote_text: RESCON commends Minister of Municipal Affairs and Housing Rob Flack as he continues to work to reduce municipal development charges and to make housing more affordable for Ontarians. Reducing DC costs in Ontario municipalities is a major step towards affordability. Premier Doug Ford and Minister Flack have led the way on development charge reduction and regulatory reform, sales tax relief and approval process changes. RESCON fully supports these efforts by Premier Ford and Minister Flack.
quotes.speaker: Richard Lyall
quotes.article_title: Canada and Ontario Making Homes More Affordable in Barrie

quotes.quote_text: The Building Industry and Land Development Association (BILD) welcomes the announcement today by the Federal and Provincial governments regarding the significant infrastructure investment for the City of Barrie in recognition of the City’s commitment to reduce development charges and the cost to build. Since August of 2025 with the introduction of a DC waiver, and then again this month with a residential development charge reduction of 50 percent, Mayor Nuttall and City Council have been leaders in advancing efforts to accelerate housing supply and economic opportunities! These changes will immediately improve project viability and our members look forward to continuing to get shovels in the ground and welcoming future homeowners to Barrie. We applaud the provincial and federal governments for recognizing that today’s meaningful contribution will support housing supply, local jobs, growth, and new homebuyers!
quotes.speaker: Dave Wilkes
quotes.article_title: Canada and Ontario Making Homes More Affordable in Barrie

quotes.quote_text: Reducing development charges can significantly improve project viability and unlock greater investment in new housing. Programs like this create better conditions for more homes to move forward, including purpose-built rental housing, giving people more choice in where and how they live. We welcome continued collaboration between governments and municipalities such as Barrie to reduce barriers, support growth and help increase housing supply across Ontario.
quotes.speaker: Tony Irwin
quotes.speaker_title: President & CEO, Federation of Rental-housing Providers of Ontario
quotes.article_title: Canada and Ontario Making Homes More Affordable in Barrie

quotes.quote_text: I’m thrilled to see the latest efforts from our federal and provincial governments to reduce development charges across Ontario through the Development Charge Reduction Program. OREA advocated for an initiative just like this in our A Pathway to Development Charge Reform policy report, and we commend our leaders for heeding our calls to bring affordability back within reach. These initiatives will help lower housing construction costs, get more homes built, and deliver the infrastructure necessary to support growing communities.
quotes.speaker: Kim Fairley
quotes.article_title: Canada and Ontario Making Homes More Affordable in Barrie

quotes.quote_text: Housing starts with infrastructure, and tackling Ontario's housing challenge requires all orders of government to work together. Investments through the DCRP will help communities build the critical infrastructure that enables growth, giving homebuilders the certainty and support they need to deliver the homes families in Ontario are counting on. We encourage municipalities across the province to take advantage of this opportunity and join us in building more homes, faster.
quotes.speaker: Brad Carr
quotes.article_title: Canada and Ontario Making Homes More Affordable in Barrie

quotes.quote_text: High-speed rail has great potential to reshape the way people move in Canada, and supports Alberta's economic growth, productivity, and regional connectivity. Today's collaboration demonstrates our shared commitment to exploring opportunities that could deliver lasting benefits for Albertans and Canadians.
quotes.speaker: Steven MacKinnon
quotes.article_title: Canada and Alberta to collaborate on High-Speed Rail

quotes.quote_text: Connecting Calgary, Red Deer and Edmonton with high-speed rail would be a generational investment in Alberta’s future. As our province continues to grow, we need to build the infrastructure that keeps people, businesses and our economy moving. By working with the federal government, we are taking the next steps toward a project that could strengthen one of Canada’s fastest-growing economic corridors and support Alberta’s growth for decades to come.
quotes.speaker: Danielle Smith
quotes.article_title: Canada and Alberta to collaborate on High-Speed Rail

quotes.quote_text: Building a stronger Canada means building big, and that means working together to deliver the infrastructure Canadians need to connect communities, grow our economy and create good jobs. By bringing the federal and provincial governments together, along with the expertise of the Major Projects Office, we will explore how we can turn this opportunity into a transformative project for Alberta and for Canada. This is what building a strong, connected and prosperous Canada looks like—working together to get big things built.
quotes.speaker: Dominic LeBlanc
quotes.article_title: Canada and Alberta to collaborate on High-Speed Rail

quotes.quote_text: This is what it means to dream big and work together. High-speed rail between Edmonton and Calgary would create incredible new job and business opportunities for Albertans while transforming Canada's third-largest transportation corridor. It would connect our communities and bring our friends and family closer together. Today's announcement reflects our shared commitment to deliver lasting benefits for Albertans, that also contribute to Canada's long-term prosperity.
quotes.speaker: Eleanor Olszewski
quotes.article_title: Canada and Alberta to collaborate on High-Speed Rail

quotes.quote_text: Throughout the development of Alberta’s Passenger Rail Master Plan, we heard that a high-speed passenger rail connection between Calgary and Edmonton via Red Deer is a priority for Albertans. We are excited to move forward with this project which will transform the way Albertans travel.
quotes.speaker: Devin Dreeshen
quotes.speaker_title: Alberta Minister of Transportation and Economic Corridors
quotes.article_title: Canada and Alberta to collaborate on High-Speed Rail

quotes.quote_text: Communities across the Northwest Territories know that building more homes starts with having the right infrastructure in place. That’s why our government is investing more than $44.9 million through the Canada Housing Infrastructure Fund infrastructure that will enable the construction of more homes in communities across the Northwest Territories, from Ulukhaktok to Fort Smith and everywhere in between.
quotes.speaker: Rebecca Alty
quotes.article_title: Canada and the Government of the Northwest Territories invest in housing-enabling infrastructure across the territory

quotes.quote_text: Access to reliable water, wastewater and solid waste infrastructure is essential to supporting housing development and building healthy, sustainable communities. Through the Canada Housing Infrastructure Fund, the GNWT is partnering with communities across the Northwest Territories to invest in critical infrastructure that will help unlock new housing opportunities, preserve existing homes and strengthen community resilience for years to come.
quotes.speaker: Vince McKay
quotes.article_title: Canada and the Government of the Northwest Territories invest in housing-enabling infrastructure across the territory

quotes.quote_text: Our community has been waiting for the infrastructure needed to support new homes. Upgrades to our water and waste systems mean more families can have safe, healthy places to live close to home. This funding is an important step forward for Behchokǫ̀, and we are proud to be part of this work alongside our partners.
quotes.speaker: Chief
quotes.article_title: Canada and the Government of the Northwest Territories invest in housing-enabling infrastructure across the territory

quotes.quote_text: Keeping Canadians safe starts with investing in our youth. Today’s investment will help community organizations in Halifax continue to provide vulnerable young people with safe spaces, trusted support networks, and positive opportunities to reach their full potential. By addressing the root causes of crime and supporting prevention efforts at the local level, we are helping youth build brighter futures while creating safer, stronger communities for everyone.
quotes.speaker: Gary Anandasangaree
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada invests in gun violence prevention in Halifax, Nova Scotia

quotes.quote_text: Keeping residents safe is one of our most important responsibilities. The Building Safer Communities Fund has helped us strengthen partnerships, support young people, and build greater community capacity to prevent violence before it happens. This continued investment will allow us to build on that work and focus resources where they can make a real difference in keeping people and our communities safe.
quotes.speaker: Mayor Andy Fillmore
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada invests in gun violence prevention in Halifax, Nova Scotia

quotes.quote_text: Police see firsthand the value of investing in people from an early age. Giving people the support and opportunities they need to build a positive future can help create pathways away from crime and violence and, ultimately, strengthen our communities.
quotes.speaker: Deputy
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada invests in gun violence prevention in Halifax, Nova Scotia

quotes.quote_text: Once again, our government is reaffirming our commitment to Francophone immigration and our recognition of the valuable contributions that every French-speaking and bilingual newcomer makes to Canada. The partnerships and investments made through the Francophone Immigration Support Program are a reflection of our shared commitment to foster the growth of our Francophone minority communities, strengthen their vitality, and help build a more dynamic and vibrant Canadian Francophonie.
quotes.speaker: Lena Metlege Diab
quotes.article_title: Canada is supporting new projects to promote Francophone immigration and strengthen Francophone minority communities

quotes.quote_text: Francophone immigration plays a vital role in strengthening Newfoundland and Labrador's communities, workforce, and economy. Through this funding from the Government of Canada, we are creating new opportunities to attract and retain Francophone and bilingual newcomers who will help address labour market challenges, support population growth, and contribute to the long-term vitality of our province's Francophone communities.
quotes.speaker: Lin Paddock
quotes.speaker_title: Minister, Growth and Rural Development of Newfoundland and Labrador
quotes.article_title: Canada is supporting new projects to promote Francophone immigration and strengthen Francophone minority communities

quotes.quote_text: Funding for the Francophone Immigration Support Program is a key driver to enhance our province’s appeal and economic vitality. It addresses a two-fold challenge—meeting the labour needs of employers in provincial priority sectors and fostering the welcome and integration of Francophone workers. Through the Destination Saskatchewan initiative, our communities will welcome new talent that will directly contribute to the prosperity and visibility of the Francophone community.
quotes.speaker: Kouamé N’Goandi
quotes.speaker_title: Executive Director, Conseil économique et coopératif de la Saskatchewan
quotes.article_title: Canada is supporting new projects to promote Francophone immigration and strengthen Francophone minority communities

quotes.quote_text: Funding for the coordinated promotional ‘ Osez le Nord ’ campaign will bring together all the key players in Francophone immigration in Northern Ontario under a single brand to enhance Northern Ontario’s appeal to Francophone families, workers and students. By highlighting the career opportunities and quality of life in our communities, ‘ Osez le Nord ’ will showcase the unique realities of Northern Ontario in a warm, authentic and engaging tone.
quotes.speaker: Thomas Mercier
quotes.speaker_title: Director, Réseau de soutien à l’immigration francophone du Nord de l’Ontario
quotes.article_title: Canada is supporting new projects to promote Francophone immigration and strengthen Francophone minority communities
