quotes.article_title: Canada and Ontario investing $2 million to protect the province’s agri-food industry

quotes.quote_text: All Canadians want the same thing – a health care system that works. The Government of Canada has invested billions of dollars to help build a sustainable and equitable system. With today’s investment, our governments are demonstrating our commitment to better care, stronger communities and a healthier future for everyone in the Northwest Territories.
quotes.speaker: Marjorie Michel
quotes.article_title: Canada and Northwest Territories partner to improve health infrastructure and access to health care for communities

quotes.quote_text: People across the Northwest Territories deserve health care that reflects the realities of living in the North and the needs of their communities. This renewed investment will support more accessible, culturally appropriate care, while strengthening community-led mental wellness supports and working in partnership with Indigenous Governments and organizations to improve health outcomes across the territory.
quotes.speaker: Rebecca Alty
quotes.article_title: Canada and Northwest Territories partner to improve health infrastructure and access to health care for communities

quotes.quote_text: Improving access to health care in the North and the infrastructure that supports it takes a long-term commitment and a partnership that recognizes the realities of our territory. The Northwest Territories is different from other parts of Canada, and the way we plan, fund and deliver health care needs to reflect that. This agreement is an important step in strengthening that partnership and building a stronger foundation for health care in the territory.
quotes.speaker: R. J. Simpson
quotes.article_title: Canada and Northwest Territories partner to improve health infrastructure and access to health care for communities

quotes.quote_text: Strong health systems depend on both the people who deliver care and the facilities that support them. Through the renewal of the Working Together Bilateral Agreement and investments through the Build Communities Strong Fund, we are strengthening health care across the Northwest Territories. By supporting our workforce, improving access to mental health and substance use services, and investing in community facilities that help residents access care closer to home, we are improving the services residents rely on and supporting healthy people and communities across the territory. By working in partnership with the Government of Canada, Indigenous Governments, and communities, we will continue to strengthen a responsive health system that meets the needs of Northerners.
quotes.speaker: Lucy Kuptana
quotes.article_title: Canada and Northwest Territories partner to improve health infrastructure and access to health care for communities

quotes.quote_text: Building and maintaining infrastructure in the North comes with unique challenges, particularly in our smaller and more remote communities. These investments will help ensure communities have safe, modern and appropriate facilities to support the delivery of health and social services close to home. Good infrastructure is essential to strong communities, and these projects will make a meaningful difference for residents while providing health and social services professionals with better facilities to do their important work. We are pleased to work with the Government of Canada, Indigenous Governments and communities to move these projects forward and strengthen infrastructure across the Northwest Territories.
quotes.speaker: Vince McKay
quotes.article_title: Canada and Northwest Territories partner to improve health infrastructure and access to health care for communities

quotes.quote_text: Education is one of the most powerful forces for transforming our country and shaping our shared future. Teachers are at the heart of that work, helping the next generation to learn, to lead and to build a stronger Canada. I congratulate the 2026 award recipients and thank all educators for their dedication, their service and their contributions to Canada.
quotes.speaker: Mark Carney
quotes.dept_en: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
quotes.article_title: Canada honours its top educators with Prime Minister’s Awards

quotes.quote_text: Canada’s teachers and educators help shape the future of our country every day. Not only are they teaching classroom subjects but they are also providing our young people with the skills to chase their dreams, think creatively, ask bold questions and grow into the leaders of tomorrow. Congratulations to the 2026 Prime Minister’s Awards recipients and thank you for all that you do to build Canada’s future.
quotes.speaker: Mélanie Joly
quotes.dept_en: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
quotes.article_title: Canada honours its top educators with Prime Minister’s Awards

quotes.quote_text: Educators are building the foundation for Canada’s future workforce. In child care centres and classrooms across the country, they are helping children and young people build the skills and confidence they need to succeed. This also means parents can go to work or return to school knowing their children are in good hands. Congratulations to this year’s recipients and thank you for your commitment to the children and families in your community.
quotes.speaker: Patty Hajdu
quotes.dept_en: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
quotes.article_title: Canada honours its top educators with Prime Minister’s Awards

quotes.quote_text: Canada and Ireland share deep cultural and economic ties, rooted in a long history that continues to shape both our countries. Through Canada–Ireland 180, we are strengthening this important relationship by creating new opportunities for artists and cultural organizations to collaborate, celebrate our shared heritage, and build connections that will last well beyond 2027.
quotes.speaker: Marc Miller
quotes.article_title: Canada expands opportunities for Canadian presenters through Canada–Ireland 180

quotes.quote_text: The Canada–Ireland 180 celebrations are a wonderful opportunity to celebrate the deep cultural ties that have connected our two countries for generations. The performing arts are at the heart of those connections, bringing people together through stories, music, dance, theatre and shared experiences. For the performing arts community, this initiative opens the door to new relationships, artistic exchanges and collaborations between Canadian and Irish artists, presenters and organizations.
quotes.speaker: Sue Urquhart
quotes.article_title: Canada expands opportunities for Canadian presenters through Canada–Ireland 180

quotes.quote_text: For CINARS, this project represents a strategic opportunity to strengthen the presence of Canadian presenters at the Biennale, increase the visibility and discoverability of international artists, and foster new collaborations and touring opportunities. Our collaboration with CAPACOA allows us to combine our expertise and networks to better connect artists with presenters, support market development, and strengthen the circulation of the performing arts across Canada and internationally.
quotes.speaker: Gilles Doré
quotes.article_title: Canada expands opportunities for Canadian presenters through Canada–Ireland 180

quotes.quote_text: Thanks to this funding in support of the Canada–Ireland 180 initiative, 50 Canadian presenters of folk music will gain access to new opportunities for international trade and collaboration at the Folk Canada Conference with an invited delegation from Culture Ireland. Folk Canada is grateful for this incredible investment from the Canadian government, and we look forward to sharing the many opportunities that will grow from this initiative in the coming year.
quotes.speaker: Rosalyn Dennett
quotes.article_title: Canada expands opportunities for Canadian presenters through Canada–Ireland 180

quotes.quote_text: Canada is making a generational investment in our defence and security, and we need institutions built to match the scale and urgency of that ambition. Establishing the Defence Investment Agency as a Crown corporation would give it the flexibility and specialized expertise to move faster, make strategic investments and deliver the capabilities our Armed Forces need. Just as importantly, it would allow us to use our defence investments to strengthen our sovereignty while building a robust Canadian defence industry, attracting investment and creating lasting economic opportunities and good jobs here at home.
quotes.speaker: Stephen Fuhr
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada introduces legislation to accelerate defence procurement, strengthen Canadian industry, and reinforce Canadian sovereignty

quotes.quote_text: We look forward to continued collaboration with the Defence Investment Agency to further strengthen defence procurement. As a Crown corporation within the National Defence portfolio, the DIA will have the direct authorities and added flexibility to streamline procurement so that the Canadian Armed Forces and Canadian Coast Guard have more secure, reliable and quicker access to the capabilities they need to protect our sovereignty and keep Canadians safe.
quotes.speaker: David J. McGuinty
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada introduces legislation to accelerate defence procurement, strengthen Canadian industry, and reinforce Canadian sovereignty

quotes.quote_text: In a more dangerous and divided world, Canada is taking action and establishing a clear and compelling path forward. With the introduction of this legislation, we are making clear that large-scale, agile defence production and procurement is here to stay. Procurement and investment must live together, by connecting the capabilities our armed forces need with the investments that will deliver them and the industrial capacity that will sustain them. As a Crown corporation, the Defence Investment Agency will integrate these priorities, delivering critical capabilities to our armed forces more efficiently while strengthening Canadian industry, driving innovation and creating economic opportunity for years to come.
quotes.speaker: Joël Lightbound
quotes.speaker_title: Minister, Public Works and Procurement and Quebec Lieutenant
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada introduces legislation to accelerate defence procurement, strengthen Canadian industry, and reinforce Canadian sovereignty

quotes.quote_text: Establishing the Defence Investment Agency as a Crown corporation is an important step in building the organization Canada needs to meet today’s defence and security challenges. It will give the DIA the tools, flexibility, and expertise to move faster and make strategic investments that deliver capabilities for the Canadian Armed Forces and the Canadian Coast Guard. Our responsibility will be to turn Canada’s defence investments into results, strengthening our industrial base, building sovereign capacity, deepening partnerships with industry, and creating economic opportunities at home. I am proud of what the DIA team has accomplished since our launch, and I look forward to leading this transition and the organization’s next chapter.
quotes.speaker: Doug Guzman
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada introduces legislation to accelerate defence procurement, strengthen Canadian industry, and reinforce Canadian sovereignty

quotes.speaker: Our government is proud to announce this new agreement with Cote d'Ivoire
quotes.speaker_title: which will help grow our two economies while creating new opportunities for our people and our businesses. This agreement reflects our shared commitment to growth, partnership, and prosperity., ", The Honourable Steven MacKinnon, Minister
quotes.article_title: Minister of Transport announces expanded air transport agreement with Côte d'Ivoire

quotes.speaker: Canada is diversifying its trade and deepening its economic relationships around the world
quotes.article_title: Minister of Transport announces expanded air transport agreement with Côte d'Ivoire

quotes.quote_text: For 25 years, ENERGY STAR Canada has helped Canadians save energy and save money. Today’s award recipients are demonstrating leadership, innovation, and a commitment to building a more affordable, energy-efficient future. Congratulations to all winners and partners who continue to help Canadians make smart energy choices.
quotes.speaker: Julie Dabrusin
quotes.article_title: ENERGY STAR® Canada recognizes leaders in energy efficiency

quotes.quote_text: Canadians deserve a sport system they can trust. That is why we are continuing to strengthen safety, integrity, accountability and transparency across the sport system. Environments that are safe, clean and fair help ensure that every participant, from playground to podium, can thrive. Strong governance and clear accountability are essential to delivering results for Canadians and building a sport system that reflects our shared values and earns the confidence of athletes, families and communities across the country.
quotes.speaker: Adam van Koeverden
quotes.article_title: Secretary of State van Koeverden announces new investments to strengthen the Canadian sport system

quotes.quote_text: The federal government's generational investment will redesign the Canadian sport system, and it is crucial that integrity be at the heart of this new era. Sport Integrity Canada’s mandate is to protect and promote the integrity of sport, and so we gratefully accept this supplemental funding that will help ensure safe, clean and fair sport. As we prepare to launch the 2027 Canadian Anti-Doping Program, this investment, in large part, will support ongoing modernization of the World Anti-Doping Agency-accredited laboratory and demonstrates Canada’s commitment to clean sport and athlete safety.
quotes.speaker: Jeremy Luke
quotes.article_title: Secretary of State van Koeverden announces new investments to strengthen the Canadian sport system

quotes.quote_text: The Canadian sport system has evolved significantly since the SDRCC was established more than 20 years ago, and this investment will strengthen our ability to continue evolving with it. Through consultation and collaboration with stakeholders across the sport system, we have an opportunity to examine how sport dispute resolution and prevention services can adapt to the changing needs of the Canadian sport system while remaining grounded in the principles of independence, cost-effectiveness and timeliness that define the SDRCC’s mission. This work will help shape the future of Canadian sport.
quotes.speaker: Francis Ménard
quotes.article_title: Secretary of State van Koeverden announces new investments to strengthen the Canadian sport system

quotes.quote_text: Investing in health care is investing in productivity. Today’s announcement reaffirms Canada’s partnership role, and it’s great news for Ontarians, and our public health care system.
quotes.speaker: Marjorie Michel
quotes.article_title: More health professionals, better care for Canadians

quotes.quote_text: Our government continues to take bold and decisive action to grow the province’s highly skilled health-care workforce to ensure people and their families have access to high-quality care, closer to home, for generations to come. We welcome this investment from the federal government which will build on the over $25 million we are investing into the Practice Ready Ontario program to support 150 participants annually starting in 2026/27 and is another important step as we continue our work to connect everyone in Ontario to primary care by 2029.
quotes.speaker: Sylvia Jones
quotes.article_title: More health professionals, better care for Canadians

quotes.quote_text: This funding is expected to create up to 200 new family physicians. For people across Ontario who don’t have a family physician, this is a big step in improving equitable access to primary care.
quotes.speaker: Viviane Lapointe
quotes.article_title: More health professionals, better care for Canadians

quotes.quote_text: Internationally educated occupational therapists (IEOTs) bring tremendous knowledge, experience and perspectives to Canada’s health system at a time when communities are seeing a growing need for occupational therapy services. We are grateful to Health Canada for the investment that is making the Canadian Hub for IEOTs possible. By bringing trusted information, practical tools and supports together in one place, we hope to make the pathway to practice clearer for IEOTs and strengthen the profession and the communities it serves.
quotes.speaker: Irving Gold
quotes.article_title: More health professionals, better care for Canadians

quotes.quote_text: Internationally educated physiotherapists have vital skills and experience that help meet the health needs of Canadians every day. This investment is helping CAPR make the pathway to physiotherapy practice in Canada easier to understand and navigate, ensuring these highly-qualified health professionals can access practical tools, resources, and support to help them prepare for practice in the Canadian healthcare system.
quotes.speaker: Dave Clements
quotes.article_title: More health professionals, better care for Canadians

quotes.quote_text: Internationally educated nurses bring valuable skills and experience to Canada's health care system, but the path to practice can often be difficult to navigate. With this support from Health Canada, the National Nursing Assessment Service is developing practical resources that help applicants understand each step of the process and move forward with greater clarity and confidence.
quotes.speaker: Penni Caron
quotes.article_title: More health professionals, better care for Canadians

quotes.quote_text: Internationally trained physicians (ITPs) are, and will continue to be, an important part of the care solution for Canadians. This funding supports our work to enhance our preparatory products, build a reliable source of information and support for ITPs on our website, and convene the International Medical Graduate Alliance, bringing together organizations and individuals, including ITPs themselves, to align efforts and avoid duplication.
quotes.speaker: Dr. Viren Naik
quotes.article_title: More health professionals, better care for Canadians

quotes.quote_text: As people in Canada continue to face challenges in accessing family doctors, internationally trained physicians (ITPs) represent an important, skilled, and valued part of the family medicine workforce. The CFPC's Re-IMGine Project is focused on evolving the pathways and supports available to internationally trained physicians (ITPs) as they pursue Certification in the College of Family Physicians of Canada (CCFP). As the professional home of every family physician in Canada, the CFPC grants the CCFP designation – a mark of excellence that demonstrates a family doctor has the training, skills, and experience required to provide continuous, comprehensive care. By evolving certification pathways and supports while upholding these standards, the Re-IMGine Project contributes to a strong family medicine workforce and upholds the trust people in Canada have in their family physicians, while championing family medicine excellence.
quotes.speaker: Dr. Makini McGuire-Brown
quotes.speaker_title: MBBS MBA PMP, PhD, Director, Re-IMGine Project
quotes.article_title: More health professionals, better care for Canadians

quotes.quote_text: Federal procurement doesn’t need more studies or promises, it needs results. This year’s report makes clear that progress is possible when there is focus and leadership, but foundational gaps remain, especially in Indigenous procurement and defence procurement. My Office will continue to push for credible governance, disciplined implementation, and the safeguards necessary to deliver the outcomes Canadians expect.
quotes.speaker: Alexander Jeglic
quotes.article_title: Procurement Ombud Releases 2025-26 Annual Report, Highlighting the Need for Accountability and Results in Federal Procurement

quotes.quote_text: We believe healthy, thriving communities begin with supporting families and ensuring children grow up connected to their First Nations culture. With today’s agreement, we are changing systems and creating a foundation for a better quality of life for all our people. I want to thank our seven Chiefs for their vision in guiding us through the work to put this agreement together, and the Minister for supporting our communities in taking charge of how their children are cared for.
quotes.speaker: Tribal
quotes.article_title: Minister Gull-Masty joins the Saskatoon Tribal Council to sign regional agreement to reform Child and Family Services

quotes.quote_text: First Nations know what their children and families need to thrive. This agreement puts that knowledge and leadership at the centre of child and family services. It supports First Nations with the flexibility and resources to invest in prevention, facilitate early intervention, and keep children connected to their families, communities, and cultures. I want to recognize Tribal Chief Mark Arcand and Saskatoon Tribal Council First Nations for the leadership, determination and years of work that brought us to this important milestone.
quotes.speaker: Mandy Gull-Masty
quotes.article_title: Minister Gull-Masty joins the Saskatoon Tribal Council to sign regional agreement to reform Child and Family Services

quotes.quote_text: We are proud to support the renovation of cultural spaces across the country. These vibrant gathering places encourage dialogue and access to culture while contributing to the vitality of local economies. By supporting projects like this one at the Hudson Village Theatre, we are affirming the theatre’s role as a pillar of the community.
quotes.speaker: Marc Miller
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada supports Hudson Village Theatre

quotes.quote_text: On behalf of my friend and colleague, the Honourable Marc Miller, Minister of Canadian Identity and Culture and Minister responsible for Official Languages, I am very pleased to announce additional federal funding for the Hudson Village Theatre. This is one of the largest federal investments in cultural infrastructure in our community’s history. After years of working to make this expansion a reality, this funding allows us to take another step closer to bringing the project to fruition and the day when the theatre will be fully realized.
quotes.speaker: Peter Schiefke
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada supports Hudson Village Theatre

quotes.quote_text: I am deeply grateful to Canadian Heritage for this $630,000 grant towards the renovations and two-storey addition to Hudson Village Theatre. This is a tremendous help in bringing a project that means so much to me and our community closer to completion.
quotes.speaker: Kalina Skulska
quotes.speaker_title: Artistic Director and Executive Director and President of the Board of Directors, Hudson Village Theatre
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada supports Hudson Village Theatre

quotes.quote_text: By supporting students who are passionate about agriculture and encouraging them to find solutions to real-world challenges, we’re investing in the next generation of agricultural leaders. We’re committed to giving young Canadians the opportunities they need to help shape a more innovative, sustainable and resilient sector for generations to come.
quotes.speaker: Heath MacDonald
quotes.speaker_title: federal Minister of Agriculture and Agri-Food
quotes.article_title: 2027 Saskatchewan Agriculture Student Scholarship now accepting applications

quotes.quote_text: Supporting tomorrow’s agriculture leaders is essential to the long-term success of our province. The Agriculture Student Scholarship recognizes outstanding students and celebrates their contributions to the future of the industry.
quotes.speaker: David Marit
quotes.article_title: 2027 Saskatchewan Agriculture Student Scholarship now accepting applications

quotes.quote_text: I think it's a great opportunity for students to get their ideas out there and be heard. If young people get involved early, it benefits the industry as a whole.
quotes.speaker: Carson Green
quotes.speaker_title: 2026 Agriculture Student Scholarship grand prize winner
quotes.article_title: 2027 Saskatchewan Agriculture Student Scholarship now accepting applications

quotes.quote_text: Since launching the Red Tape Review last year, we have made progress in removing unnecessary barriers, updating outdated rules and making government work better for Canadians. Today’s legislation builds on that work and supports a more modern, efficient and competitive regulatory system.
quotes.speaker: Shafqat Ali
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada Introduces Legislation to Reduce Red Tape and Support Economic Growth and Competitiveness

quotes.quote_text: I would like to congratulate Mr. Paquette and Mr. Parry on their appointments. These talented leaders bring valuable experience and a commitment to serving Canadians and building a stronger, more connected transportation system. I look forward to the positive contributions they will make in their new roles.
quotes.speaker: Steven MacKinnon
quotes.article_title: Transport Minister Steven MacKinnon announces new leadership appointments at VIA Rail and CATSA

quotes.quote_text: Alberta’s military bases and key infrastructure are essential to Canada's defence, serving as training and logistics hubs that support and prepare the Canadian Armed Forces for operations at home and around the world, while also generating thousands of well-paying jobs and supporting the region’s economic growth. As we continue making investments to rebuild, rearm and reinvest in our military, Alberta’s role will continue to grow.
quotes.speaker: The Honourable
quotes.article_title: Minister McGuinty visits CFB Edmonton to highlight Canada’s defence investments in Alberta

quotes.quote_text: Alberta’s ingenuity and expertise drives a stronger and more secure Canada. As we rebuild, rearm and reinvest in the Canadian Armed Forces, investments by PrairiesCan in innovative small- and medium-sized businesses here in Alberta are helping to bring new defence technologies to market, expand production, and create good jobs. Together, we are turning Alberta’s strengths into the capabilities Canada needs to defend our sovereignty and support our allies.
quotes.speaker: The Honourable
quotes.article_title: Minister McGuinty visits CFB Edmonton to highlight Canada’s defence investments in Alberta

quotes.quote_text: This arrest and resulting criminal charges reflect the CBSA's role in upholding the law with integrity and consistency. Those who attempt to smuggle illegal firearm parts into our country will be identified, investigated and prosecuted.
quotes.speaker: Trishann Pascal
quotes.article_title: CBSA makes arrest and lays charges in firearm investigation

quotes.quote_text: Our trade must reflect our values. Canada is committed to ensuring that our supply chains reflect the values we stand for: fairness, accountability and respect for human dignity. The perspectives shared through these consultations will help inform meaningful action to prevent goods produced with forced labour from entering Canada and support a more responsible and equal global trading system.
quotes.speaker: Anita Anand
topic_en: Maintain, grow and improve your business
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada releases What We Heard reports on fighting forced labour

quotes.quote_text: No one should profit from the exploitation of workers. As Canada diversifies trade and strengthens supply chains, respect for human rights must remain at the centre of those efforts. The feedback received during these consultations will help us strengthen Canada’s approach to addressing forced labour, so we can better protect workers’ rights and help create fairness for businesses that operate responsibly.
quotes.speaker: Patty Hajdu
topic_en: Maintain, grow and improve your business
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada releases What We Heard reports on fighting forced labour

quotes.quote_text: Affordable housing is also about affordable energy bills. By supporting energy-efficient retrofits in apartment buildings and multi-unit housing, we're helping lower costs for Canadians, improve housing quality, and build more sustainable communities.
quotes.speaker: Gregor Robertson
quotes.article_title: Prime Minister Carney announces landmark investment to retrofit one million homes, cutting energy costs and emissions

quotes.quote_text: The investment through the Canada Greener Affordable Homes Program demonstrates that manageable rents and sustainability go hand in hand. At the Housing Trust of Nova Scotia, we are committed to providing high-quality homes that are energy-efficient, environmentally responsible, and offer manageable rents to working households. This funding has helped us reduce operating costs, improve resident comfort and well-being, and ensure that rents remain stable and manageable over the long term. In this massive undertaking, we ensured that every resident remained in place – no displacements. We are grateful to the Government of Canada and Minister Gregor Robertson for supporting solutions that strengthen communities while advancing Canada's housing and climate goals.
quotes.speaker: Brian Tabor
quotes.speaker_title: Chair of the Housing Trust of Nova Scotia
quotes.article_title: Prime Minister Carney announces landmark investment to retrofit one million homes, cutting energy costs and emissions

quotes.speaker: As a long-standing member of the Housing Trust of Nova Scotia and with a passion for environmental impact
quotes.speaker_title: we don’t have to risk manageable rents, to achieve important environmental impacts. We can advance work that achieves two social impacts, through collaboration and partnership.”, Charity Carr, Advisory Member, Housing Trust of Nova Scotia
quotes.article_title: Prime Minister Carney announces landmark investment to retrofit one million homes, cutting energy costs and emissions

quotes.quote_text: Investing in energy efficiency is one of the most practical ways to make life more affordable for Canadians while building a cleaner, more competitive economy. By helping more households access efficient technologies like heat pumps and supporting upgrades across homes and buildings, these investments will lower energy costs, improve comfort and deliver lasting benefits for communities across the country.
quotes.speaker: Martha Casey
quotes.article_title: Prime Minister Carney announces landmark investment to retrofit one million homes, cutting energy costs and emissions

quotes.quote_text: Libraries are important community hubs that bring people together while providing access to culture, technology, and information. When we invest in local infrastructure like libraries, we support vibrant and thriving neighbourhoods, and the Build Communities Strong Fund is providing strategic, targeted investments to empower and unlock potential in our region. The Waverley library has served Thunder Bay for 75 years, and today’s announcement is a big step toward another 75 years of success.
quotes.speaker: Patty Hajdu
quotes.dept_en: Federal Economic Development Agency for Northern Ontario - FedNor
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada investing $1 million in community infrastructure in Thunder Bay

quotes.quote_text: Thunder Bay Public Library is proud to provide our community with inspiring and vibrant gathering spaces where anyone can achieve a lifetime of learning, grow as a person, and fulfill endless possibilities. We thank FedNor for their partnership in continuing that mission by supporting the Waverley Library renovations. Our mission is to facilitate knowledge sharing and help build a connected and healthy community, and this ambitious transformation project will support us in doing exactly that—bringing Thunder Bay together today, tomorrow, and beyond.
quotes.speaker: Richard Togman
quotes.dept_en: Federal Economic Development Agency for Northern Ontario - FedNor
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada investing $1 million in community infrastructure in Thunder Bay

quotes.quote_text: Canada needs a strong and resilient life sciences sector that can develop, manufacture and deliver the critical health products Canadians depend on. The Government of Canada’s investment in Jubilant Radiopharma will strengthen radiopharmaceutical production in Quebec, support high-quality jobs and help ensure Canada has the domestic capacity and expertise needed to respond to growing health needs. By supporting the production of critical biopharmaceutical products at home, the government is strengthening the country’s economy and health security.
quotes.speaker: Mélanie Joly
quotes.dept_en: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada announces new investment to strengthen Canada’s domestic radiopharmaceutical production capacity

quotes.quote_text: The radiopharmaceutical and life sciences industries help build our economy and save lives. Today’s investment will enable Quebec and Canada to remain global leaders in the field of radioisotopes.
quotes.speaker: Marjorie Michel
quotes.dept_en: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada announces new investment to strengthen Canada’s domestic radiopharmaceutical production capacity

quotes.quote_text: This investment recognizes Jubilant Radiopharma’s innovation capabilities in Nuclear Medicine and the important role our sector plays in advancing both diagnostic and therapeutic treatments. This project will build our deep capability here in Quebec, create and secure high-value jobs, and ensure a reliable supply of essential radiopharmaceutical products in Canada and around the world.
quotes.speaker: Harsher Singh
quotes.dept_en: Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada announces new investment to strengthen Canada’s domestic radiopharmaceutical production capacity

quotes.quote_text: The Dehcho / Deho / Kuukpak / Nagwichoonjik / Grand Rivière / Fleuve Mackenzie / Mackenzie River is a lifeline for the Northwest Territories, sustaining diverse ecosystems and wildlife from Great Slave Lake to the Arctic Ocean. This nomination is an opportunity to recognize the River’s extraordinary natural heritage and reinforce our commitment to protecting the waters, habitats, and biodiversity that make this landscape so unique.
quotes.speaker: Julie Dabrusin
quotes.article_title: Governments of Canada and Northwest Territories accept the nomination of the Dehcho / Deho / Kuukpak / Nagwichoonjik / Grand Rivière / Fleuve Mackenzie / Mackenzie River in the Northwest Territories as a Canadian Heritage River

quotes.quote_text: The Dehcho / Deho / Kuukpak / Nagwichoonjik / Grand Rivière / Fleuve Mackenzie / Mackenzie River is much more than a waterway. It is a vital part of the history, culture, and identity of the Dene, Métis, and Inuvialuit Peoples who live along its banks. This nomination recognises the deep and enduring connections that exist between these communities and the lands and waters of the Northwest Territories, and the importance of carrying those connections forward into the future.
quotes.speaker: Rebecca Alty
quotes.article_title: Governments of Canada and Northwest Territories accept the nomination of the Dehcho / Deho / Kuukpak / Nagwichoonjik / Grand Rivière / Fleuve Mackenzie / Mackenzie River in the Northwest Territories as a Canadian Heritage River

quotes.quote_text: In the Northwest Territories, rivers are our lifeblood. The Dehcho / Deho / Kuukpak / Nagwichoonjik / Grand Rivière / Fleuve Mackenzie / Mackenzie River is one of our most vital. For generations, it has provided for us. The nomination to the Canadian Heritage Rivers System is a significant step toward ensuring its importance and continued protection, so that it can remain a source of life, connection and vitality for future generations.
quotes.speaker: Jay MacDonald
quotes.speaker_title: Northwest Territories Minister of the Environment and Climate Change
quotes.article_title: Governments of Canada and Northwest Territories accept the nomination of the Dehcho / Deho / Kuukpak / Nagwichoonjik / Grand Rivière / Fleuve Mackenzie / Mackenzie River in the Northwest Territories as a Canadian Heritage River

quotes.quote_text: Waterways in the Northwest Territories are a vessel of our cultures. For thousands of years, the Dehcho / Deho / Kuukpak / Nagwichoonjik / Grand Rivière / Fleuve Mackenzie / Mackenzie River has provided for the people who live here. The nomination to the Canadian Heritage Rivers System recognizes the River’s significance to the territory and the country and is an important milestone towards preserving the cultural legacy of the River for years to come.
quotes.speaker: Caitlin Cleveland
quotes.speaker_title: Northwest Territories Minister of Education, Culture and Employment
quotes.article_title: Governments of Canada and Northwest Territories accept the nomination of the Dehcho / Deho / Kuukpak / Nagwichoonjik / Grand Rivière / Fleuve Mackenzie / Mackenzie River in the Northwest Territories as a Canadian Heritage River

quotes.quote_text: For the Métis people of Fort Providence, our extended families and Métis descendants beyond our region, the Dehcho—the Big River, which we call ‘la Grande Rivière’ in our Michif dialect—is part of our history, culture and everyday lives. This nomination recognizes the connection our people have maintained with the river through generations of travel, harvesting and shared knowledge. As the stewardship plan takes shape, Métis voices and the knowledge of our Elders must help guide the care of the river for future generations.
quotes.speaker: President Albert J. Lafferty
quotes.article_title: Governments of Canada and Northwest Territories accept the nomination of the Dehcho / Deho / Kuukpak / Nagwichoonjik / Grand Rivière / Fleuve Mackenzie / Mackenzie River in the Northwest Territories as a Canadian Heritage River

quotes.quote_text: Kuukpak is central to many Inuvialuit and their identity, culture and way of life - 365 days a year. The Inuvialuit Final Agreement affirms our responsibility to protect the lands and waters that have sustained us for generations. This nomination must elevate beyond a designation - it must lead to stewardship that respects Inuvialuit rights, knowledge and decision-making, so that Kuukpaak (the Mackenzie River) remains healthy and continues to sustain our communities for generations to come.
quotes.speaker: Erwin Elias
quotes.article_title: Governments of Canada and Northwest Territories accept the nomination of the Dehcho / Deho / Kuukpak / Nagwichoonjik / Grand Rivière / Fleuve Mackenzie / Mackenzie River in the Northwest Territories as a Canadian Heritage River

quotes.quote_text: This Final Self-Government Agreement is Canada’s formal recognition of the identity, culture, and inherent right to Self-Government of the Tłegǫ́hłı̨ Got’įnę. It provides the formal basis for a new government-to-government relationship between us and the Government of Canada, and a government-to-government relation between us and the Government of the Northwest Territories. It is our generation’s legacy to our children and future generations. We will do our best to use it to preserve, protect, exercise, and advance the inherent and treaty rights of the Tłegǫ́hłı̨ Got’įnę for the benefit of all our people living in Canada, here today. But our youth are the future, and this agreement provides our youth with the foundations to do the same when they take on the task of preserving, protecting, exercising and advancing our rights. Use this Self-Government Agreement, learn from the mistakes we may make and take us into the future—secure as Sahtu Dene/Metis people within the larger Canadian mosaic.
quotes.speaker: Sherry Hodgson
quotes.dept_en: Crown-Indigenous Relations and Northern Affairs Canada
quotes.article_title: Canada marks Royal Assent of legislation for Self-Government Treaty with the Tłegǫ́hłı̨ Got’įnę

quotes.quote_text: Reconciliation requires action. We welcome Canada’s decision to move forward with legislation to give legal force to the Final Self-Government Agreement for the Tłegǫ́hłı̨ Got’įnę, establishing it as a Self-Government Treaty. Collaborative governance is a cornerstone of our mandate, and this step reflects a shared commitment to recognising Indigenous rights and building a stronger future in partnership across the Northwest Territories.
quotes.speaker: R.J. Simpson
quotes.dept_en: Crown-Indigenous Relations and Northern Affairs Canada
quotes.article_title: Canada marks Royal Assent of legislation for Self-Government Treaty with the Tłegǫ́hłı̨ Got’įnę

quotes.quote_text: At its core, this legislation recognises an enduring truth: that the Tłegǫ́hłı̨ Got’įnę have an inherent right to govern themselves, as they have since long before Canada existed. Today, we celebrate the renewal of Canada’s relationship with the Tłegǫ́hłı̨ Got’įnę and the new opportunities that self-government will bring. I extend my heartfelt congratulations to the leadership, Elders, negotiators, and community members whose dedication and hard work over more than two decades made this milestone achievement possible.
quotes.speaker: Rebecca Alty
quotes.dept_en: Crown-Indigenous Relations and Northern Affairs Canada
quotes.article_title: Canada marks Royal Assent of legislation for Self-Government Treaty with the Tłegǫ́hłı̨ Got’įnę

quotes.quote_text: Building a stronger Canada means making life more affordable while creating a cleaner and more resilient future. By helping homeowners improve the energy efficiency of their homes, we are lowering energy costs, reducing pollution, and putting more money back in Canadians’ pockets. Through investments that help families use less energy and take advantage of Canada’s clean electricity advantage, we are building stronger communities, a more competitive economy, and a healthier environment for generations to come.
quotes.speaker: Wade Grant
quotes.speaker_title: Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister, Climate Change and Nature
quotes.article_title: The Government of Canada is supporting new measures to lower energy costs and reduce emissions

quotes.quote_text: Home energy retrofits make life more affordable and improve our environment. This investment will lower energy bills, cut greenhouse gas emissions, and create good jobs across Canada. We are taking decisive action to deliver lasting savings for Canadians and build a cleaner, more sustainable future.
quotes.speaker: Bruce Fanjoy
quotes.article_title: The Government of Canada is supporting new measures to lower energy costs and reduce emissions

quotes.quote_text: Sarnia–Lambton–Bkejwanong is home to skilled workers and innovative businesses that are strengthening Canada’s industrial base and creating new opportunities for growth. By investing in companies like AlumaPower and Promart Industrial Products, the Government of Canada is helping businesses advance innovative technologies, improve productivity and expand their operations. These investments will strengthen the regional economy, reinforce Canada’s industrial strengths, and help build Canada strong.
quotes.speaker: Evan Solomon
quotes.dept_en: Federal Economic Development Agency for Southern Ontario
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada supports growth and competitiveness of two businesses in Sarnia

quotes.quote_text: Sarnia–Lambton–Bkejwanong has a proud history of manufacturing, innovation and industrial excellence, supported by skilled workers and businesses that are ready to seize new opportunities. Today’s investments in AlumaPower and Promart Industrial Products will help local companies strengthen their capabilities and grow right here in our community. This is good news for local businesses, workers and the future of our regional economy.
quotes.speaker: Marilyn Gladu
quotes.dept_en: Federal Economic Development Agency for Southern Ontario
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada supports growth and competitiveness of two businesses in Sarnia

quotes.quote_text: We are extremely grateful for this support, which will accelerate the commercialization of our technology. National defence requires power generation that is safe, clean, reliable, and difficult to detect in the field. This investment will help us bring our products to market faster, strengthen Canada's defence innovation ecosystem, and create high-quality jobs as we scale. On behalf of the entire AlumaPower team, we thank FedDev Ontario for this support.
quotes.speaker: Rob Alexander
quotes.dept_en: Federal Economic Development Agency for Southern Ontario
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada supports growth and competitiveness of two businesses in Sarnia

quotes.quote_text: This investment is about where we want ProMart to be five, 10 and 20 years from now. We want to build more here in Sarnia, invest in our people, bring world-class technology onto our shop floor and compete for some of the biggest nuclear, energy and infrastructure projects being built in Canada. FedDev Ontario’s support is helping us make that jump faster, and we are incredibly excited about what comes next.
quotes.speaker: Marc Parizeau
quotes.speaker_title: Vice President, Promart Industrial Products Ltd.
quotes.dept_en: Federal Economic Development Agency for Southern Ontario
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada supports growth and competitiveness of two businesses in Sarnia

quotes.quote_text: SMEs drive the Quebec economy. In today’s business climate, they need stability, predictability and support to grow and become more competitive. The new Productivity Mega Deduction will allow businesses like Ferreol Skis to purchase equipment and deduct a range of costs in the first year. This means we are not only cutting taxes on new investment, but we are also enabling companies of any size to modernize their facilities, create high-quality jobs and boost their production capacity. That is how we build a Canada that has the means to achieve its ambitions.
quotes.speaker: Joël Lightbound
quotes.speaker_title: Minister, Public Works and Procurement and Quebec Lieutenant
quotes.article_title: Minister Lightbound visits a company in Beaupré to highlight the new Productivity Mega Deduction to help businesses invest, grow and create jobs in Canada

quotes.quote_text: This is one of the most significant changes to Canada’s business tax system in half a century, and a game changer for investment in this country. With the Productivity Mega Deduction, we are reinforcing Canada’s position as the most competitive country in the G7 for new business investment and setting the conditions for an investment supercycle. This is about unlocking investment at a scale we have not seen in generations, so businesses can build, expand and grow in Canada— creating high-paying careers and building a stronger, more productive and more resilient economy.
quotes.speaker: François-Philippe Champagne
quotes.article_title: Minister Lightbound visits a company in Beaupré to highlight the new Productivity Mega Deduction to help businesses invest, grow and create jobs in Canada

quotes.quote_text: Canada is positioning itself as a top choice for setting up and growing a business. With the Productivity Mega Deduction, small companies like ours have an incentive to invest more. Whether the goal is to increase exports, create value in a sovereign defence supply chain or create new good jobs, this supportive business environment drives companies to focus on productivity, innovation and growth plans.
quotes.speaker: Jonathan Audet
quotes.article_title: Minister Lightbound visits a company in Beaupré to highlight the new Productivity Mega Deduction to help businesses invest, grow and create jobs in Canada

quotes.quote_text: Productivity is the key to our businesses’ competitiveness. Every day, Québec International provides the region’s SMEs with guidance on their innovation, growth and export plans. Ferreol Skis is an excellent example of this. By encouraging investment in equipment, technology and strategic assets, the Productivity Mega Deduction is giving them concrete leverage to develop faster, increase their presence in international markets and create more high-quality jobs.
quotes.speaker: Maude Mercier-Larouche
quotes.speaker_title: Senior Director, Public and Corporate Affairs
quotes.article_title: Minister Lightbound visits a company in Beaupré to highlight the new Productivity Mega Deduction to help businesses invest, grow and create jobs in Canada

quotes.quote_text: Tourism is a critical industry in Northern Ontario because our region has so much history and culture to offer. Investments in events like the Algoma Fall Festival support local economies by supporting tourism opportunities, and help us find common ground, new or preexisting, with our friends and neighbours. The Algoma Fall Festival has a rich tradition of over half a century of success, and we are helping to carry that success into the future.
quotes.speaker: Patty Hajdu
quotes.dept_en: Federal Economic Development Agency for Northern Ontario - FedNor
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada investing $35,000 in 2026 Algoma Fall Festival

quotes.quote_text: Algoma region is a place of boundless treasure—experiences of breathtaking wilderness, rich and enlightening history, and vibrant and inspiring cultures. The 52 years of the Algoma Fall Festival have been an important piece of that, and the Government of Canada is making sure it remains a valuable experience to both locals and tourists alike. Sault Ste. Marie, just like the rest of Algoma region, has a lot to offer, and I’m proud to say that the Algoma Fall Festival will continue to both contribute to and share that wealth of experience.
quotes.speaker: Terry Sheehan
quotes.dept_en: Federal Economic Development Agency for Northern Ontario - FedNor
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada investing $35,000 in 2026 Algoma Fall Festival

quotes.quote_text: Our northern community is home to incredibly talented artists with unique and important perspectives, stories and work. The Algoma Arts Festival Association is proud to enrich our community by bringing people together to experience excellence in the arts. With the support of FedNor, Canadian Heritage and the Government of Canada, we are building on the 54-year legacy of the Algoma Fall Festival while expanding in exciting new ways. This includes Maada’ookiidaa – Let’s Share Our Gifts, our programming guided by our Indigenous Advisory Group that celebrates Indigenous artists, voices and stories. Maada’ookiidaa creates space for truth-telling, listening and learning, and encourages all of us to better understand our collective responsibility to walk the path toward truth, reconciliation and healing. It is an important part of how our Festival continues to bring people together through the arts.
quotes.speaker: Donna Hilsinger
quotes.dept_en: Federal Economic Development Agency for Northern Ontario - FedNor
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada investing $35,000 in 2026 Algoma Fall Festival

quotes.quote_text: For 75 years, Orford Music has held an important place in the Eastern Townships as well as Quebec’s cultural landscape. By supporting its festival and concert season, we are investing in our artists, our economy and a culture that brings us together and showcases Quebec and Canada beyond our borders. I congratulate Orford Music on this auspicious anniversary and thank the organization for its commitment to supporting music and our culture.
quotes.speaker: Marc Miller
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada supports arts and culture in the Eastern Townships region

quotes.quote_text: Orford Music is more than just a place for musical training and performance. It’s an institution in tune with our region, which allows artists from here and beyond to develop their talent and share their passion. With this investment, we are helping preserve an exceptional facility while giving it the ability to continue to evolve. It’s a great way to recognize its heritage but above all invest in its future.
quotes.speaker: Louis Villeneuve
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada supports arts and culture in the Eastern Townships region

quotes.quote_text: This contribution from the Government of Canada represents vital support for the mission and development of Orford Music. It allows us to pursue, in the coming years, ambitious programming focused on artistic excellence, the emergence of new talent and better access to music for an ever-growing audience. During this anniversary year, this support signifies the importance of Orford Music in Quebec’s cultural landscape. It also encourages us to continue our work with confidence and enthusiasm.
quotes.speaker: Françoise Parent
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada supports arts and culture in the Eastern Townships region

quotes.quote_text: Having been born in Swift Current, I know the pride Saskatchewan people take in what they grow, make, and build—and the determination they bring to keeping their communities strong. As unjustified U.S. tariffs put pressure on businesses and workers, our government is standing with them. These investments through PrairiesCan will help Saskatchewan businesses produce more here at home, reach new markets, and create good jobs—building on the province’s strengths to secure a stronger economic future for Canada.
quotes.speaker: Eleanor Olszewski
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada helps Saskatchewan businesses adapt and grow amid unjustified U.S. tariffs

quotes.quote_text: In the face of global trade uncertainty, Saskatchewan businesses are doing what Prairie businesses do best: adapting and investing in new opportunities because our products can compete with anyone, anywhere. World-class organizations and workers across Saskatchewan are working hard to weather the impacts of unjustified tariffs, and we’ve got their backs. Today’s investment of over $11.2 million for eight Saskatchewan businesses will help them produce more here at home, create good jobs, and find new customers around the world.
quotes.speaker: Buckley Belanger
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada helps Saskatchewan businesses adapt and grow amid unjustified U.S. tariffs

quotes.quote_text: The continued support of the BSP program has been instrumental in Northern Nutrients’ growth. The contribution from BSP will help ensure the tripling of our sulphur fertilizer capacity to 150,000 metric tons per year is a successful project that will provide efficient crop nutrients to the local market and beyond for years to come.
quotes.speaker: Ross Guenther
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada helps Saskatchewan businesses adapt and grow amid unjustified U.S. tariffs

quotes.quote_text: Prairies Economic Development Canada's funding for the Prairie Connect project will allow the Western Canadian Short Line Railway Association to generate greater visibility for rail freight transportation opportunities across rural Saskatchewan. Our province is fortunate to have thousands of kilometres of rail infrastructure to help transport Saskatchewan products to destinations around the world. Prairie Connect will help link small, medium, and large shippers with railway operators and loading locations that can support their business expansion and diversification.
quotes.speaker: Rachel Mackenzie
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada helps Saskatchewan businesses adapt and grow amid unjustified U.S. tariffs

quotes.quote_text: In every community, we want Canadians to see the benefits of a stronger, more productive economy. That means more opportunities for workers, stronger local businesses, and a country where skilled newcomers and Canadians can build a future together. The Productivity Mega Deduction is one critical part of our plan to create those opportunities and make sure the benefits of growth are felt in Atlantic Canada and across the country.
quotes.speaker: Lena Metlege Diab
quotes.article_title: Minister Metlege Diab highlights new Productivity Mega Deduction to help businesses invest, grow, and create jobs in Canada

quotes.quote_text: This is one of the most significant changes to Canada’s business tax system in half a century, and a game changer for investment in this country. With the Productivity Mega Deduction, we are reinforcing Canada’s position as the most competitive country in the G7 for new business investments and setting the conditions for an investment supercycle. This is about unlocking investment at a scale we have not seen in generations, so businesses can build, expand and grow in Canada—creating high-paying careers and building a stronger, more productive and more resilient economy.
quotes.speaker: François-Philippe Champagne
quotes.article_title: Minister Metlege Diab highlights new Productivity Mega Deduction to help businesses invest, grow, and create jobs in Canada

quotes.quote_text: Here in Alberta, we have seen how Canadians have come together to help one another in times of crisis. From the experience of the Fort McMurray and Jasper wildfires, we know that we are stronger when we are united to face these challenges together. Funding from our government through the Humanitarian Workforce Program is helping the Canadian Red Cross train personnel who are ready to deliver meaningful support where and when it is needed most, turning Canadian values into meaningful action on the ground.
quotes.speaker: Eleanor Olszewski
quotes.article_title: Federal government invests in Canadian Red Cross to support Canadians during emergencies

quotes.quote_text: Emergencies can happen at any time, and having the right resources in place can make all the difference in providing essential support when people need it most. This investment will help the Canadian Red Cross strengthen and sustain a skilled and ready humanitarian workforce that can quickly mobilize to support communities affected by large-scale emergencies. We are grateful for the Government of Canada’s continued partnership as we work together to ensure Canadians receive compassionate, timely, and coordinated support before, during and after emergencies.
quotes.speaker: Melanie Soler
quotes.speaker_title: Vice President, Emergency Management, Canadian Red Cross
quotes.article_title: Federal government invests in Canadian Red Cross to support Canadians during emergencies
Minister Sidhu to lead Team Canada Trade Mission to India to unlock new bilateral trade opportunities

quotes.quote_text: Investing in health care is investing in our economy and our future. The results we are seeing in the Yukon and across Canada show that investments in our public health care system and working together work. Once finalized, this agreement will help the Yukon continue improving access to care and building healthier, stronger communities across the territory.
quotes.speaker: Marjorie Michel
quotes.article_title: Canada and Yukon reach agreement in principle to improve access to health care

quotes.quote_text: Yukoners deserve access to quality health care when and where they need it. This renewed agreement will support practical improvements that make a big difference in people’s lives – from better access to primary care in Whitehorse to stronger mental health and substance use services and more connected care across the territory. By continuing to work together, we are helping build a health system that responds to the needs of Yukoners and their communities.
quotes.speaker: Brendan Hanley
quotes.article_title: Canada and Yukon reach agreement in principle to improve access to health care

quotes.quote_text: This agreement gives us the ability to make targeted investments where they can have the greatest impact for Yukoners. We are especially pleased to use this new funding to provide increased resources for our rural health centres, which is a priority raised by Yukon First Nations, municipalities, and Yukoners.
quotes.speaker: Brad Cathers
quotes.article_title: Canada and Yukon reach agreement in principle to improve access to health care

quotes.quote_text: Canadians are a critical part of the conversation when it comes to protecting species at risk. People who live and work on the water see what is changing, and that knowledge helps shape listing decisions under the Species At Risk Act. Working together, we can protect more species and keep our waters healthy for future generations.
quotes.speaker: Joanne Thompson
quotes.article_title: Government of Canada proposes listing several aquatic species under the Species at Risk Act

quotes.quote_text: Newfoundland and Labrador is ready to build. We have the resources, expertise, people, and the know-how. This co-operation agreement with the province implements a “one project, one review” approach to environmental and impact assessments on major projects. We are simplifying the process to attract more investment to support our communities. Together, we’re building Newfoundland and Labrador strong to build Canada strong.
quotes.speaker: Joanne Thompson
quotes.article_title: Newfoundland and Labrador and Canada sign co-operation agreement to accelerate project assessments

quotes.quote_text: This agreement represents another milestone in efficient project reviews and shows our commitment to supporting responsible sustainable development that protect the environment, strengthen the economy, and uphold obligations to Indigenous Peoples .
quotes.speaker: Julie Dabrusin
quotes.article_title: Newfoundland and Labrador and Canada sign co-operation agreement to accelerate project assessments

quotes.quote_text: This agreement in principle reflects the determination of the government of Newfoundland and Labrador and the federal government to deliver for Canadians. By reducing duplication and coordinating impact assessments, we are creating greater certainty for investors and Indigenous rights holders and helping major projects move more efficiently.
quotes.speaker: Dominic LeBlanc
quotes.speaker_title: President, Internal Trade and One Canadian Economy
quotes.article_title: Newfoundland and Labrador and Canada sign co-operation agreement to accelerate project assessments

quotes.quote_text: Our government is focused on delivery, not delay, and this co-operation agreement with Newfoundland and Labrador is another step in getting big things built in Newfoundland and Labrador, from energy to mines to roads and new transmission lines. Improving efficiency and streamlining approvals with our partners in the province means that we can meet the moment by responsibly and efficiently building the infrastructure that will secure Canada’s economic future.
quotes.speaker: Tim Hodgson
quotes.article_title: Newfoundland and Labrador and Canada sign co-operation agreement to accelerate project assessments

quotes.quote_text: The cooperation agreement aims to streamline project assessments. By eliminating duplication in environmental assessments and regulatory processes, the Government of Newfoundland and Labrador and the Government of Canada will create efficiency, increase certainty for stakeholders and attract investment in our province. Together, we will continue to ensure environmental protections are upheld and development occurs in a sustainable manner for all of us.
quotes.speaker: Andrea Barbour
quotes.article_title: Newfoundland and Labrador and Canada sign co-operation agreement to accelerate project assessments

quotes.quote_text: HMCS Ottawa ’s deployment demonstrated the Canadian Armed Forces’ ability to operate seamlessly from the Indo-Pacific to the North American arctic regions, advancing Canada's strategic interests alongside allies and partners. Whether operating in the Indo-Pacific, or contributing to continental defence in northern waters, HMCS Ottawa’s deployment demonstrates Canadian Armed Forces’ operational agility and readiness in achieving our operational objectives at home and abroad. I am proud of the sailors and embarked personnel whose professionalism and dedication made this deployment such a success.
quotes.speaker: Lieutenant-General Steve Boivin
quotes.article_title: His Majesty’s Canadian Ship Ottawa returns to Esquimalt following Operations HORIZON and LATITUDE

quotes.quote_text: From strengthening partnerships and interoperability in the Indo-Pacific to supporting continental defence in northern waters, His Majesty’s Canadian Ship Ottawa demonstrated the professionalism, readiness and versatility of the Royal Canadian Navy. We proudly welcome the ship’s company home to Esquimalt.
quotes.speaker: Rear-Admiral David Patchell
quotes.speaker_title: Commander Maritime Forces Pacific / Joint Task Force Pacific
quotes.article_title: His Majesty’s Canadian Ship Ottawa returns to Esquimalt following Operations HORIZON and LATITUDE

quotes.quote_text: Operating alongside our allies and partners during RIMPAC and Operations HORIZON and LATITUDE demonstrated the interoperability, capability, and professionalism of His Majesty’s Canadian Ship Ottawa’s sailors. I am incredibly proud of what the crew accomplished throughout this deployment, specifically their commitment to regenerating sailors, and am grateful for the steadfast support of our families and friends back home.
quotes.speaker: Commander Justin Simmons
quotes.article_title: His Majesty’s Canadian Ship Ottawa returns to Esquimalt following Operations HORIZON and LATITUDE

images.alt_text: WeChat articles from the Youli-Youmian account that targeted LPC Leader Mark Carney. | Image caption 1: WeChat articles from the Youli-Youmian account that targeted LPC Leader Mark Carney. Social media engagement for these articles was high, even exceeding the engagement level on state-controlled media outlets like the People’s Daily, which averages about 30,000 interactions per post / Image caption 2: Bot-like WeChat news accounts that appear dedicated to amplifying content from the Youli-Youmian account. These accounts do not post original content, and often re-post Youli-Youmian content in a sequence, and only minutes apart. Some of the bot-like accounts continue to re-post Youli-Youmian content days after it was originally posted, likely to improve discoverability of the article, and boosting Youli-Youmian’s presence in user feeds.

images.alt_text: Building Canada Now | Text version One project, one decision, within one year under Canada’s Impact Assessment Act (IAA) Previous approach Multiple consultation processes Multiple decisions From project submissions to federal project decision in 5+ Years Step 1: Proponents prepare a comprehensive application, gather studies and information for permitting and impact assessment Step 2: Impact Assessment Act Decision Crown consultation Federal decision 1 Step 3 Permit 1: e.g. Fisheries Authorization Decision Crown consultation Federal decision 2 Step 4 Permit 2: e.g. Species at Risk Act Decision Crown consultation Federal decision 3 Step 5 Permit 3+: e.g. Additional Federal Authorizations Crown consultation Federal decision 4+ Step 6: Construction can begin New Approach One single coordinated federal decision One consultation process From project submissions to federal project decision in no more than one year Step 1: Proponents prepare a comprehensive application, gather studies and information for permitting and impact assessment Step 2 Coordinated Crown Consultation Process: One process per Indigenous group per project Step 3 One Federal Decision: IA and Permits Step 4 Single Conditions Document: e.g. Navigable Waters; Fisheries Authorizations; Species at Risk Step 5: Construction can begin
